tourism.zh: n. 观光业, 游览 / [经] 旅游业

inventive.ety: From Middle English inventif, inventyfe, borrowed from Old French inventif, borrowed from Medieval Latin inventivus. By surface analysis, invent + -ive.

inventor.zh: n. 发明家 / [法] 发明人, 发明家, 创造者
def: someone who is the first to think of or make something
One who invents, either as a hobby or as an occupation.
inventor.ety: Borrowed from Latin inventor. By surface analysis, invent + -or.

In an inverse order or manner; by inversion.

invertebrate.zh: a. 无脊椎的, 无骨气的 / n. 无脊椎动物, 无骨气的人

lacking a backbone or spinal column

investment.zh: n. 投资 / [医] 包埋料, 围模料, 包埋法, 围模法
def: the act of investing; laying out money or capital in an enterprise with the expectation of profit
money that is invested with an expectation of profit
the commitment of something other than money (time, energy, or effort) to a project with the expectation of some worthwhile result

investor.zh: n. 投资者 / [经] 投资者
def: someone who commits capital in order to gain financial returns
A person who invests money in order to make a profit.

invigorate.zh: vt. 使精力充沛, 鼓舞, 搞活, 使健壮
invigorate.ety: First attested in 1646; borrowed from New Latin invigōrātus, perfect passive participle of invigōrō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix). By surface analysis, in- + vigo

inviolable.zh: a. 不可亵渎的, 不可侵犯的, 神圣的 / [法] 不可侵犯的, 神圣的
def: incapable of being transgressed or dishonored
immune to attack; incapable of being tampered with
inviolable.ety: From Middle French inviolable, from Latin inviolābilis (“untouchable”), from violō (“violate”). Equivalent to in- + violable. Piecewise doublet of unviolable.

invisible.zh: a. 看不见的, 无形的 / [经] 无形的, 表面上看不见的, 未列在公开帐目的
def: impossible or nearly impossible to see; imperceptible by the eye
invisible.ety: From Middle English invisible, from Old French invisible, from Late Latin invīsibilis. Displaced native Old English unġesewenlīċ. Morphologically in- + visible. Piecewise doublet of unvisible.

involuntary.zh: a. 自然而然的, 无意识的, 不知不觉的, 偶然的, 不随意的 / [医] 不随意的
def: not subject to the control of the will- John F.Kennedy
controlled by the autonomic nervous system; without conscious control
involuntary.ety: From in- + voluntary, from Late Latin involontarius, from in + volontarius.

infusion.zh: n. 注入, 泡制, 注入物 / [化] 浸渍; 浸泡
def: a solution obtained by steeping or soaking a substance (usually in water)
the process of extracting certain active properties (as a drug from a plant) by steeping or soaking (usually in water)
(medicine) the passive introduction of a substance (a fluid or drug or electrolyte) into a vein or between tissues (as by gravitational force)
infusion.ety: From Middle English infusioun, from Old French infusion, from Latin infusio, infusionem (“a pouring into, a wetting, a dyeing, a flow”), from infundo.

ingenious.zh: a. 灵敏的, 精巧的, 聪明的
def: Of a person, displaying genius, ingenuity or brilliance; inventive.
Of a thing, characterized by genius; cleverly contrived or done.
ingenious.ety: Borrowed from Middle French ingénieux, from Old French engenious, from Latin ingeniōsus (“endowed with good natural capacity, gifted with genius”), from ingenium (“innate or natural quality, natural c

ingenuity.zh: n. 心灵手巧, 精巧, 精巧设计

ingenuous.zh: a. 坦白的, 正直的, 天真的
def: characterized by an inability to mask your feelings; not devious
ingenuous.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin ingenuus (“of noble character, frank”). Doublet of ingenu.

inglorious.zh: a. 不名誉的, 可耻的, 不出名的
def: (used of conduct or character) deserving or bringing disgrace or shame- Rachel Carson
inglorious.ety: From Latin inglōriōsus. By surface analysis, in- + glorious.

inhabitable.zh: a. 可居住的, 可栖居的
def: Not habitable; not suitable to be inhabited.
inhabitable.ety: From Middle English inhabitable, inhabytabill, from Middle French inhabitable and its etymon Latin inhabitābilis (“uninhabitable”). By surface analysis, in- + habitable.

inhabitant.zh: n. 居民, 居住者 / [医] 居民
def: a person who inhabits a particular place
Someone or thing who lives in a place.
A possible value for a type.
inhabitant.ety: From Middle English inhabitantes (n. plural) and inhabitaunt (adj.), from Old French inhabitant, from Latin inhabitāns, present participle of inhabitō (“to inhabit”), from in- (“in”) + habitō (“to dwe

inherent.zh: a. 固有的, 与生俱来的 / [医] 固有的, 生来的
def: existing as an essential constituent or characteristic
in the nature of something though not readily apparent
inherent.ety: From Latin inhaerentem, accusative singular of inhaerēns, present active participle of inhaereō (“to be closely connected with; to adhere to”).

inheritance.zh: n. 遗传, 遗产 / [医] 遗传
def: hereditary succession to a title or an office or property
that which is inherited; a title or property or estate that passes by law to the heir on the death of the owner
(genetics) attributes acquired via biological heredity from the parents
inheritance.ety: Inherited from Middle English enheritaunce, inheritaunce, borrowed from Anglo-Norman, Old French enheritaunce, from enheriter. By surface analysis, inherit + -ance.

inhibitor.zh: n. 禁止者, 抑制人, 抑制物, 抑制因素, 抑制剂, 阻化剂 / [计] 禁止器, 抑制剂
def: a substance that retards or stops an activity
One who, or that which, inhibits.
Any substance capable of stopping or slowing a specific chemical reaction.

inhumanity.zh: n. 不人道, 残暴 / [法] 无人性, 野蛮, 残酷
def: the quality of lacking compassion or consideration for others
inhumanity.ety: From Middle French inhumanité, from Latin inhumanitas, equivalent to inhuman + -ity.

inimitable.zh: a. 无法仿效的, 独特的, 无比的
def: Beyond imitation, surpassing all others; matchless.
inimitable.ety: Borrowed from Middle French inimitable, from Latin inimitabilis, corresponding to in- + imitable.

injection.zh: n. 注射, 注射剂 / [化] 注入; 注射
def: the forceful insertion of a substance under pressure
any solution that is injected (as into the skin)
the act of putting a liquid into the body by means of a syringe
injection.ety: Borrowed from Middle French injection, from Latin iniectio. The mathematical sense is from French injection, introduced by Nicolas Bourbaki in their treatise Éléments de mathématique. Equivalent to in

injunction.zh: n. 命令, 禁令, 劝告 / [经] 指令, 禁令
def: (law) a judicial remedy issued in order to prohibit a party from doing or continuing to do a certain activity
injunction.ety: From Middle English iniunccyon, iniunccion, from Old French injonctïon, from Latin iniūnctiō (“command, injunction”).

injustice.zh: n. 不公平, 非正义的行为 / [法] 不公正, 不公平, 权利侵害
def: the practice of being unjust or unfair
injustice.ety: From Middle English injustice, from Old French injustice, from Latin iniustitia. Equivalent to in- + justice. Displaced native Old English unrihtwīsnes.

innumerable.zh: a. 无数的, 数不清的
def: Not capable of being counted, enumerated, or numbered.
Of a very high number; extremely numerous.
innumerable.ety: From in- + numerable; from Middle English innumerable, from Latin innumerābilis, from in- + numerābilis.

inoffensive.zh: a. 无害的, 不触犯人的, 不讨厌的
def: substituting a mild term for a harsher or distasteful one

inordinate.zh: a. 过度的, 紊乱的, 过分的
def: Excessive; unreasonable or inappropriate in magnitude.
inordinate.ety: From Middle English inordinat, from Latin inōrdinātus (“not arranged, disordered, irregular”), from in- + ordinatus, past participle of ōrdināre (“to arrange, order”).

inorganic.zh: a. 无机的, 无生物的, 非自然形成的 / [医] 无机的
def: relating or belonging to the class of compounds not having a carbon basis
lacking the properties characteristic of living organisms

inquiry.zh: n. 质询, 探索, 调查, 询盘 / [计] 询问; 查询
def: a systematic investigation of a matter of public interest
inquiry.ety: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-It

inquisition.zh: n. 调查, 探究, 审理, 宗教裁判所 / [医] 调查, 审查
def: a former tribunal of the Roman Catholic Church (1232-1820) created to discover and suppress heresy
a severe interrogation (often violating the rights or privacy of individuals)
inquisition.ety: From Old French inquisicion, from Latin inquisitio, from inquirere. The sense implying persecution is influenced by the name of the Spanish Inquisition, which is a cardinal exemplar of government inqu

inquisitive.zh: a. 好问的, 想知道的, 好追根究底的
inquisitive.ety: Late 14th century, from Old French inquisitif, from Late Latin inquisitivus, from Latin inquisitus, past participle of inquirere. See also inquire.

insanity.zh: n. 疯狂, 愚顽, 精神错乱 / [医] 精神病
def: relatively permanent disorder of the mind
The state of being insane; madness.
insanity.ety: A three-part word (root 'sane', prefix 'in-' meaning 'not', suffix '-ity', meaning 'the state of'). Derived from Latin precursory equivalents. Two possible candidates for construction order: * insane

insatiable.zh: a. 不知足的, 贪求无厌的 / [医] 不能满足的, 不饱的
def: Not satiable; incapable of being satisfied or appeased; very greedy.
One who or that which cannot be satiated.
insatiable.ety: Inherited from Middle English insaciable, from Middle French insatiable, from Old French insaciable, from Late Latin insatiabilis. By surface analysis, in- + satiable.

inscription.zh: n. 题字, 碑铭 / [医] 划, 药量记载

insider.zh: n. 内部的人, 权威人士, 知道内情的人 / [经] 熟悉内情者

insincerity.zh: n. 不诚实, 无诚意, 伪善 / [经] 不诚实

insistence.zh: n. 坚持, 坚决主张

insomnia.ety: Borrowed from Latin īnsomnia, from Latin in- (“without”) + somnus (“sleep”, noun) + -ia, equivalent to in- + somn- + -ia.

inspector.zh: n. 检查员, 巡视员 / [化] 检查员

inspiration.zh: n. 灵感, 鼓舞人心的人或物, 妙计, 吸气 / [医] 吸[气]

instructive.zh: a. 有益的, 增进知识的

insubstantial.zh: a. 脆弱的, 无实体的, 非实质的

insufferable.zh: a. 不可忍受的, 忍耐不住的

Not sufficient; lacking competent power or ability; unqualified, unequal, unfit.

insurrection.zh: n. 起义, 暴动, 反抗 / [法] 起义, 叛乱, 暴动

The action of part or all of a national population violently rising up against the government or other authority; (countable) an instance of this; a revolt, an uprising; specifically, one t…

incorporate.zh: a. 合并的, 组成公司的, 一体化的 / vt. 吸收, 合并, 使组成公司, 体现 / vi. 合并, 混合, 组成公司
def: make into a whole or make part of a whole

incorrigible.zh: a. 无药可救的, 积习难改的 / n. 不可救药的人
def: Defective and impossible to materially correct or set aright.
Unmanageable; impervious to correction by punishment or pain.
incorrigible.ety: From Middle English incorrigible, from Middle French incorrigible (1334), or directly from Latin incorrigibilis (“not to be corrected”), from in- (“not”) + corrigere (“to correct”) + -ibilis (“-able”)

increasingly.zh: adv. 逐渐地, 渐增地

incredulous.zh: a. 怀疑的, 不轻信的

Skeptical, disbelieving, or unable to believe.

incriminate.zh: vt. 连累, 暗示...有罪, 控告 / [法] 控告, 使入罪, 连累

incurable.zh: a. 不能医治的, 不能矫正的, 无救的 / n. 不治的病人, 无救的人

incursion.zh: n. 侵入, 侵略, 奇袭

indifference.zh: n. 不重视, 无兴趣, 漠不关心 / [法] 中立, 不偏袒, 不重视

indifferent.zh: a. 漠不关心的, 无重要性的, 中立的 / [医] 中性的, 无作用的, 无亲和力的, 淡漠的

indifferent.ety: From Old French indifferent, from Latin indifferens. By surface analysis, in- + different.

indignant.zh: a. 愤怒的, 愤慨的

indignation.zh: n. 愤怒, 愤慨, 义愤

indignity.ety: Borrowed from Latin indignitās, indignitātem. Equivalent to indign + -ity.

indispensable.zh: n. 不可缺少之物 / a. 不可缺少的, 责无旁贷的, 绝对必要的
def: not to be dispensed with; essential
indispensable.ety: Borrowed from Middle French indispensable, from Medieval Latin indispensābilis, corresponding to in- + dispensable.

def: not open to question; obviously true

indistinguishable.zh: a. 不能辨别的, 不能区别的
def: exactly alike; incapable of being perceived as different
not capable of being distinguished or differentiated

individual.zh: n. 人, 个人, 个体 / a. 个别的, 个人的, 独特的
def: being or characteristic of a single thing or person

indoctrinate.zh: vt. 教训, 教导, 灌输

infamous.zh: a. 无耻的, 不名誉的, 声名狼藉的
def: Having a bad reputation; disreputable; notorious; unpleasant or evil; widely known, especially for something scornful.
infamous.ety: From Middle English enfamouse, in-fames, infamous, from Medieval Latin īnfāmōsus, from Latin īnfāmis; by surface analysis, in- + famous. Displaced native Old English unhlīsful.

indubitable.zh: a. 无疑的, 确实的, 明显的 / [法] 不容置疑的, 明确的

indubitable.ety: Either from French indubitable or Latin indubitābilis. By surface analysis, in- + dubitable.

inducement.zh: n. 诱因, 动机, 吸引力, 刺激物 / [法] 诱惑, 引诱, 诱因

induction.zh: n. 归纳法, 感应, 就职, 入门 / [计] 归纳法

an electrical phenomenon whereby an electromotive force (EMF) is generated in a closed circuit by a change in the flow of current

def: in such a manner as could not be otherwise

ineligible.zh: a. 无被选任资格的, 不适任的, 无益的 / n. 无被选任资格的人, 不合录用资格的人

inequity.zh: n. 不公平, 不公正

inequity.ety: From in- + equity. Piecewise doublet of iniquity.

inescapable.zh: a. 逃不掉的, 不可避免的

Impossible (unable) to avoid or escape; not escapable.

inestimable.zh: a. 无价的, 无法估计的
def: Not able to be estimated; not able to be calculated, computed or comprehended, as because of great scale, degree or magnitude.
inestimable.ety: From Middle French inestimable, from Latin inaestimābilis, from in (“un-”, “not”) + aestimābilis (“estimable”). Equivalent to in- + estimable.

inexhaustible.zh: a. 用不完的, 无穷尽的, 不知疲倦的
def: that cannot be entirely consumed or used up
incapable of being entirely consumed or used up

inexpensive.zh: a. 便宜的, 不贵重的
def: relatively low in price or charging low prices
Involving little expense; reasonable in price; cheap.

inexplicable.zh: a. 不能说明的, 不能解释的, 费解的
def: incapable of being explained or accounted for
Impossible to explain; not easily accounted for.
Something that is impossible to explain.
inexplicable.ety: From Middle English inexplicable, from Middle French inexplicable, from Latin inexplicābilis, from in- (“not”) + explicābilis (“explicable”). By surface analysis, in- + explicable.

infection.zh: n. 传染, 影响, 传染病 / [医] 传染, 感染
def: the pathological state resulting from the invasion of the body by pathogenic microorganisms
(phonetics) the alteration of a speech sound under the influence of a neighboring sound
(medicine) the invasion of the body by pathogenic microorganisms and their multiplication which can lead to tissue damage and disease
infection.ety: From Old French infection, from Late Latin īnfectiō. Equivalent to infect + -ion.

infectious.zh: a. 有传染性的, 易传染的 / [医] 传染性的
def: caused by infection or capable of causing infection
infectious.ety: Borrowed from New Latin īnfectiōsus. By surface analysis, infect + -ious.

Something that is infelicitous or inappropriate
infelicity.ety: From in- + felicity, from Latin infelicitas.

infidelity.zh: n. 不信神, 无信仰, 背信
def: Unfaithfulness in a marriage or an intimate (sexual or romantic) relationship: practice or instance of having a sexual or romantic affair with someone other than one's spouse, without the c…
Unfaithfulness in some other moral obligation.
infidelity.ety: From Middle English infidelite, from Middle French infidelité (modern French infidélité) and its etymon Latin īnfidēlitās. Equivalent to infidel + -ity.

infiltrate.zh: vt. 使浸润, 使潜入, 使渗入 / vi. 渗入 / n. 渗透物
def: cause (a liquid) to enter by penetrating the interstices
enter a group or organization in order to spy on the members
pass into or through by filtering or permeating
infiltrate.ety: From Middle English infiltrate (adjective), from Medieval Latin infiltrātus, from infiltrō.

infinite.zh: n. 无限, 神 / a. 无穷的, 无限的, 极大的
def: having no limits or boundaries in time or space or extent or magnitude
the unlimited expanse in which everything is located

infinite.ety: From Middle English infinite, from Old French infinit and its etymon Latin īnfīnītus, from in- (“not”) + fīnis (“end”) + the perfect passive participle ending -ītus. By surface analysis, in- + finite.

infinity.zh: n. 无限大, 无限 / [计] 无穷
def: Endlessness, unlimitedness, absence of a beginning, end or limits to size.
A number that has an infinite numerical value that cannot be counted.

A place where sick or injured people are cared for, especially a small hospital; sickhouse.
A clinic or dispensary within another institution.
infirmary.ety: From Medieval Latin infirmaria, from Latin infirmus.

infirmity.zh: n. 虚弱, 病身, 疾病 / [医] 衰弱
def: the state of being weak in health or body (especially from old age)
Feebleness, frailty or ailment, especially due to old age.

inflammable.zh: a. 易燃的, 易怒的 / [化] 易燃的

inflammation.zh: n. 怒火, 发火, 燃烧, 发炎 / [医] 炎[症]
def: a response of body tissues to injury or irritation; characterized by pain and swelling and redness and heat
the state of being emotionally aroused and worked up
inflammation.ety: From Middle French inflammation, from Latin īnflammātiō, equivalent to inflame + -ation.

inflammatory.zh: a. 激动的, 煽动的, 炎症性的 / [医] 炎的, 炎性的

inadvertent.zh: a. 漫不经心的, 非故意的

inalienable.zh: a. 不能让与的, 不能转售的, 不能夺取的, 不可分割的

inalienable.ety: Borrowed around 1645 from French inaliénable, from in- + aliénable (“alienable”), equivalent to in- + alienable.

inanimate.zh: a. 失去知觉的, 没生命的, 无精打采的 / [医] 无生命的, 无生机的

inarticulate.ety: From the substantivation of the above adjective through the associated taxon's name (Inarticulata). Used by contrast with Articulata.

incantation.ety: From Middle English incantacioun, from Old French incantation, from Latin incantatio. More at enchant.

incapacitate.zh: vt. 使无能力, 使无行为能力 / [法] 使无资格, 使无能力, 剥夺资格
def: make unable to perform a certain action
incapacitate.ety: Mid-17th century, from incapacity + -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare French incapaciter.

incarcerate.zh: vt. 下狱, 监禁, 禁闭 / [法] 监禁, 使下狱, 禁闭

To lock away; to imprison, especially for breaking the law.
To confine; to shut up or enclose; to hem in.

inception.zh: n. 起初, 获得学位
def: an event that is a beginning; a first part or stage of subsequent events
The creation or beginning of something; the establishment.
A layering, nesting, or recursion of something within itself.

incisive.zh: a. 敏锐的, 机敏的, 激烈的, 切入的, 锋利的 / [医] 切牙的, 切的

A narrow-edged tooth at the front of the mouth of mammals, between the canines and adapted for cutting; in humans there are four in each jaw.

inclination.zh: n. 倾向, 趋向, 倾斜度, 点头 / [化] 倾角

incomparable.zh: a. 无比的, 不能比较的
def: such that comparison is impossible; unsuitable for comparison or lacking features that can be compared
So much better than another as to be beyond comparison.
incomparable.ety: From Middle English incomparable, from Middle French incomparable, from Old French [Term?], from Latin incomparābilis. By surface analysis, in- + comparable.

incompetent.zh: a. 无能力的, 无资格的, 机能不全的, 不胜任的 / n. 无能力者

incompetent.ety: Borrowed from French incompétent, from Late Latin incompetentem, from Latin incompetēns, equivalent to in- + competent.

incongruity.zh: n. 不协调, 不一致, 不合适 / [化] 异元性; 不相容性

The state of being incongruous, or lacking congruence.

incongruity.ety: From Middle French incongruité, from Medieval Latin incongruitās, from Latin incongruus.

incongruous.zh: a. 不协调的, 不一致的, 不合适的

interrogative.zh: n. 疑问词, 问号 / a. 疑惑的, 疑问的

def: consolidating two or more things; union in (or into) one body
learning (of values or attitudes etc.) that is incorporated within yourself

prone.ety: From Middle English prone, proone, proon, from Latin prōnus (“turned forward, bent or inclined”), from prō (“forward”).

def: a function word that is used in place of a noun or noun phrase
A part of speech that refers anaphorically to a noun or noun phrase, which cannot ordinarily be preceded by a determiner and rarely takes an attributive adjective.
Any of the third-person pronouns by which a person prefers to be referred to, typically reflecting their gender identity; often communicated as a subject–object pair.
pronoun.ety: From pro- + noun, modeled on Middle French pronom, from Latin pronomen, itself a calque of Ancient Greek ᾰ̓ντωνῠμῐ́ᾱ (ăntōnŭmĭ́ā).

pronounce.zh: v. 发音, 宣告, 断言
def: speak, pronounce, or utter in a certain way
pronounce.ety: Recorded since c.1330 as Middle English pronouncen (“to utter, declare officially”), from

proof.zh: n. 证据, 证明, 试验, 检验, 考验 / a. 不能透入的, 证明用的, 防...的, 耐...的 / vt. 检验, 试验, 校对, 使不被穿透
def: any factual evidence that helps to establish the truth of something
a formal series of statements showing that if one thing is true something else necessarily follows from it
make or take a proof of, such as a photographic negative, an etching, or typeset
proof.ety: From Middle English proof, from Old French prove, from Late Latin proba (“a proof”), from Latin probō (“to prove”); see prove; compare also the doublet probe.

prop.zh: n. 支柱, 支持者, 倚靠人, 道具, 螺旋桨 / vt. 支撑, 维持
def: a support placed beneath or against something to keep it from shaking or falling
support by placing against something solid or rigid
any movable articles or objects used on the set of a play or movie
prop.ety: From Middle English proppe (“a prop, support, support for a vine or plant”), from Middle Dutch proppe (“support, support for a vine, stopper for a bottle”). Compare Middle Low German proppe (“plug, st

def: cause to move forward with force
propel.ety: From Middle English propellen (“drive out, expel”), from Latin propellō, from pro- (“forward”) and pellō (“to push, to move”).

proper.zh: a. 适当的, 固有的, 高尚的, 专属的 / adv. 完全地, 彻底地
def: marked by suitability or rightness or appropriateness
having all the qualities typical of the thing specified
proper.ety: From Middle English propre, from Anglo-Norman proper, propre, Old French propre (French: propre), from Latin proprius.

property.zh: n. 财产, 所有权, 性质, 属性 / [计] 属性
def: something owned; any tangible or intangible possession that is owned by someone;
a basic or essential attribute shared by all members of a class
any area set aside for a particular purpose
property.ety: From Middle English propertee, properte, propirte, proprete, borrowed from Anglo-Norman and Old French propreté, proprieté (“propriety, fitness, property”), from Latin proprietās (“a peculiarity, one'

prophecy.zh: n. 预言, 预言能力
def: knowledge of the future (usually said to be obtained from a divine source)
a prediction uttered under divine inspiration
prophecy.ety: From Middle English prophecie, from Old French prophetie, from Latin prophētīa, from Ancient Greek προφητεία (prophēteía, “prophecy”), from προφήτης (prophḗtēs, “speaker of a god”), from πρό (pró, “be

def: predict or reveal through, or as if through, divine inspiration
prophesy.ety: From Middle English prophecien; partly from prophecie, and partly from Middle French prophecier, prophesier, from prophecie (“prophecy”). Doublet of prophecy.

prophet.zh: n. 预言者, 先知, 提倡者
def: an authoritative person who divines the future
someone who speaks by divine inspiration; someone who is an interpreter of the will of God
prophet.ety: From Middle English prophete, from Anglo-Norman prophete, from Latin prophēta, from Ancient Greek προφήτης (prophḗtēs, “one who speaks for a god”), from πρό (pró, “before”) + φημί (phēmí, “to tell”).

proponent.zh: n. 建议者, 支持者 / [法] 提议者, 辩护者, 支持者
def: a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea
One who supports something; an advocate.
One who makes a proposal or proposition.
proponent.ety: From Latin prōpōnēns, present participle of prōpōnō (“to put forward; propose”).

proprietary.zh: a. 所有者的, 所有权的, 私有的 / n. 所有者, 业主, 所有权
def: an unincorporated business owned by a single person who is responsible for its liabilities and entitled to its profits
protected by trademark or patent or copyright; made or produced or distributed by one having exclusive rights
proprietary.ety: From French propriétaire, from Latin proprietārius. By surface analysis, propriety + -ary. Compare with the Latin proprietas (“property”) and proprius (“ownership”).

proprietor.zh: n. 所有者 / [经] 所有人, 资本主, 业主
def: (law) someone who owns (is legal possessor of) a business
A sole owner of an unincorporated business, also called a sole proprietor.

propriety.zh: n. 礼貌, 规矩, 适当 / [计] 专有权
def: The particular character or essence of someone or something; individuality.
propriety.ety: From late Middle English proprietee, propretee, propriete (“ownership”), borrowed from Anglo-Norman propreté, Middle French proprieté, from Latin proprietās. By surface analysis, prop(e)r + -iety. Dou

prosaic.zh: a. 散文的, 散文体的, 平凡的
def: not challenging; dull and lacking excitement
prosaic.ety: From Middle French prosaïque, from Medieval Latin prosaicus (“in prose”), from Latin prosa (“prose”), from prorsus (“straightforward, in prose”), from Old Latin provorsus (“straight ahead”), from pro-

prose.zh: n. 散文 / v. 写散文 / a. 散文的, 平凡的
def: ordinary writing as distinguished from verse
matter of fact, commonplace, or dull expression
prose.ety: From Middle English prose, from Old French prose, from Latin prōsa (“straightforward”) from the term prōsa ōrātiō (“a straightforward speech – i.e. without the ornaments of verse”). further etymology

prosper.zh: vi. 繁荣, 兴隆, 成功 / vt. 使成功, 使昌盛
def: make steady progress; be at the high point in one's career or reach a high point in historical significance or importance
To be successful; to succeed; to be fortunate or prosperous; to thrive; to make gain.
prosper.ety: From Old French prosperer, from Latin prosperō (“to render happy”), from prosperus (“prosperous”), from Proto-Italic *prosparos, from Proto-Indo-European *speh₁- (“to succeed”), whence also Latin spēs

prostate.zh: a. 前列腺的 / n. 前列腺
def: a firm partly muscular chestnut sized gland in males at the neck of the urethra; produces a viscid secretion that is the fluid part of semen
prostate.ety: Borrowed from Middle French prostate, a learned borrowing from Medieval Lat

prostrate.zh: a. 拜倒的, 降伏的, 俯卧的, 衰竭的, 沮丧的 / vt. 弄倒, 使屈服, 使俯伏, 使平卧
def: stretched out and lying at full length along the ground
get into a prostrate position, as in submission

protect.zh: vt. 防卫, 保护, 警戒 / [法] 庇护, 保护, 警戒
def: shield from danger, injury, destruction, or damage
use tariffs to favor domestic industry
protect.ety: Attested in English since 1530, from Latin prōtēctus (“covered, protected”), past participle of prōtegō, prōtegere (“to cover the front, protect”) from prō, prō- (“before, in front of”) + tegō, tegere

protein.zh: n. 蛋白质 / a. 蛋白质的

Any of numerous large, complex naturally-produced molecules composed of one or more long chains of amino acids, in which the amino acid groups are held together by peptide bonds.
One of three major classes of food or source of food energy (4 kcal/gram) abundant in animal-derived foods (meat) and some vegetables, such as legumes.
protein.ety: From proto- + -ein. Suggested by Jöns Jacob Berzelius in a letter to Gerardus Johannes Mulder, from French protéine and German Protein, both coined based on Ancient Greek πρωτεῖος (prōteîos, “primary”

protest.zh: n. 抗议, 反对, 抗议书, 断言 / v. 反对, 抗议, 断言
def: a formal and solemn declaration of objection
express opposition through action or words
protest.ety: PIE word *tréyes From the Middle English verb protesten, from Old French protester, from Latin prōtestārī, from prō + testor, from testis (“witness”).

protocol.zh: n. 草案, 礼仪, 协议 / v. 拟定 / [计] 协议, 协议列表实用程序
def: (computer science) rules determining the format and transmission of data
forms of ceremony and etiquette observed by diplomats and heads of state
protocol.ety: Borrowed from Middle French protocolle, protocole (“document, record”), from Late Latin protocollum (“the first sheet of a volume (on which contents and errata were written)”), from Byzantine Greek πρ

proud.zh: a. 骄傲的, 自大的, 自豪的, 辉煌的, 壮丽的
def: feeling self-respect or pleasure in something by which you measure your self-worth; or being a reason for pride
having or displaying great dignity or nobility
proud.ety: From Middle English proud, prout, prut, from Old English prūd, prūt (“proud, arrogant, haughty”) (compare Old English prȳtung (“pride”); prȳde, prȳte (“pride”), see also Old English deal), probably fr

provenance.ety: Borrowed from French provenance (“origin”), from Middle French provenant, present participle of provenir (“come forth, arise”), from Latin provenio (“to come forth”).

proverb.zh: n. 谚语, 格言, 箴言 / vt. 使众所周知, 用谚语表达
def: a condensed but memorable saying embodying some important fact of experience that is taken as true by many people
A commonly used sentence expressing popular wisdom.
Any commonly used turn of phrase expressing a metaphor, simile, or descriptive epithet.
proverb.ety: From Old French proverbe, from Latin proverbium.

province.zh: n. 省, 地方, 职权, 领域 / [法] 省, 地方, 领域
def: the territory occupied by one of the constituent administrative districts of a nation
the proper sphere or extent of your activities

provoke.zh: vt. 激怒, 惹起, 诱导 / [法] 刺激, 煽动, 激怒
def: evoke or provoke to appear or occur
provoke.ety: Borrowed from Middle French provoquer, from Old French, from Latin prōvocāre. Doublet of provocate.

provost.zh: n. 教务长, 监督员, 牧师 / [法] 监督者, 负责官员, 监狱看守

The head of various other ecclesiastical bodies, even (rare, obsolete) muezzins.

prowess.zh: n. 英勇, 勇敢, 超凡技术

Skillfulness or extraordinary ability in a particular area of expertise; dexterity, mastery, or proficiency.
Distinguished bravery or courage, especially in battle; heroism.
prowess.ety: From Middle English prowesse, prouwesse, proues, prouesce, prouesse (“bravery in battle; act of bravery; excellence; nobility of character; intelligence”), from Old French proeche, proesce, proeësche

prowl.zh: n. 潜行, 徘徊, 悄悄踱步 / vi. 潜行以觅食, 徘徊 / vt. 徘徊
def: move about in or as if in a predatory manner
loiter about, with no apparent aim
the act of prowling (walking about in a stealthy manner)
prowl.ety: From Middle English prollen, of unknown origin.

prude.zh: n. 拘守礼仪的人, 故作正经的人
def: a person excessively concerned about propriety and decorum
A person who is or tries to be excessively proper, especially one who is easily offended by matters of a sexual nature.
prude.ety: From French prude, from Old French prude, prode, feminine of prou, prod, prud (“good, excellent, brave”), from Latin prōde. Related to proud but unrelated to prudent.

prune.zh: n. 洋李, 李子干, 深紫红色, 傻瓜 / vt. 修剪, 砍掉, 删除 / vi. 删除, 删节
def: cultivate, tend, and cut back the growth of
weed out unwanted or unnecessary things

pry.zh: n. 杠杆, 窥探, 好奇者 / vi. 打听, 窥探 / vt. 撬动, 撬开, 费力得到
def: to move or force, especially in an effort to get something open: "Raccoons managed to pry the lid off the garbage pail"
search or inquire in a meddlesome way

prelude.zh: n. 前奏, 序幕, 序诗, 前奏曲 / vi. 作为前奏 / vt. 作为...的开头
def: something that serves as a preceding event or introduces what follows
serve as a prelude or opening to
music that precedes a fugue or introduces an act in an opera
prelude.ety: From Middle French prélude (“singing to test a musical instrument”), from Medieval Latin preludium, from Latin praelūdere.

premier.zh: n. 总理, 首相 / a. 首位的, 最初的
def: the person who holds the position of head of the government in the United Kingdom
be performed for the first time
premier.ety: Borrowed from Middle French premier (adjective), from Latin prīmārius. Doublet of primary.

premiere.zh: v. 初次公演, 首次露面 / n. 初次的演出 / a. 首次的, 首位的
def: the first public performance of a play or movie

premise.zh: n. 前提, 房屋连地基, 上述各项 / vt. 预先提出, 引出, 作为...的前提 / vi. 作出前提
def: a statement that is assumed to be true and from which a conclusion can be drawn
set forth beforehand, often as an explanation
furnish with a preface or introduction

premium.zh: n. 额外补贴, 奖金, 奖赏, 保险费 / [医] 保险费

the amount that something in scarce supply is valued above its nominal value

prepare.zh: vt. 准备, 筹备, 使在思想上有准备, 制造, 调制 / vi. 预备
def: make ready or suitable or equip in advance for a particular purpose or for some use, event, etc
prepare for eating by applying heat
to prepare verbally, either for written or spoken delivery
prepare.ety: Partially a back-formation from preparation; and partially borrowed from Middle French preparer, from Classical Latin praeparāre (“make ready in advance”), from prae- (“pre-”) + parāre (“make ready”).

preposterous.zh: a. 反常的, 乖戾的, 荒谬的, 首末倒置的
def: Absurd, or contrary to common sense.
preposterous.ety: From Latin praeposterus (“with the hinder part before, reversed, inverted, perverted”), from prae (“before”) + posterus (“coming after”).

presence.zh: n. 出席, 面前, 存在, 仪态, 风度 / [电] 出现
def: the state of being present; current existence
the immediate proximity of someone or something
an invisible spiritual being felt to be nearby
presence.ety: Through Old French presence, from Latin praesentia (“a being present”), from praesentem. Displaced native Old English andweardnes.

present.zh: n. 现在, 礼品, 瞄准 / a. 现在的, 出席的 / vt. 介绍, 引见, 赠送, 提出, 呈现, 上演
def: temporal sense; intermediate between past and future; now existing or happening or in consideration
give an exhibition of to an interested audience
being or existing in a specified place

preside.zh: vi. 统辖, 当主人, 主持 / [法] 主持, 负责, 指挥
def: To act as president or chairperson.
preside.ety: From Old French presider, from Latin praesidēre (“preside”), from pre- (“before”) + sedere (“to sit”). Displaced Old English foresittan, which might have been a calque of the Latin.

press.zh: n. 压, 揿, 按, 人群, 印刷机, 压力, 出版社, 记者, 报刊, 新闻舆论, 紧迫 / vt. 压, 压榨, 紧抱, 逼迫, 推进, 强迫征募, 催逼 / vi. 压, 重压, 催促, 拥挤, 奋力前进, 受压
def: exert pressure or force to or upon
force or impel in an indicated direction

prestige.zh: n. 声望, 威望, 威信 / [经] 商誉, 声誉
def: a high standing achieved through success or influence or wealth etc.
The quality of how good the reputation of something or someone is, how favourably something or someone is regarded.

pretend.zh: v. 假装, 伪称, 自命, 自称
def: make believe with the intent to deceive
pretend.ety: From Anglo-Norman pretendre, Middle French pretendre (French prétendre (“to claim, demand”)), from Latin praetendere (“to put forward, hold out, pretend”), from prae- (“pre-”) + tendō (“stretch”); see

pretense.zh: n. 借口, 虚假, 伪装
def: the act of giving a false appearance
pretense.ety: Borrowed from Middle French pretensse, from Late Latin praetēnsus, past participle of Latin praetendō (“to pretend”), from prae- (“before”) + tendō (“to stretch”); see pretend.

pretext.zh: n. 借口, 托词 / v. 以...为借口
def: something serving to conceal plans; a fictitious reason that is concocted in order to conceal the real reason
pretext.ety: From Latin praetextum (“an ornament, etc., wrought in front, a pretense”), neuter of praetextus, past participle of praetexere (“to weave before, fringe or border, allege”).

def: to a moderately sufficient extent or degree
pleasing by delicacy or grace; not imposing
pretty.ety: From Middle English prety, preti, praty, prati, from Old English prættiġ (“tricky, crafty, sly, cunning, wily, astute”), from Proto-West Germanic *prattug, from Proto-Germanic *prattugaz (“boastful, s

prevent.zh: v. 预防, 防止, 阻止, 妨碍
def: keep from happening or arising; make impossible
stop (someone or something) from doing something or being in a certain state
prevent.ety: From Middle English preventen (“anticipate”), from Latin praeventus, perfect passive participle of praeveniō (“to anticipate”), from prae (“before”) + veniō (“to come”).

previous.zh: a. 早先的, 前面的, 过急的 / [法] 以前的, 生前的, 前述的
def: just preceding something else in time or order
(used especially of persons) of the immediate past

prey.zh: n. 被掠食者, 牺牲者 / vi. 捕食
def: a person who is the aim of an attack (especially a victim of ridicule or exploitation) by some hostile person or influence
animal hunted or caught for food
profit from in an exploitatory manner

price.zh: n. 价格, 代价, 价值 / vt. 定...的价格
def: the property of having material worth (often indicated by the amount of money something would bring if sold)
the amount of money needed to purchase something
price.ety: From Middle English price (“price, prize, value, excellence”), borrowed from Old French pris, preis, from Latin pretium (“worth, price, money spent, wages, reward”); compare praise, precious, appraise

insulting terms of address for people who are stupid or irritating or ridiculous

priest.zh: n. 祭司, 牧师, 神父, 神质人员, 僧侣, 泰斗

a person who performs religious duties and ceremonies in a non-Christian religion

def: An original form or object which is a basis for other forms or objects (particularly manufactured items), or for its generalizations and models.
An early sample or model built to test a concept or process.

protagonist.zh: n. 主人公, 主角, 领导者

the principal character in a work of fiction
protagonist.ety: From Ancient Greek πρωταγωνιστής (prōtagōnistḗs, “a chief actor”), from πρῶτος (prôtos, “first”) + ἀγωνιστής (agōnistḗs, “a combatant, pleader, actor”). By surface analysis, prot- (“first”) + agonist

preternatural.zh: a. 超自然的, 异常的

To put forward; to offer for discussion or debate.
propound.ety: From the Middle English proponen (“to put forward”), from Latin prōpōnere (“to put forward”), from prō- (“before”) + pōnere (“to put”). Doublet of propose. Compare expound.

progress.zh: n. 进步, 发展, 前进 / vi. 进步, 进行

the act of moving forward (as toward a goal)

prohibit.zh: vt. 禁止, 阻止 / [经] 禁止
def: To forbid, disallow, or proscribe officially; to make illegal or illicit.
prohibit.ety: From Middle English prohibiten, from Latin prohibeō (“to fend off, prevent, prohibit”) (through past participle prohibitus).

project.zh: n. 计划, 设计, 事业 / vt. 计划, 设计, 投掷, 发射, 使凸出, 放映 / vi. 凸出

prologue.zh: n. 开场白, 序言, 序幕 / vt. 为...作序, 加上...前言
def: A speech or section used as an introduction, especially to a play or novel.
prologue.ety: From Middle English prologue, prologe, from Old French prologue, from Latin prologus, from Ancient Greek πρόλογος (prólogos). Equivalent to pro- + -logue.

prolong.zh: vt. 延长, 拖延, 拖长 / [化] 冷凝管
def: lengthen in time; cause to be or last longer
lengthen or extend in duration or space
prolong.ety: Either a back-formation from prolongation, or from Old French prolonguer or porloignier, from Latin prōlongō, from prō + longō. Doublet of purloin.

promote.zh: vt. 促进, 晋升, 创办, 推销 / [经] 促进, 推广, 推销
def: contribute to the progress or growth of
give a promotion to or assign to a higher position
make publicity for; try to sell (a product)
promote.ety: From Latin prōmōtus, perfect passive participle of prōmoveō (“move forward, advance”).

proportion.zh: n. 比例, 比率, 均衡, 部分, 面积 / vt. 使成比例, 使均衡
def: the quotient obtained when the magnitude of a part is divided by the magnitude of the whole
balance among the parts of something
proportion.ety: From Middle English proporcion, from Old French proportion, from Latin prōportiō (“comparative relation, proportion, symmetry, analogy”), from pro (“for, before”) + portio (“share, part”); see portion

propose.zh: vt. 计划, 打算, 建议, 提议, 求(婚) / vi. 打算, 求婚
def: make a proposal, declare a plan for something
present for consideration, examination, criticism, etc.
propose.ety: From Middle English proposen, from Anglo-Norman proposer (verb), propos (noun), Middle French proposer (verb), propos (noun), from Latin prōpōnō, prōpōnere, with conjugation altered based on poser. Do

proscribe.zh: vt. 剥夺...的公民权, 使失去法律保护, 把...充军, 把...放逐, 排斥, 禁止
proscribe.ety: From Middle English proscriben, from Latin prōscrībō (“to proclaim, forbid, banish”).

prosecute.zh: vt. 告发, 起诉, 彻底进行, 执行, 从事 / vi. 告发, 起诉, 作检察官
def: conduct a prosecution in a court of law
bring a criminal action against (in a trial)
carry out or participate in an activity; be involved in
prosecute.ety: Borrowed from Latin prōsecūtus, perfect participle of prōsequor. Doublet of pursue, from Old French. Compare also persecute.

prospect.zh: n. 景色, 展望 / vt. 勘探, 勘察 / vi. 勘探, 有前途
def: belief about (or mental picture of) the future
someone who is considered for something (for an office or prize or honor etc.)
prospect.ety: From Middle English prospecte, from Latin prōspectus (“view, sight, prospect; panorama”), from prōspiciō (“to look forward”) + -tus (suffix forming action nouns), from pro (“before, forward”) + speciō

prostitute.zh: n. 妓女, 男娼 / vt. 使沦为妓女 / a. 卖淫的, 堕落的
def: a woman who engages in sexual intercourse for money
sell one's body; exchange sex for money
prostitute.ety: From Latin prōstitūtus, past participle of prōstituō, from prō̆ (“for, before”) + statuō (“to set up, to erect”).

protract.zh: vt. 延长, 拖延, 伸出, 绘制 / [法] 延迟, 拖延, 延长
def: lengthen in time; cause to be or last longer
To draw out; to extend, especially in duration.
protract.ety: From the past participle stem of Latin prōtrahō. By surface analysis, pro- + tract.

protrude.zh: vi. 伸出, 突出 / vt. 使伸出, 使突出
def: extend out or project in space

provide.zh: vt. 提供, 供应, 规定, 预备 / vi. 作准备, 抚养, 规定
def: give something useful or necessary to
give what is desired or needed, especially support, food or sustenance
determine (what is to happen in certain contingencies), especially by including a proviso condition or stipulation
provide.ety: Inherited from Middle English providen, from Latin prōvidēre (“to foresee, act with foresight”). Doublet of purvey.

prefigure.zh: vt. 预示, 预见, 预想
prefigure.ety: From Middle English prefiguren, from Latin praefigurare, from figurare (“to shape, picture”).

prefix.zh: 前缀, 称谓 / [计] 地区号码, 前缀

prefix.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin praefīxum, from Latin praefīxus, past participle of praefīgō (“to (fix, fasten, set up) in front”, “to fix on the (end, extremity)”) (from prae- (“before”) + fīgō (“to fix”, “

prejudice.zh: n. 偏见, 成见, 侵害 / vt. 使存偏见, 使有成见, 侵害
def: a partiality that prevents objective consideration of an issue or situation
prejudice.ety: From Middle English prejudice, from Old French prejudice, derived from Latin praeiūdicium (“previous judgment or damage”), from prae- (“before”) + iūdicium (“judgment”).

premature.zh: a. 早产的, 过早的, 不成熟的 / n. 早产儿, 过早发生的事物
def: born after a gestation period of less than the normal time
uncommonly early or before the expected time
premature.ety: From Latin praemātūrus, equivalent to pre- + mature. First use appears c. 1440 in a translation of Palladius's De Re Rustica.

premeditate.zh: v. 预谋, 预先考虑
def: consider, ponder, or plan (an action) beforehand
think or reflect beforehand or in advance
premeditate.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin praemeditātus, past participle of praemeditor (“to premeditate”). By surface analysis, pre- + meditate.

prenatal.zh: a. 出生以前的, 孕期的 / [医] 产前的, 出生前的
def: A person who is expecting to give birth.

preschool.zh: a. 就学前的 / n. 育幼院, 幼稚园
def: an educational institution for children too young for elementary school
Of or relating to the years of early childhood before attendance at primary school.

prescribe.zh: v. 规定, 指定, 嘱咐, 开处方
def: To order (a drug or medical device) for use by a particular patient (under licensed authority).
To specify by writing as a required procedure or ritual; to lay down authoritatively as a guide, direction, or rule of action.
prescribe.ety: Borrowed from Latin praescrībere, from prae- (“before, in front”) and scrībere (“to write”).

preserve.zh: vt. 保护, 保持, 保存, 维持, 腌, 禁猎 / vi. 加工食品, 禁猎 / n. 加工成的食品, 禁猎地, 保护区, 防护物
def: keep or maintain in unaltered condition; cause to remain or last

def: Set in advance, especially as a default.
The preset settings are fine for most users.

presume.zh: vt. 假定, 推测, 擅自, 意味着 / vi. 擅自行动, 相信

presume.ety: From Middle English presumen, from Anglo-Norman presumer and its source, Latin praesūmere (“to take beforehand, anticipate”), from prae- + sūmere (“to take”).

a screening for a select audience in advance of release for the general public
preview.ety: From pre- + view; compare Old French preveü, past participle of preveoir (“to foresee”).

process.zh: n. 程序, 进行, 过程 / vt. 加工, 使...接受处理, 对...处置, 对...起诉 / a. 经加工的, 有特殊光效的

subject to a process or treatment, with the aim of readying for some purpose, improving, or remedying a condition
process.ety: From Middle English proces, from Old French procés (“journey”), from Latin prōcessus (“course, progression”), nominalization of prōcēdō (“proceed, advance”).

the period from 1920 to 1933 when the sale of alcoholic beverages was prohibited in the United States by a constitutional amendment

an optical instrument that projects an enlarged image onto a screen

the lawyers acting for the state to put the case against the defendant

prospective.zh: a. 预期的, 将来的 / [经] 预期的, 未来的

prospectus.ety: From French prospectus (“a prospectus”), borrowed from Latin prospectus. Doublet of prospect and prospekt.

prostitution.zh: n. 卖淫, 糟蹋, 滥用 / [法] 卖淫, 滥用

provident.zh: a. 有先见之明的, 有远虑的, 节俭的

an early warning about a future event

parity.zh: n. 同等, 同位, 平价, 奇偶性 / [计] 奇偶性

(mathematics) a relation between a pair of integers: if both integers are odd or both are even they have the same parity; if one is odd and the other is even they have different parity
(computer science) a bit that is used in an error detection procedure in which a 0 or 1 is added to each group of bits so that it will have either an odd number of 1's or an even number of…
parity.ety: From Middle French parité, from Late Latin paritās, from Latin pār (“equal”). Equivalent to pari- + -ty.

parliamentary.zh: a. 国会的, 议会的, 议会制度的
def: relating to or having the nature of a parliament
having the supreme legislative power resting with a body of cabinet ministers chosen from and responsible to the legislature or parliament
in accord with rules and customs of a legislative or deliberative assembly

parody.zh: n. 打油诗文, 诙谐的模仿诗文, 拙劣的模仿 / vt. 拙劣模仿, 作模仿诗文
def: a composition that imitates or misrepresents somebody's style, usually in a humorous way
make a spoof of or make fun of
parody.ety: From Latin parōdia, from Ancient Greek παρῳδία (parōidía, “parody”), from παρά (pará, “besides”) + ᾠδή (ōidḗ, “song”).

partial.zh: a. 部分的, 偏袒的, 偏爱的 / n. 分音
def: being or affecting only a part; not total
the derivative of a function of two or more variables with respect to a single variable while the other variables are considered to be constant
partial.ety: From Middle English partiall, parcial, from Old French parcial (“biased or particular”), from Late Latin partiālis (“of or pertaining to a part”), from Latin pars (“part”).

particular.zh: n. 一项(或条、点), 个别项目, 详细说明 / a. 特别的, 独有的, 挑剔的, 详尽的
def: unique or specific to a person or thing or category
separate and distinct from others of the same group or category
a fact about some part (as opposed to general)
particular.ety: From Middle English particuler, from Anglo-Norman particuler, Middle French particuler, particulier, from Late Latin particularis (“partial; separate, individual”), from Latin particula (“(small) part

particulate.zh: n. 微粒 / a. 微粒的
def: a small discrete mass of solid or liquid matter that remains individually dispersed in gas or liquid emissions (usually considered to be an atmospheric pollutant)
particulate.ety: From New Latin particulātus (“divided into small parts”) (also particulāta (“small parts”), from its neuter plural), from Classical Latin particula (“particle”), from pars (“part, piece”) + -cula (dim

partisan.zh: n. 党羽, 虔诚信徒, 同党, 游击队员 / a. 党派的, 偏袒的, 效忠的, 献身的, 盲目推崇的
def: a fervent and even militant proponent of something
devoted to a cause or party
an ardent and enthusiastic supporter of some person or activity
partisan.ety: From French partisan, from Italian partigiano (“defender of a party”), from parte (“part”). Doublet of partigiano. Attested in English from the late 15th century in the noun sense of "party adherent",

partition.zh: n. 分割, 隔离物, 隔墙, 财产分割 / vt. 区分, 瓜分, 隔开, 分割 / [计] 分区; 划分
def: a vertical structure that divides or separates (as a wall divides one room from another)
divide into parts, pieces, or sections
(computer science) the part of a hard disk that is dedicated to a particular operating system or application and accessed as a single unit
partition.ety: Recorded c.1430, "division into shares, distinction," from Middle English particioun, from Old French particion (modern partition), from Latin partitio, partitionem (“division, portion”), from partitu

partly.zh: adv. 部分地, 在一定程度上
def: in part; in some degree; not wholly
In part, or to some degree, but not completely.

passage.zh: n. 通道, 通过, 移居, 航行, 一段, 走廊 / vi. 通过, 经过, 航行, 横渡, 争吵 / vt. (使)马以斜横步前进, 使传代
def: the act of passing from one state or place to the next
a section of text; particularly a section of medium length
a way through or along which someone or something may pass
passage.ety: Borrowed into Middle English from Old French passage, from passer (“to pass”).

passionate.zh: a. 热情的, 热烈的, 易怒的, 热恋的
def: Given to strong feeling, sometimes romantic, sexual, or both.
passionate.ety: From Middle English passionat, from Medieval Latin passiōnātus (“affected, impassioned, libidinous, easely angered”). Equivalent to passion + -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Compare French passionné.

pasteurize.zh: vt. 用巴氏法灭菌 / [医] 施行巴氏消毒
def: heat food in order to kill harmful microorganisms
To heat food for the purpose of killing harmful organisms such as bacteria, viruses, protozoa, molds, and yeasts.
pasteurize.ety: Borrowed from French pasteuriser. From Louis Pasteur, the inventor of the process, + -ize.

pastoral.zh: n. 牧歌, 田园诗 / a. 牧人的, 田园生活的, 牧师的, 田园式的
def: of or relating to a pastor
a musical composition that evokes rural life
a letter from a pastor to the congregation
pastoral.ety: From Middle French, Old French pastoral, from Latin pāstōrālis, from pāstor (“shepherd”), + adjective suffix -ālis.

patchy.zh: a. 补缀的, 凑合的, 不调和的, 散落的, 斑驳的, 不完全的
def: irregular or uneven in quality, texture, etc.
Full of, or covered with, patches; abounding in patches.
Not constant or continuous; intermittent or uneven.

paternal.zh: a. 父亲的, 父系的, 似父亲的, 得自父亲的, 家长式统治的 / [法] 父系的, 父亲的
def: belonging to or inherited from one's father
relating to or characteristic of or befitting a parent
paternal.ety: From Old French paternal (“of a father”) (12th c.), from Vulgar Latin paternālis (“paternal”), from Latin paternus (“of or pertaining to a father, paternal”), from pater (“father”).

paternity.zh: n. 父亲身份, 父系血统, 创始人(身份), 来源, 出处 / [医] 父权, 亲权; 父系
def: the state of being a father
the kinship relation between an offspring and the father
the act of initiating a new idea or theory or writing
paternity.ety: From Middle French paternité, from Old French, from Latin paternitās (“paternity”), from paternus (“of or pertaining to a father, paternal”) + -itās, from pater (“father”).

pathetic.zh: a. 悲哀的, 可怜的, 感伤的, 差劲的 / [医] 感情的
pathetic.ety: From Middle French pathétique, from Latin patheticus, from Ancient Greek παθητικός (pathētikós, “subject to feeling, capable of feeling, impassioned”), from παθητός (pathētós, “one who has suffered, s

patrician.zh: n. 贵族, 有教养的人 / a. 贵族的, 显贵的
def: a person of refined upbringing and manners
befitting a person of noble origin
patrician.ety: Borrowed from Middle French patricien, from Latin patricius, derived from patrēs cōnscrīptī (“Roman senators”). May also have been derived from Latin patricius + -ian

patriot.zh: n. 爱国者, 爱国主义者
def: one who loves and defends his or her country
A person who loves and zealously supports and defends their country.
patriot.ety: From Middle French patriote, from Late Latin patriōta (“fellow countryman”) from the Ancient Greek πατριώτης (patriṓtēs, “of the same country”), from πατρίς (patrís, “father land", "country”), from πα

patronage.zh: n. 赞助, 恩赐态度, 光顾, 任免权, 保护人的身份 / [经] 光顾, 资助, 赞助
def: the act of providing approval and support
support by being a patron of
patronage.ety: From Middle English patronage, from Old French patronage (modern French patronage). Equivalent to patron + -age. Piecewise doublet of patternage.

patronize.zh: vt. 保护, 支援, 赞助, 庇护, 惠顾
def: do one's shopping at; do business with; be a customer or client of
patronize.ety: From patron + -ize (verb ending); or from Old French patroniser, from Medieval Latin patronizāre (“to lead a galley as patron”). Piecewise doublet of patternize.

paunchy.zh: a. 大肚子的, 大腹便便的
def: Having a paunch; having a prominent stomach; potbellied.

pavement.zh: n. 路面, 人行道, 铺面路, 铺路材料
def: the paved surface of a thoroughfare
material used to pave an area
walk consisting of a paved area for pedestrians; usually beside a street or roadway
pavement.ety: From Middle English pament, from Anglo-Norman pavement and reinforced by Middle French pavement; both from Latin pavīmentum (“paved surface or floor”), from pavīre (“to beat, to ram, to tread down”).

payable.zh: a. 可付的, 到期的, 应付的, 有利益的 / [经] 应付的
def: subject to or requiring payment especially as specified
a liability account showing how much is owed for goods and services purchased on credit

payment.zh: n. 付款, 支付的款项(或实物), 偿还, 报应, 惩罚 / [经] 支付, 缴纳, 支付款额
def: a sum of money paid or a claim discharged
an act of requiting; returning in kind
payment.ety: Variant of French Paiement. This surname is mostly found in Canada.

pacific.zh: n. 太平洋 / a. 太平洋的, 太平洋沿岸的, 爱好和平的, 安静的, 平息的
def: the largest ocean in the world
relating to or bordering the Pacific Ocean
disposed to peace or of a peaceful nature
pacific.ety: From Latin pācificus (“peace-making”), so called by Magellan because he sailed peacefully over it after weathering Cape Horn.

pacifist.zh: n. 和平主义者, 反战论者, 不抵抗主义者
def: someone opposed to violence as a means of settling disputes
pacifist.ety: From French pacifiste, equivalent to pacific + -ist.

pacify.zh: vt. 使平静, 安慰, 绥靖, 使服从
def: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of
fight violence and try to establish peace in (a location)
pacify.ety: From Middle French pacifier, from Latin pāx (“peace”) + faciō (“to do, make”). Cognate with pay and peacify.

package.zh: n. 包裹, 套装软件, 包, 包装用物, 程序包 / vt. 包装, 打包 / a. 一揽子的
def: a collection of things wrapped or boxed together
package.ety: Equivalent to pack + -age. Possibly influenced by Anglo-Latin paccagium or Old French pacquage.

packet.zh: n. 小包, 一批信件, 大量, 信息包 / vt. 打包, 装进小包 / [计] 分组, 分组报文, 数据分组
def: a collection of things wrapped or boxed together
(computer science) a message or message fragment
packet.ety: From Middle English pacquet; either from Middle French pacquet, or formed independently from pak and -et.

painful.zh: a. 痛苦的, 困难的, 令人烦恼的 / [医] 疼痛的
def: causing misery or pain or distress
painful.ety: From Middle English paynful, peinful, peynful, paynefull, peynefull, equivalent to pain + -ful. Compare Danish pinefuld (“painful”).

def: a worker who is employed to cover objects with paint
a line that is attached to the bow of a boat and used for tying up (as when docking or towing)
painter.ety: From a variation of panther, paralleling other Southern pronunciations for can't and aunt (see ain't for more details).

palatable.zh: a. 美味的, 好吃的, 可口的 / [医] 适口的, 味美的
def: acceptable to the taste or mind

palpable.zh: a. 可感知的, 明显的, 触摸得到的 / [医] 可触知的
def: capable of being perceived; especially capable of being handled or touched or felt
palpable.ety: From Middle French palpable and its source, Latin palpābilis, which is from palpō (“to touch softly”) + -bilis.

palpitate.zh: vi. 悸动, 心跳, 发抖 / [医] 心悸
def: cause to throb or beat rapidly
palpitate.ety: Borrowed from Latin palpitō, palpitātus (“throb, pulsate, palpitate”).

parallelism.zh: n. 平行, 对应, 类似, 比拟 / [计] 并行性
def: The state or condition of being parallel; agreement in direction, tendency, or character.
The state of being in agreement or similarity; resemblance, correspondence, analogy.
parallelism.ety: From parallel + -ism and from Late Latin parallelismus.

paralyze.zh: vt. 使瘫痪, 使麻痹 / [医] 使麻痹, 使瘫痪
def: make powerless and unable to function
cause to be paralyzed and immobile
paralyze.ety: Partly a borrowing from French. Probably partly either (i) formed within English, by derivation. Or partly (ii) a borrowing from French, combined with an English element. Etymons: Middle English paral

paranoid.zh: a. (似)患妄想狂的, (似)患偏执狂的 / n. 患妄想狂的人

parasitic.zh: a. 寄生的, 由寄生虫引起的 / [计] 寄生的
def: relating to or caused by parasites
of plants or persons; having the nature or habits of a parasite or leech; living off another

particularize.zh: v. 详细说明, 列举, 使特殊
def: To make particular, as opposed to general; to restrict to a specific or individual case, class etc.; to single out.
To be specific about (individual instances); to go into detail (about), to specify.

partiality.zh: n. 偏心, 偏颇, 不公平, 特别喜欢, 癖好 / [法] 偏袒, 偏见, 不公平
def: an inclination to favor one group or view or opinion over alternatives
partiality.ety: From Middle English parcialite, parcialtee, parcyalte, partialte, percialite, from Middle French partialité and its etymon Medieval Latin partiālitās. Doublet of partialitas.

partially.zh: adv. 部分地, 一部分地, 不公平地
def: in part; in some degree; not wholly
To a partial degree or extent, incompletely.

particularly.zh: adv. 特别, 格外, 尤其, 详细地, 细致地
def: to a distinctly greater extent or degree than is common
specifically or especially distinguished from others

patriotic.zh: a. 爱国的, 有爱国心的 / [法] 爱国的, 有爱国心的
def: inspired by love for your country
Inspired by or showing patriotism; done out of love of one's country; zealously and unselfishly devoted to the service of one's country
A postage stamp, Civil War token, etc. bearing a patriotic design.
patriotic.ety: From French patriotique, from Late Latin patriōticus, from Ancient Greek πατριωτικός (patriōtikós), from πατριώτης (patriṓtēs), equivalent to patriot + -ic.

patriotism.zh: n. 爱国心, 爱国精神, 爱国主义
def: love of country and willingness to sacrifice for it
Love of one's country; devotion to the welfare of one's compatriots; passion which inspires one to serve one's country.

paradoxical.zh: a. 似非而是的, 矛盾的, 诡论的 / [医] 奇异的, 矛盾的, 逆理的, 反常的
def: seemingly contradictory but nonetheless possibly true

paradoxically.zh: adv. 反论, 荒谬, 自相矛盾, 似非而可能是
def: In a paradoxical manner; so as to create a paradox.

paralysis.zh: n. 麻痹, 停顿, 瘫痪 / [医] 麻痹, 瘫痪
def: loss of the ability to move a body part
The complete loss of voluntary control of part of a living body, such as one or more limbs.
A state of being unable to act.
paralysis.ety: Borrowed from Latin paralysis, from Ancient Greek παράλυσις (parálusis, “palsy”), from παραλύω (paralúō, “to disable on one side”). By surface analysis, para- + -lysis. Doublet of palsy.

partake.zh: vt. 参与, 分担, 分享 / vi. 分享, 参与, 带有
def: have some of the qualities or attributes of something
have, give, or receive a share of
partake.ety: Back-formation from Middle English part-takinge, part-takynge (“a sharing; partaking”), a calque of Latin particeps (“participating”); equivalent to part + take. Compare take part. In the sense of tak

passport.zh: n. 护照, 手段, 通行证 / [法] 通行证, 护照
def: any authorization to pass or go somewhere
a document issued by a country to a citizen allowing that person to travel abroad and re-enter the home country
any quality or characteristic that gains a person a favorable reception or acceptance or admission
passport.ety: From French passeport, from passer (“pass”) + port (“port”). Compare portpass. Equivalent to pass + port.

password.zh: n. 密码, 口令, 通行手段 / [计] 口令
def: a secret word or phrase known only to a restricted group
A word relayed to a person to gain admittance to a place or to gain access to information.
A string of characters used to log in to a computer or network, to access a level in a video game, and so on; archetypally a word but nowadays often an alphanumeric string or a phrase.
password.ety: From pass + word. The sentry-passing sense predates the cryptographic sense and was its inspiration.

pastime.zh: n. 消遣, 娱乐, 游戏
def: a diversion that occupies one's time and thoughts (usually pleasantly)
Something which amuses, and serves to make time pass agreeably.
pastime.ety: From earlier passtime, pass-time, from Middle English passe tyme, passetyme, calque of Middle French passetemps.

pathway.zh: n. 路径, 途径 / [医] 路径, 道
def: a bundle of myelinated nerve fibers following a path through the brain
pathway.ety: From Middle English pathwei, equivalent to path + way. Cognate with German Pfadweg, Afrikaans padweg.

patriarch.zh: n. 创办人, 家长, 元老, 教长, (天主教)教皇 / [法] 家长, 族长, 创始人
def: title for the heads of the Eastern Orthodox Churches (in Istanbul and Alexandria and Moscow and Jerusalem)
the male head of family or tribe
any of the early biblical characters regarded as fathers of the human race
patriarch.ety: From Middle English patriark, patriarche, from Late Latin patriarcha; later reinforced by Old French patriarche, from Ancient Greek πατριάρχης (patriárkhēs, “the founder of the tribe/family”), from An

patricide.zh: n. 杀父(罪), 杀父者 / [法] 杀父, 杀父者
def: a person who murders their father
patricide.ety: Borrowed from Middle French patricide or Latin patricīdium. Equivalent to patri- + -cide.

patrimony.zh: n. 祖传的财物, 继承物 / [经] 世袭财产, 遗产
def: an inheritance coming by right of birth (especially by primogeniture)
patrimony.ety: From earlier patrimoyne, from patremoyne, from Middle French patrimoine/patremoine, semilearned borrowing from Latin patrimōnium, from pater (“father”) + -mōnium (“state, condition”). First attested i

paycheck.zh: n. 付薪水的支票, 薪水
def: a check issued in payment of wages or salary
A periodic payment, usually in the form of a paper check, received by an employee from an employer for work performed.
paycheck.ety: From pay (“wages or salary”) + check (“a means of payment”).

payoff.zh: n. 发工资, 分赃, 贿赂, 盈利, 报酬, 报应, 结果, 高潮, 决定因素 / a. 决定性的, 产生结果的, 支付的
def: the final payment of a debt
payment made to a person in a position of trust to corrupt his judgment
the income or profit arising from such transactions as the sale of land or other property

payroll.zh: n. 工资名单, 饷金名单, 发放的工资总额 / [计] 工资表, 工资单
def: a list of employees and their salaries
the total amount of money paid in wages
the department that determines the amounts of wage or salary due to each employee

padlock.zh: n. 挂锁, 关闭, 禁止进入
def: a detachable lock; has a hinged shackle that can be passed through the staple of a hasp or the links in a chain and then snapped shut
padlock.ety: From earlier pad lock (19th c.); Middle English padlock, padlokke, from pad-, of unknown origin, + lok (“lock”). Perhaps originally a lock for a pad (“gate”), or a gate opening to a path, or a lock fo

painstaking.zh: n. 辛苦, 苦心, 工夫 / a. 辛苦的, 勤勉的, 小心的
def: characterized by extreme care and great effort
Carefully attentive to details; studious; diligent in performing a process or procedure.
The application of careful and attentive effort.
painstaking.ety: From pains + taking; see take pains. The /ˈpeɪnˌsteɪkɪŋ/ pronunciation which dominates in the United States suggests a reanalysis of the word as pain + staking.

pancake.zh: n. 薄烤饼, 薄煎饼, 烙饼
def: a flat cake of thin batter fried on both sides on a griddle
An thin batter cake similar to a crepe, typically unleavened.
pancake.ety: German surname, Americanized and translated from Pfannkuch, Pfannkuche, also found in north/Low German as Pannkoke, Pankauke, as well as Dutch Pannekoek. All mean "pancake", and could be from a nickna

paperback.zh: n. 平装本, 纸面本
paperback.ety: From paper + back, a shortening of the older term paper-backed book.

def: work that involves handling papers: forms or letters or reports etc.

parachute.zh: n. 降落伞 / vi. 跳伞
def: rescue equipment consisting of a device that fills with air and retards your fall
jump from an airplane and descend with a parachute
parachute.ety: Borrowed from French parachute, from para- (“protection against”) (as in parasol) and chute (“fall”).

paragraph.zh: n. 段落, 短评 / vt. 将...分段, 分段落 / vi. 写短讯
def: one of several distinct subdivisions of a text intended to separate ideas; the beginning is usually marked by a new indented line
divide into paragraphs, as of text
paragraph.ety: From Middle English paragraf, from Middle French paragraphe from Latin paragraphus (“sign for start of a new section of discourse”), from Ancient Greek παράγραφος (parágraphos), from παρά (pará, “besi

parameter.zh: n. 参变数, 参变量, 参数, 参量 / [计] 参量; 参数
def: a constant in the equation of a curve that can be varied to yield a family of similar curves
any factor that defines a system and determines (or limits) its performance
(computer science) a reference or value that is passed to a function, procedure, subroutine, command, or program
parameter.ety: From French paramètre, from New Latin parametrum (“parameter”), from Ancient Greek παρα- (para-, “beside”) + μέτρον (métron, “measure”).

paranoia.zh: n. 偏执狂, 多疑症 / [法] 妄想狂, 偏执狂
def: a psychological disorder characterized by delusions of persecution or grandeur
A psychotic disorder, now called delusional disorder, often (in one of six subtypes) characterized by delusions of persecution and a perceived threat against the individual affected with th…
paranoia.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek παράνοια (paránoia, “madness”), from παράνοος (paránoos, “demented”), from παρά (pará, “beyond, beside”) + νόος (nóos, “mind, spirit”). By surface analysis, para-

paraphrase.zh: n. 释义, 解述, 改写 / vt. 改写, 解述 / vi. 释义, 意译
def: rewording for the purpose of clarification
express the same message in different words
paraphrase.ety: From Middle French paraphrase, from Latin paraphrasis, from Ancient Greek παράφρασις (paráphrasis), equivalent to para- + phrase. Doublet of paraphrasis.

paralytic.zh: a. 麻痹的, 患麻痹的, 中风的 / n. 麻痹患者, 中风患者
def: relating to or of the nature of paralysis
paralytic.ety: Borrowed from French paralytique, from Latin paralyticus, from Ancient Greek παραλυτικός (paralutikós, “paralyzed”).

def: a person who passes by casually or by chance

pathologic.zh: a. 病理学的, 由疾病引起的, (非正式)不合理的, 仅由想象引起的, 不理智的 / [医] 病理的
def: caused by or altered by or manifesting disease or pathology
of or relating to the practice of pathology

pathology.zh: n. 病理学, 病理, 病状, 病变 / [医] 闰理学
def: the branch of medical science that studies the causes and nature and effects of diseases
any deviation from a healthy or normal condition
pathology.ety: From French pathologie, from Ancient Greek πάθος (páthos, “disease”) and -λογία (-logía, “study of”). By surface analysis, path- + -ology or patho- + -logy.

patriarchal.zh: a. 家长的, 族长的, 由族长统治的 / [法] 家长的, 家长制的, 主教的
def: characteristic of a form of social organization in which the male is the family head and title is traced through the male line
relating to or characteristic of a man who is older or higher in rank
patriarchal.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin patriarchālis, from patriarcha + -ālis. Sychronically analyzable as patriarch + -al.

painkiller.zh: n. 解痛药, 止痛片, 止痛药
def: a medicine used to relieve pain
A drug that numbs the pain in the body.
second part of the Stone Age beginning about 750,00 to 500,000 years BC and lasting until the end of the last ice age about 8,500 years BC
of or relating to the second period of the Stone Age (following the eolithic)

paperweight.zh: n. 镇纸, 压纸物, 压纸器

possibility.zh: n. 可能性, 可能的事 / [法] 可能性, 可能发生的事, 不确定权
