a tentative insight into the natural world; a concept that is not yet verified but that if true would explain certain facts or phenomena
possibility.ety: From Middle English possibilite, from Middle French possibilité (from Old French possibilite) and directly from Late Latin possibilitās (“possibility”), from Latin possibilis (“possible”); see possibl

def: to a degree possible of achievement or by possible means

postage.zh: n. 邮资 / [经] 邮费, 邮资
def: a small adhesive token stuck on a letter or package to indicate that that postal fees have been paid

postal.zh: a. 邮政的, 邮局的 / [经] 邮政的
def: of or relating to the system for delivering mail
Relating to the collection, sorting and delivery of mail.
postal.ety: From post + -al, modelled on French postal.

poster.zh: n. 海报, 招贴, 驿马
def: a sign posted in a public place as an advertisement
someone who pastes up bills or placards on walls or billboards
a horse kept at an inn or post house for use by mail carriers or for rent to travelers

postulate.zh: n. 假定, 基本条件 / vt. 要求, 假定
def: (logic) a proposition that is accepted as true in order to provide a basis for logical reasoning
take as a given; assume as a postulate or axiom
postulate.ety: Borrowed from Latin postulātum, a neuter nominalization of postulātus, perfect passive participle of postulō, possibly from poscō. See -ate (noun-forming suffix) for more. Cognate with French postulat

potency.zh: n. 力量, 权力, 效力 / [化] 能力
def: the power or right to give orders or make decisions
capacity to produce strong physiological or chemical effects
the inherent capacity for coming into being
potency.ety: Borrowed from Latin potentia. Doublet of Potenza.

potent.zh: a. 有力的, 有说服力的, 有效的 / [医] 有力的, 有性交能力的
def: having or wielding force or authority
having a strong physiological or chemical effect
potent.ety: From Middle English potent, borrowed from Latin potens, potentis (“powerful, strong, potent”), present participle of posse (“to be able”), from potis (“able, powerful, originally a lord, master”).

potter.zh: n. 陶工, 制陶工人
def: a craftsman who shapes pottery on a potter's wheel and bakes them it a kiln
do random, unplanned work or activities or spend time idly
potter.ety: From Middle English pottere, from Old English pottere (“potter”, in placenames), from Proto-West Germanic *pottārī (“pot-maker”), equivalent to pot + -er. Influenced by Anglo-Norman poter, Old French

pottery.zh: n. 陶器, 陶器厂 / [化] 陶器
def: ceramic ware made from clay and baked in a kiln
a workshop where clayware is made
pottery.ety: From Old French poterie, from potier (“potter”), from the root of pot, equivalent to pot + -ery. First attested in the 13th century.

poverty.zh: n. 贫穷, 贫困, 缺乏 / [医] 贫乏, 缺乏
def: the state of having little or no money and few or no material possessions
The quality or state of being poor; lack of money
A deficiency of something needed or desired
poverty.ety: From Middle English poverte, from Old French poverté (Modern French pauvreté), from Latin paupertās, from pauper (“poor”) + -tas (“noun of state suffix”). Cognates include pauper, poor.

powerful.zh: a. 有力的, 有权力的, 强大的
def: having great power or force or potency or effect
strong enough to knock down or overwhelm
powerful.ety: From Middle English pouerful, powarfull. By surface analysis, power + -ful.

poetic.zh: a. 诗的, 诗意的, 诗人的
poetic.ety: From Middle French poetique, from Latin poeticus, from Ancient Greek ποιητικός (poiētikós) from ποιέω (poiéō, “make”). Displaced native Old English sċoplīċ and lēoþlīċ. Doublet of poietic.

poetry.zh: n. 诗, 韵文, 诗歌艺术
def: any communication resembling poetry in beauty or the evocation of feeling
poetry.ety: From Middle English poetrye, poetrie, a borrowing from Old French pöeterie, pöetrie, from Medieval Latin poētria, from poēta (“poet”), from Ancient Greek ποιητής (poiētḗs, “poet; author; maker”). Disp

poignant.zh: a. 辛酸的, 尖锐的, 剧烈的
def: keenly distressing to the mind or feelings
poignant.ety: From Middle English poynaunt, poynant, borrowed from Anglo-Norman puignant, poynaunt etc., present participle of poindre (“to prick”), from Latin pungō (“prick”). Doublet of pungent.

pointless.zh: a. 不尖的, 钝的, 不得要领的
def: not having a point especially a sharp point
serving no useful purpose; having no excuse for being
pointless.ety: From Middle English pointles, poynteles, poyntlees. By surface analysis, point + -less.

poisonous.zh: a. 有毒的, 恶毒的, 讨厌的 / [医] 有毒的
def: having the qualities or effects of a poison
marked by deep ill will; deliberately harmful
poisonous.ety: From Middle English poisounous, poysonouse. By surface analysis, poison + -ous.

poker.zh: n. 戳的人, 拨火棍, 纸牌戏 / vt. 烙制
def: fire iron consisting of a metal rod with a handle; used to stir a fire
any of various card games in which players bet that they hold the highest-ranking hand
poker.ety: American English, perhaps from first element of German Pochspiel, from German pochen, perhaps from French poque. First appeared in the 19th century.

polar.zh: a. 两极的, 极地的, 正好相反的, 极性的 / n. 极线, 极面
def: having a pair of equal and opposite charges
characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
located at or near or coming from the earth's poles
polar.ety: Learned borrowing from Late Latin polāris. By surface analysis, pole + -ar.

polemical.zh: a. 好辩的；好争论的；挑起论战的
def: of or involving dispute or controversy
Being an attempt to evaluate the arguments comprehensively.
Prone to causing disputes; inclined to causing the expression of opposing opinions, disputatious, contentious, edgy.
polemical.ety: From polemic + -al. By surface analysis, polem- + -ic + -al.

political.zh: a. 政治的, 政治上的, 政党的, 从事政治的 / [法] 政治的, 政治上的, 党派政治的
def: involving or characteristic of politics or parties or politicians- Daniel Goleman
of or relating to your views about social relationships involving authority or power
of or relating to the profession of governing

politician.zh: n. 政客, 政治家, 从事党派政治的人 / [法] 政客, 政治家
def: a leader engaged in civil administration
a person active in party politics
a schemer who tries to gain advantage in an organization in sly or underhanded ways

pollinate.ety: From pollin- (compound form of "pollen") + -ate (verb-forming suffix). From oblique stem of Latin pollen, pollinis.

pollster.zh: n. 民意调查人, 民意测验经办人
def: someone who conducts surveys of public opinion
A professional who conducts or analyzes opinion polls.

pollutant.zh: n. 污染物质 / [法] 污染物
def: waste matter that contaminates the water or air or soil
A foreign substance that makes something dirty, or impure, especially waste from human activities.

pollution.zh: n. 污染, 玷污 / [化] 污染
def: undesirable state of the natural environment being contaminated with harmful substances as a consequence of human activities
the act of contaminating or polluting; including (either intentionally or accidentally) unwanted substances or factors
pollution.ety: From Middle English pollucioun, pollucion (“desecration, impurity”), from Anglo-Norman pollutiun, Middle French pollution, pollucion, and their source, post-classical Latin pollūtiō (“defilement, dese

pompous.zh: a. 爱炫耀的, 虚夸的, 盛大的
def: characterized by pomp and ceremony and stately display
pompous.ety: From Middle English pompous, from Old French pompeux, pompos, from Late Latin pomposus, from Latin pompa (“pomp”), from Ancient Greek πομπή (pompḗ, “a sending, a solemn procession, pomp”), from πέμπω

ponderable.zh: a. 可估量的, 可称量的, 有重量的 / n. 值得估量的事物
def: capable of being weighed or considered- James Jeans

ponderous.zh: a. 沉重的, 笨重的, 毫无趣味的, 生硬的
def: slow and laborious because of weight
having great mass and weight and unwieldiness
the character of the positive electric pole
a quality or state characterized by certainty or acceptance or affirmation and dogmatic assertiveness
the quality of being encouraging or promising of a successful outcome

potentate.zh: n. 有权的人, 有势力的人, 统治者
def: a ruler who is unconstrained by law
A powerful leader; a monarch; a ruler.
potentate.ety: From Middle English potentat, from Old French, from Late Latin potentātus (“rule, political power”), from Latin potēns (“powerful, strong”), the active present participle of possum (“to be able”).

popularity.zh: n. 名声, 受大众欢迎, 流行
def: the quality of being widely admired or accepted or sought after
The quality or state of being popular; especially, the state of being widely liked or in favor with the people at large.
The quality or state of being adapted or pleasing to common, poor, or vulgar people
popularity.ety: From popular + -ity, from Latin popularitas (“an effort to please the people”).

population.zh: n. 人口, 人口数 / [化] 群体; 总体
def: the people who inhabit a territory or state
a group of organisms of the same species inhabiting a given area
(statistics) the entire aggregation of items from which samples can be drawn
population.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin populatio (“a people, multitude”), as if a noun of action from Classical Latin populus, equivalent to populate + -ion. Doublet of poblacion.

positively.zh: adv. 明确地, 肯定地, 无疑地, (非正式)确实地, 真正地
def: so as to be positive; in a positive manner
positively.ety: From Middle English positively, equivalent to positive + -ly.

potential.zh: n. 潜在性, 可能性, 潜力, 潜能, 势, 位 / a. 有潜力的, 可能的, 潜在的
def: the inherent capacity for coming into being
expected to become or be; in prospect
potential.ety: From Late Latin potentialis, from Latin potent

polarity.zh: n. 极性, 截然相反 / [医] 极性, 极性现象
def: a relation between two opposite attributes or tendencies
having an indicated pole (as the distinction between positive and negative electric charges)

polarize.zh: v. (使)偏振, (使)极化, (使)两极分化
def: cause to vibrate in a definite pattern
cause to concentrate about two conflicting or contrasting positions
become polarized in a conflict or contrasting situation
polarize.ety: From French polariser, equivalent to polar + -ize.

pollination.zh: n. 授粉 / [医] 授粉[作用], 传粉[作用]
def: transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of a plant
The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma; effected by insects, birds, bats and the wind etc.
lack of elegance as a consequence of being pompous and puffed up with vanity
The quality of being pompous; self-importance.
pomposity.ety: From Middle English pomposite (“solemnity”), from Latin pompōsitās. By surface analysis, pomp + -osity.

pontifical.zh: a. 教皇的, 主教的, 大祭司的 / n. 主教全套服饰, 主教仪典
def: the vestments and other insignia of a pontiff (especially a bishop)
proceeding from or ordered by or subject to a pope or the papacy regarded as the successor of the Apostles
denoting or governed by or relating to a bishop or bishops

pontificate.zh: vi. 自负地谈论, 执行教皇职务
def: the government of the Roman Catholic Church
talk in a dogmatic and pompous manner
pontificate.ety: From the past participle stem of Medieval Latin pontificō, from Latin pontifex (“high priest”), from pons (“bridge”) + facere (“make”).

potentiality.zh: n. 潜在性, 可能性
def: the inherent capacity for coming into being
an aptitude that may be developed
corn having small ears and kernels that burst when exposed to dry heat
small kernels of corn exploded by heat
popcorn.ety: Short for popped corn. By surface analysis, pop + corn.

portfolio.zh: n. 皮包, 公文包, 部长职务, 有价证券财产目录, 艺术代表作选辑 / [法] 公文包, 文件夹, 阁员职务
def: a large, flat, thin case for carrying loose papers or drawings or maps; usually leather
a set of pieces of creative work collected to be shown to potential customers or employers
a list of the financial assets held by an individual or a bank or other financial institution
portfolio.ety: From Italian portafoglio; cognate with French portefeuille (“folder, wallet”), from Latin portāre (“to carry”) and folium (“sheet”). The meaning "collection of responsibilities" came by extension in t

def: public box for deposit of mail
a card for sending messages by post without an envelope
A rectangular piece of thick paper or thin cardboard, typically used for sending messages by mail without the need for an envelope.
To send a postcard to someone.
a code of letters and digits added to a postal address to aid in the sorting of mail
A sequence of letters and numbers added to a postal address to aid the sorting and delivery of post or mail.
The region denoted by such a sequence.

postman.zh: n. 邮递员 / [法] 邮递员, 理财法庭的高级律师
def: a man who delivers the mail
Someone who delivers the post (mail) to, and/or collects the post from, residential or commercial addresses, or from public mailboxes.
One of the two most experienced barristers in the Court of Exchequer, who have precedence in motions, so called from the place where he sat, the other of the two being the tubman.

postmaster.zh: n. 邮政局长 / [计] 邮件主管员
def: the person in charge of a post office
The head of a post office.
The administrator of an electronic mail system.

potash.zh: [化] 钾碱 / [医] 钾硷, 碳酸钾, 草硷
def: a potassium compound often used in agriculture and industry
The water-soluble part of wood ash, used for making soap and glass and as a fertilizer (chemically speaking, an impure form of potassium carbonate (K₂CO₃) mixed with other potassium salts).
Potassium. Chiefly used in the names of compounds of the form "... of potash".
potash.ety: From pot + ash, because the substance was originally obtained by leaching ash in water and then boiling down the resulting solution in a pot. Compare Dutch potas, German Pottasche.

def: whatever happens to be available especially when offered to an unexpected guest or when brought by guests and shared by all
A meal, especially one offered to a guest, consisting of whatever food is available.
Whatever is available in a particular situation.
potluck.ety: From pot + luck. According to the Oxford English Dictionary, sense 3 (“a shared meal consisting of whatever guests have brought”) is unlikely to have been influenced by potlatch.

potpourri.zh: n. 混合物, 杂曲, 混成曲, 杂集, 大杂烩
def: a collection containing a variety of sorts of things
a musical composition consisting of a series of songs or other musical pieces from various sources
a jar of mixed flower petals and spices used as perfume
potpourri.ety: From French pot-pourri (“stew, potpourri”), a calque of Spanish olla podrida (“stew”, literally “rotten pot”). Doublet of olla podrida.

pocketbook.zh: n. 笔记本, 钱袋, 皮夹, 经济来源
def: a pocket-size case for holding papers and paper money
pocketbook.ety: 1610s, from pocket + book, popularized in its sense as a paperback by the success of Pocket Books in the United States after its 1939 launch.

pockmark.zh: n. 痘疮, 麻子 / [医] 量袋器
def: a scar or pit on the skin that is left by a pustule of smallpox or acne or other eruptive disease
mark with or as if with pockmarks
a member of a police force
A police officer, usually a male.
A glass rod capped at one end with rubber, used in a chemistry laboratory for gravimetric analysis.

policewoman.zh: n. 女警察 / [法] 女警察

pornography.zh: n. 色情描写, 黄色书刊, 色情画, 色情照片, 色情文学 / [法] 色情画, 色情文学, 黄色读物
def: creative activity (writing or pictures or films etc.) of no literary or artistic value other than to stimulate sexual desire
The explicit literary or visual depiction of sexual subject matter; any display of material of an erotic nature.
The depiction of (non-sexual) subject matter so that it elicits feelings analogous to erotic pleasure; any such depiction.
pornography.ety: Borrowed from French pornographie. By surface analysis, porno- + -graphy.

potboiler.zh: n. (以糊口而写的)粗制滥造文艺作品, 粗制滥造作品的人
def: a literary composition of poor quality that was written quickly to make money (to boil the pot)

polyglot.zh: a. (使用)多种语言的, 多种文字对照的 / n. 使用多种语言的人, 多种文字对照本
def: a person who speaks more than one language
having a command of or composed in many languages
polyglot.ety: PIE word *glōgʰs Borrowed from Attic Greek πολύγλωττος (polúglōttos, “speaking many languages, multilingual”), alternative form of Ancient Greek πολῠ́γλωσσος (polŭ́glōssos, “speaking many languages, m

def: a person of great and varied learning
A person with extraordinarily broad and comprehensive knowledge.
polymath.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek πολυμαθής (polumathḗs, “having learnt much”), first attested in 1624. From πολύς (polús, “much”) (for more, see poly-) + μανθάνω (manthánō, “to learn”). Compare op

poseur.zh: n. 装模作样的人；装腔作势的人
def: a person who habitually pretends to be something he is not
One who affects some behaviour, style, attitude or other condition, often to impress or influence others.

postdate.zh: vt. 填迟...的日期 / n. 事后日期
def: establish something as being later relative to something else

postgraduate.zh: a. 大学毕业后的, 大学研究院的 / n. 研究生
def: a student who continues studies after graduation
of or relating to studies beyond a bachelor's degree

postpone.zh: vt. 延迟, 使延期, 缓办, 搁延 / vi. 延缓, 延缓发作
def: hold back to a later time
To delay or put off an event, appointment, etc.
To place after in order; to deem less important.
postpone.ety: From Latin postpōnō (“to put after; to postpone”) from post (“after”) + pōnō (“to put; to place”), compare forestall.

postscript.zh: n. 附言 / [计] PostScript页面描述语言
def: a note appended to a letter after the signature
textual matter that is added onto a publication; usually at the end
postscript.ety: From New Latin postscriptum, from Latin, neuter of postscriptus, past participle of postscrībō (“write after”), from post (“after”) + scrībō (“write”). By surface analysis, post- + script.

def: belonging to the period after a war
any of numerous synthetic resins; they are light and strong and weather resistant
a complex ester used for making fibers or resins or plastics or as a plasticizer
any of a large class of synthetic fabrics

polygon.zh: n. 多角形, 多边形 / [计] 多边形
def: a closed plane figure bounded by straight sides
A plane figure bounded by edges that are all straight lines.
The boundary of such a figure.
polygon.ety: From Ancient Greek πολύγωνον (polúgōnon), from πολύς (polús, “many”) + γωνία (gōnía, “angle”), equivalent to poly- + -gon.

polymer.zh: n. 聚合物, 聚合体 / [化] 多聚体; 高分子; 大分子; 聚合物
def: a naturally occurring or synthetic compound consisting of large molecules made up of a linked series of repeated simple monomers
A long or larger molecule consisting of a chain or network of many repeating units, formed by chemically bonding together many identical or similar small molecules called monomers. A polyme…
A material consisting of such polymer molecules.
polymer.ety: From poly- + -mer, from Ancient Greek πολύς (polús, “many”) + μέρος (méros, “part”). Coined by Jöns Jacob Berzelius in 1833, though his definition was quite different from the modern one.

polytechnic.zh: a. 各种工艺的, 工艺教育的 / n. 工艺专科学校, 理工专科学校
def: a technical school offering instruction in many industrial arts and applied sciences
That teaches applied arts, sciences, technology, engineering and other academic subjects.
An educational institute that teaches applied arts and sciences rather than academic subjects.
polytechnic.ety: First attested in 1805. From French polytechnique, from the École polytechnique, engineering school founded 1794 in Paris; from Greek πολύτεχνος "skilled in many arts," from πολύς "many" (see poly-) +

posthumous.zh: a. 遗腹的, 死后的 / [医] 遗腹的
def: occurring or coming into existence after a person's death
Taking place after one's own death.
posthumous.ety: From Latin posthumus, a variant spelling of postumus, superlative form of posterus (“coming after”), the ⟨h⟩ added by association with humus (“ground, earth”) referring to burial.

polyandry.zh: n. 一妻多夫, 多雄蕊式 / [医] [一雌]多雄配合, [一妻]多夫配合
def: having more than one husband at a time
A form of polygamy where a woman is married to two or more husbands simultaneously.
The mating pattern whereby a female copulates with plural males.

suborn.zh: vt. 使作伪证, 唆使, 怂恿, 收买
def: incite to commit a crime or an evil deed
induce to commit perjury or give false testimony
suborn.ety: PIE word *upó Borrowed from Anglo-Norman suburner, subhorner, and Middle French suborner, subourner (“to induce (someone) to commit a crime (specifically perjury) or wrongdoing”) (modern French suborn

succour.zh: n. 解救, 援助者 / vt. 解救, 援助
succour.ety: The noun is derived from Middle English socour, interpreted as the singular form of socours (“help; encouragement; remedy; protection; helper, protector”), which is from Anglo-Norman socurs, sucurs an

surfeit.zh: n. 过食, 过度, 恶心 / vt. 使厌腻, 使沉溺于 / vi. 饮食过度
def: the state of being more than full
the quality of being so overabundant that prices fall
surfeit.ety: From Middle English surfeite, surfet, a borrowing from Anglo-Norman surfet, surfeit and Old French sorfet, sorfait, past participle of surfaire (“to augment, exaggerate, exceed”), from sur- (“over”) +

superior.zh: n. 长者, 占优势的人, 上级 / a. 上级的, 出众的, 高傲的
def: of high or superior quality or performance
of or characteristic of high rank or importance
one of greater rank or station or quality
superior.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French superiour, from Latin superior (“higher, upper”).

superlative.zh: a. 最上的, 无比的, 过度的 / n. 最好的人(物), 最高程度, 最高级
def: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development
superlative.ety: From Middle English superlatyf, from Old French superlatif, from Late Latin superlātīvus, from Latin superlātus (“carried above, over; extravagant, of hyperbole”), past participle of superfero (“carry

supersede.zh: vt. 代替, 取代, 接替 / [法] 替代, 替换, 充任
def: take the place or move into the position of
To displace in favor of itself.
supersede.ety: From Middle French superseder (“postpone, defer”), from Latin supersedēre, from super (“over”) + sedēre (“to sit”). The meaning “to replace” is from 1642, probably by association with unrelated preced

def: an irrational belief arising from ignorance or fear
A belief considered to be irrational, unfounded, or based solely on fear and ignorance, particularly credulous reverence towards and belief in supernatural forces.
superstition.ety: From Middle French superstition, from Latin superstitio (“superstition”), from superstāre (“to stand above, to stand upon, to survive”) + -tiō (“-tion: forming nouns”), from super- (“above, over, upon

superstitious.zh: a. 迷信的 / [法] 迷信的, 由迷信引起的
def: showing ignorance of the laws of nature and faith in magic or chance
Arising from or having the character of superstitions.
superstitious.ety: From Old French superstitieux, from Latin superstitiōsus, from superstitio + -ōsus. Cognate with Dutch superstitieus.

supine.zh: a. 仰卧的, 掌心向上的, 懒散的 / [医] 仰卧的, 旋后的
supine.ety: The adjective is borrowed from Latin supīnus, from *sup- (see sub (“under”)) + -īnus (“of, pertaining to”). The word is cognate with Catalan supí, Italian supino, Old French sovin, Middle French souvi

def: a light evening meal; served in early evening if dinner is at midday or served late in the evening at bedtime
a social gathering where a light evening meal is served
supper.ety: From Middle English soper, from Old French soper, from sope (“soup”). Compare French souper.

def: take the place or move into the position of
To take the place of; to replace, to supersede.
supplant.ety: From Middle English supplanten, supplaunten, from Old French supplanter, from Latin supplantō (“trip up”), from sub (“from below, under”) + planta (“sole”).

supple.zh: a. 柔软的, 逢迎的, 顺从的 / vt. 使柔软, 使顺从
def: (used of e.g. personality traits) readily adaptable
supple.ety: From Middle English souple, from Old French souple, soupple (“soft, lithe, yielding”), from Latin supplic-, supplex (“suppliant, submissive, kneeling”), of uncertain formation. Either from sub + plicō

supply.zh: n. 补给, 供给, 供应品 / vt. 补给, 供给, 提供, 补充 / vi. 替代
def: give something useful or necessary to
an amount of something available for use
circulate or distribute or equip with
supply.ety: From Middle English supplien, borrowed from Old French soupleer, souploier, from Latin suppleo (“to fill up, make full, complete, supply”). The Middle English spelling was modified to conform to Latin

support.zh: n. 支持, 支撑, 援助, 供养, 支撑物 / vt. 支援, 支撑, 帮助, 支持, 忍受, 供养, 证实 / [计] 后援; 支持
def: give moral or psychological support, aid, or courage to

extent.ety: From Middle English extente, from Anglo-Norman extente and Old French estente (“valuation of land, stretch of land”), from estendre, extendre (“extend”) (or from Latin extentus), from Latin extendere

extract.zh: n. 榨出物, 精汁, 摘录, 选段 / vt. (费力地)取出, 采掘, 榨取, 摘录, 吸取 / [计] 提取
def: remove, usually with some force or effort; also used in an abstract sense
a solution obtained by steeping or soaking a substance (usually in water)
extract.ety: Borrowed from Latin extractum, neuter perfect passive participle of extrahō, from ex- (“out of”) + trahō (“to drag”).

extraterrestrial.zh: a. 地球外的, 地球大气圈外的
def: originating or located or occurring outside Earth or its atmosphere
a form of life assumed to exist outside the Earth or its atmosphere

extrovert.zh: n. 外向性格的人 / [医] 外倾[性格]者
def: (psychology) a person concerned more with practical realities than with inner thoughts and feelings
being concerned with the social and physical environment
extrovert.ety: Alteration of earlier extravert (by influence of introvert), from German Extravert, popularized in psychology by Phyllis Blanchard's 1918 "Psycho-Analytic Study of August Comte". By surface analysis,

extrude.zh: vt. 挤出, 压出, 逐出 / vi. 伸出, 突出
def: form or shape by forcing through an opening
To form or shape (a metal, plastic etc.) by forcing it through a die or an opening.

except.zh: vt. 除, 除外 / vi. 反对 / prep. 除了...之外, 若不是, 除非
def: prevent from being included or considered or accepted
except.ety: Borrowed from Middle French excepter, from Latin exceptus.

excess.zh: n. 过度, 剩于, 超过, 超额 / a. 过量的, 额外的
def: a quantity much larger than is needed
more than is needed, desired, or required
immoderation as a consequence of going beyond sufficient or permitted limits
excess.ety: From Middle English exces (“excess, ecstasy”), from Old French exces, from Latin excessus (“a going out, loss of self-possession”), from excedere, excessum (“to go out, go beyond”). See exceed.

exchange.zh: n. 交换, (电话)交换局, 交换机, 汇兑, 交易所 / v. 交换, 交易, 兑换 / [计] 交换; 电话局
def: chemical process in which one atom or ion or group changes places with another
give to, and receive from, one another
a mutual expression of views (especially an unpleasant one)
exchange.ety: From Middle English eschaungen, from Anglo-Norman eschaungier, Old French eschanger, from the Old French verb eschangier, eschanger (whence modern French échanger), from Vulgar Latin *excambiāre (from

excise.zh: n. (烟、酒等)消费税, 货物税, 国产税 / vt. 切除
def: remove by erasing or crossing out or as if by drawing a line
a tax that is measured by the amount of business done (not on property or income from real estate)
excise.ety: From Middle Dutch excijs, altered under the influence of Latin excisus (“cut out, removed”), from earlier accijs (“tax”), from Old French acceis (“tax, assessment”) (whence modern French accise), from

exclaim.zh: v. 大叫, 呼喊, 大声叫
def: utter aloud; often with surprise, horror, or joy
exclaim.ety: From Middle French exclamer, from Latin exclāmō, exclāmāre (“call out”), from ex- + clāmō (“to call”).

exclude.zh: vt. 除外, 排除, 排斥 / [医] 除外(诊断)
def: prevent from being included or considered or accepted
exclude.ety: Borrowed from Latin exclūdō, from prefix ex- (“out”) + variant form of verb claudō (“close”).

excogitate.zh: vt. 想出, 研究出, 设计, 发明
def: come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort
excogitate.ety: From Latin excōgitāre, from ex- + cōgitāre (“think”).

exculpate.zh: vt. 使无罪, 开脱 / [法] 使无罪, 申辩无罪, 辩解
def: pronounce not guilty of criminal charges
To clear of or to free from guilt; exonerate.
exculpate.ety: From Medieval Latin exculpātus, perfect passive participle of exculpō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ex- (“out, from”) + culpa (“fault; blame”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix).

exhibitor.zh: n. (展览会的)参加者, 电影院经理, 电影院老板, 电影放映者, 展出者 / [法] 出示证物人, 展览者, 提供者
def: someone who organizes an exhibit for others to see
exhibitor.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin exhibitor. First attested in 1654. By surface analysis, exhibit + -or.

exporter.zh: n. 出口商, 输出者, 出口公司 / [经] 出口商, 输出者
def: a businessperson who transports goods abroad (for sale)
One who, or that which, exports: especially a person who or organization that exports or sells goods made in one country for delivery in another country.

expurgate.zh: vt. 删除, 修订, 使纯洁
def: edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate
To edit out (incorrect, offensive, or otherwise undesirable information) from a book or other publication; to cleanse; to purge.
To undertake editing out incorrect, offensive, or otherwise undesirable information from (a book or other publication); to cleanse; to purge.
expurgate.ety: From Latin expurgātus, perfect passive participle of expurgō (“purge, cleanse, purify”).

extemporize.zh: v. 即席演说, 即兴演奏, 当场作成
def: manage in a makeshift way; do with whatever is at hand

exhibition.zh: n. 表现, 展览会, 展览品 / [医] 投药, 展览, 展出
def: a collection of things (goods or works of art etc.) for public display
exhibition.ety: From Old French exhibicion. Equivalent to exhibit + -ion.

exorbitant.zh: a. 过度的, 过高的, 过分的
def: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
Exceeding proper limits; excessive or unduly high; extravagant.
exorbitant.ety: From Middle English exorbitant, through Old French from Late Latin exorbitāns, present active participle of exorbitō (“to go out of the track”), from ex (“out”) + orbita (“wheel-track”); see orbit. Co

expatriate.zh: n. 移居国外者, 侨民, 被流放者, 背井离乡者 / vt. 逐出国外, 脱离国籍, 放逐 / vi. 移居国外
def: a person who is voluntarily absent from home or country
move away from one's native country and adopt a new residence abroad
expatriate.ety: The verb is first attested in 1787, the adjective and noun in 1812; borrowed from Medieval Latin expatriātus, perfect passive participle of expatriō (“to banish”) (see -ate (etymology 1,2 and 3)), fro

expedient.zh: n. 权宜之计 / a. 权宜的, 方便的, 有用的
def: a means to an end; not necessarily a principled or ethical one
expedient.ety: From Middle English expedient, from Old French expedient, from Latin expediens (stem expedient-), present participle of expedire (“to bring forward, to dispatch, to expedite; impers. to be profitable,

expedite.zh: vt. 加快, 促进, 发出 / a. 畅通的, 无阻碍的, 迅速的, 方便的
def: speed up the progress of; facilitate
expedite.ety: From Latin expedītus (“unimpeded, unfettered”), perfect passive participle of expediō (“bring forward, set right”).

expenditure.zh: n. 开支, 费用, 用光, 消费额 / [经] 支出, 费用, 消费
def: money paid out; an amount spent
the act of spending money for goods or services
expenditure.ety: From stem of Medieval Latin expenditus, irregular perfect passive participle of expendō (“to weigh, to pay out”), + -ure (“process or result”).

explosion.zh: n. 爆发, 激增, 爆炸(声) / [化] 爆炸
def: a violent release of energy caused by a chemical or nuclear reaction
the act of exploding or bursting
explosion.ety: From French explosion, from Latin explōsiōnis, genitive form of explōsio, from explōdo (“to drive out by clapping”), from ex- and plōdo (“to clap or strike”). For more information see explode.

explosive.zh: n. 炸药, 爆破音 / a. 易爆发的, 爆炸的, 暴躁的
def: serving to explode or characterized by explosion or sudden outburst
liable to lead to sudden change or violence
a chemical substance that undergoes a rapid chemical change (with the production of gas) on being heated or struck
explosive.ety: From Latin explōs-, stem of the perfect passive participle of explōdō + the suffix -ive.

exposition.zh: n. 阐述, 讲解, 说明, 博览会, 展览会 / [经] 展览会, 集市, 义卖市场
def: a systematic interpretation or explanation (usually written) of a specific topic
a collection of things (goods or works of art etc.) for public display
an account that sets forth the meaning or intent of a writing or discourse
exposition.ety: From Middle English exposicioun, from Old French esposicion, from Latin expositiō, from expōnere (“to put forth”). The sense meaning "exhibition" is a later semantic loan from French exposition.

expository.zh: a. 说明的, 解释的
def: serving to expound or set forth
Serving to explain, explicate, or elucidate; expositive; of or relating to exposition.

expostulate.zh: vi. 劝诫, 告诫；忠告
def: reason with (somebody) for the purpose of dissuasion
To protest or remonstrate; to reason earnestly with a person on some impropriety of conduct [(often) with with].
expostulate.ety: From Latin expostulō (“demand, claim”) + -ate (verb-forming suffix). By surface analysis, ex- + postulate.

exposure.zh: n. 暴露, 揭发, 揭露 / [化] 曝光量; 照射; 照射量
def: vulnerability to the elements; to the action of heat or cold or wind or rain or "they died from exposure";
the act of subjecting someone to an influencing experience

expression.zh: n. 表达, 表现, 词语, 措辞 / [计] 表达式
def: the feelings expressed on a person's face
the communication (in speech or writing) of your beliefs or opinions
expression.ety: Borrowed from Middle French expression, from Late Latin expressiō, expressiōnem (“a pressing out”). Morphologically express + -ion.

expressive.zh: a. 表达的, 富于表情的
def: Conveying the speaker's emotions and/or attitudes, in addition to the denotative or literal meaning.

expressly.zh: adv. 明白地, 清楚地, 特意地
def: with specific intentions; for the express purpose
In an express or explicit manner; in a clear or specific manner.

expropriate.zh: vt. 剥夺, 没收, 征用 / [法] 征用, 没收, 剥夺...的所有权
def: To deprive a person of (their private property) for public use.
To surrender a claim to private property without material compensation; to deprive oneself of private propriety rights.

expulsion.zh: n. 逐出, 开除, 驱逐, 排气 / [医] 逼出
def: the act of forcing out someone or something
the act of expelling or projecting or ejecting
expulsion.ety: From Middle English expulsioun, from Old French expulsion, from Latin expulsio, expulsionem.

extemporaneous.zh: a. 无准备的, 即席的, 临时的 / [医] 临时的, 当时的
def: with little or no preparation or forethought
With inadequate preparation or without advance thought; offhand.
extemporaneous.ety: From Late Latin extemporāneus, from Latin ex tempore (“impromptu”).

extension.zh: n. 延长, 扩充, 范围, 扩展名 / a. 伸缩的 / [计] 扩展名, 扩充名
def: a mutually agreed delay in the date set for the completion of a job or payment of a debt
act of expanding in scope; making more widely available
the spreading of something (a belief or practice) into new regions
extension.ety: From Middle English extensioun, from Old French estension, from Latin extensiō, extensiōnem.

extensive.zh: a. 广的, 广泛的, 多方面的 / [经] 广大的, 扩大的
def: large in spatial extent or range or scope or quantity
broad in scope or content- T.G.Winner
of agriculture; increasing productivity by using large areas with minimal outlay and labor
extensive.ety: From late Middle English, borrowed from Late Latin extensīvus, from Latin extensus.

extenuate.zh: vt. 减轻, 为...找借口 / [法] 减轻, 低估, 藐视
def: lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of
Of a person: emaciated, wasted, weakened; of the body or part of it: atrophied, shrunken, withered.
Of a quality or thing: lessened, weakened.
extenuate.ety: From Middle English extenuat (“(medicine) made thin, emaciated”), from Latin extenuātus (“diminished, reduced, thinned”), perfect passive participle of extenuō (“to diminish, reduce, thin”) (see -ate

external.zh: n. 外部, 外面 / a. 外部的, 客观的, 表面的
def: happening or arising or located outside or beyond some limits or especially surface
external.ety: From Late Middle English, from Medieval Latin externus (“outward, external”), from exter/exterus (“on the outside, outward”).

exterminate.zh: vt. 扑灭, 消灭, 根绝
def: kill en masse; kill on a large scale; kill many
destroy completely, as if down to the roots "root out corruption"
exterminate.ety: Borrowed from Latin exterminātus, perfect passive participle of exterminō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ex- (“thoroughly”) + terminō (“to finish, close, end”), from terminus (“limit, end”) +

extraction.zh: n. 抽出, 取出, 拔出术, 抽出物 / [化] 萃取; 提取
def: the process of obtaining something from a mixture or compound by chemical or physical or mechanical means
the action of taking out something (especially using effort or force)
extraction.ety: From Old French estraction, from Medieval Latin extractio.

extractor.zh: n. 抽出器, 拔取的人, 抽出者 / [计] 抽取字; 析取字
def: an instrument for extracting tight-fitting components
an apparatus that uses centrifugal force to separate particles from a suspension
a mechanism in a firearm that pulls an empty shell case out of the chamber and passes it to the ejector

extraordinary.zh: a. 非常的, 特别的, 非凡的 / [经] 非常的, 特别的, 临时的
def: beyond what is ordinary or usual; highly unusual or exceptional or remarkable
far more than usual or expected
(of an official) serving an unusual or special function in addition to those of the regular officials
extraordinary.ety: From Latin extrāōrdinārius, from extrā ōrdinem (“outside the order”). By surface analysis, extra- + ordinary. Doublet of extraordinaire.

def: draw from specific cases for more general cases
gain knowledge of (an area not known or experienced) by extrapolating

exacerbate.zh: vt. 使恶化, 使增剧, 激怒, 使加剧
exacerbate.ety: First attested in 1660; borrowed from Latin exacerbātus, perfect passive participle of Latin exacerbō (“to provoke”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ex- (“out of; thoroughly”) + acerbō (“to emb

exception.zh: n. 例外, 除外, 异议 / [计] 例外; 异常
def: an instance that does not conform to a rule or generalization
exception.ety: From Middle English exception, excepcioun, from Anglo-Norman excepcioun, from Old Frenc

excessive.zh: a. 过度的, 过多的, 极端的 / [法] 过度的, 过分的, 额外的
def: unrestrained, especially with regard to feelings
excessive.ety: From Middle English excessive, excessif, from Old French excessif, from Medieval Latin excessivus, equivalent to excess + -ive.

exclamation.zh: n. 惊呼, 激烈言词, 惊叹词
def: a loud complaint or protest or reproach
exclamation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French exclamation, from Latin exclāmātiō, from exclāmō (“to cry out”) + -tiō.

exclusion.zh: n. 排除, 除外, 逐出 / [医] 排除, 除外, 分离术
exclusion.ety: From Middle English exclusion, exclusioun, from Old French [Term?] and Latin exclusiō, from exclūdō. By surface analysis, exclude + -sion.

exclusive.zh: a. 排外的, 独占的, 唯一的 / [计] 独占的
def: not divided or shared with others
a news report that is reported first by one news organization
excluding much or all; especially all but a particular group or minority
exclusive.ety: From Latin exclūsīvus, from excludere (“to shut out, exclude”), from ex- (“out”) + variant form of verb claudere (“to close, shut”).

excursion.zh: n. 远足, 游览圆, 短程旅行 / [医] 移动, 离轨, 逸出
def: wandering from the main path of a journey
excursion.ety: Borrowed from Latin excursiō (“a running out, an inroad, invasion, a setting out, beginning of a speech”), from excurrere (“to run out”), from ex (“out”) + currere (“to run”). By surface analysis, exc

extortionate.zh: a. 敲诈的, 勒索的, 过度的, 昂贵的 / [法] 勒索的, 敲诈的, 强夺的
def: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
Of, related to, or typifying extortion (“the practice of obtaining money or other property by the use of force or threats”).
Greatly exceeding what is moderate or reasonable; exorbitant.

expediency.zh: n. 权宜, 方便, 私利
def: the quality of being suited to the end in view
The quality of being fit or suitable to effect some desired end or the purpose intended; suitability for particular circumstance or situation.
Pursuit of the course of action that brings the desired effect even if it is unjust or unprincipled.

expedition.zh: n. 远征, 探险队, 迅速
def: a military campaign designed to achieve a specific objective in a foreign country
an organized group of people undertaking a journey for a particular purpose
a journey organized for a particular purpose
expedition.ety: From Middle French expédition, and its source, Latin expeditio.

expeditious.zh: a. 迅速的, 敏捷的
def: Completed or done with efficiency and speed; facilitating speed.
expeditious.ety: From Middle English expedycius (“useful, fitting”), from Latin expedītus (“disengaged, ready, convenient, prompt; unfettered, unencumbered”), past participle of expediō.

extensively.zh: adv. 广大, 广延, 外延, 大面积(耕种), 粗放, 广博, 广泛, 广阔

externalize.zh: vt. 给...以外型, 使客观化, 使具体化 / [医] 表面化
def: make external or objective, or give reality to

extraordinarily.zh: adv. 非凡, 破例, 特别, 非常, 离奇, 使人惊奇, 惊人, 特命, 特派

exceptionable.zh: a. 可反对的, 可抗议的
def: liable to objection or debate; used of something one might take exception to
Liable to cause disapproval, objection or debate.

exceptional.zh: a. 例外的, 异常的, 特别的
def: far beyond what is usual in magnitude or degree
surpassing what is common or usual or expected
deviating widely from a norm of physical or mental ability; used especially of children below normal in intelligence

excessively.zh: adv. 过多, 极度, 过度, 过分
def: to a degree exceeding normal or proper limits

exclusively.zh: adv. 排他地, 仅仅, 专门, 只, 仅, 唯一地, 专有地
def: without any others being included or involved
to the exclusion of anything or anyone else; solely or entirely
exclusively.ety: From Middle English exclusyvely; equivalent to exclusive + -ly.

exceptionally.zh: adv. 特殊地；异常地；例外地
def: To an unusual, remarkable or exceptional degree.
a broad highway designed for high-speed traffic
A divided highway, especially one whose intersections and direct access to adjacent properties have been eliminated.

explicate.zh: vt. 详细说明, 解释, 说明, 引伸
def: elaborate, as of theories and hypotheses

coruscate.zh: vi. 闪烁, 熠熠生辉, 焕发
def: be lively or brilliant or exhibit virtuosity
coruscate.ety: From Latin coruscātus, perfect passive participle of coruscō (“to flash, gleam”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

cosset.zh: n. 供玩赏的小动物, 爱畜 / vt. 宠爱, 珍爱, 溺爱
def: To treat like a pet; to overly indulge.
To fondle; to touch or stroke lovingly.
cosset.ety: Perhaps from Middle English cotsete, from Old English cotsǣta (“cottager”), from cot (“cottage”) (Modern English cot (“cottage”) (archaic)) + -sǣta (“-sitter”); compare coscet. Compare German Hauslamm

coterie.zh: n. 同人, 圈内人, 小集团
def: an exclusive circle of people with a common purpose
A circle of individuals who associate with one another for a common purpose.
A communal burrow of prairie dogs.
be false to; be dishonest with
cozen.ety: Perhaps from obsolete Italian cozzonare (“to cheat”), from cozzone (“middleman, broker”), from Latin cōciō (“dealer”).

def: To disdain; to value at little or nothing; to treat or regard with contempt.
To commit an offence of contempt, such as contempt of court; to unlawfully flout (e.g. a ruling).
contemn.ety: From Middle English contempnen, from Old French contemner, from Latin contemnō (“to scorn”). See also contempt.

contumacious.zh: a. 不听命令的, 反抗权威的, 反抗法院命令的 / [法] 反抗法院命令的, 不听命令的
def: Contemptuous of authority; willfully disobedient; rebellious.
Willfully disobedient to the summons or orders of a court.
contumacious.ety: From Latin contumāx (“stubborn, obstinate”) + -ious. By surface analysis, contum(ax) + -acious.

contumacy.zh: n. 拒不服从, 反抗权威 / [法] 不听法院命令, 藐视法庭
def: willful refusal to appear before a court or comply with a court order; can result in a finding of contempt of court
obstinate rebelliousness and insubordination; resistance to authority
contumacy.ety: From Latin contumācia, from contumāx (“refusing to appear in a court of law in disobedience of a summons; insolent, obstinate, stiff-necked”).

convalesce.zh: vi. 渐渐康复, 渐愈
def: get over an illness or shock
To recover health and strength gradually after sickness or weakness.
convalesce.ety: From Latin convalēscere, from con- (intensive prefix) + valēscere (“to become strong”), inchoative of valēre (“to be strong”).

cornice.zh: n. 檐口 / vt. 给...装檐口
def: a decorative framework to conceal curtain fixtures at the top of a window casing
a molding at the corner between the ceiling and the top of a wall
cornice.ety: From Middle French corniche or Italian cornice, possibly from either (1) Latin cornīx (“crow”) or (2) Latin coronis (“curved line, flourish in writing”), from Ancient Greek κορωνίς (korōnís). See also

corpuscle.zh: n. 细胞, 血球, 微粒 / [计] 微粒, 粒子
def: (nontechnical usage) a tiny piece of anything
either of two types of cells (erythrocytes and leukocytes) and sometimes including platelets
corpuscle.ety: From Latin corpusculum, diminutive of corpus (“body”).

complaisance.zh: n. 谦恭, 殷勤, 顺从
def: a disposition or tendency to yield to the will of others
The quality of being complaisant, amiable or agreeable.
complaisance.ety: From French. See complaisant. By surface analysis, com- + plaisance.

complaisant.zh: a. 谦恭的, 殷勤的, 顺从的
def: showing a cheerful willingness to do favors for others
Willing to do what pleases others; obliging; agreeable.
complaisant.ety: From French complaisant (“willing to please”), from complaire, from Latin complacēre (“please well”), from com- (“with”) + placeō (“please”).

concatenate.zh: vt. 如锁链般连接, 使连锁, 连结 / a. 连锁的, 连结的
def: combine two strings to form a single one
add by linking or joining so as to form a chain or series
concatenate.ety: From the perfect passive participle stem of Latin concatēnāre (“to link or chain together”), from con- (“with”) + catēnō (“chain, bind”), from catēna (“a chain”).

condign.zh: a. (尤指惩罚)应得的, 适宜的
def: fitting or appropriate and deserved; used especially of punishment
Fitting, appropriate, deserved, especially denoting punishment.
condign.ety: From Middle English condigne, from Old French condigne, from Latin condignus, from con- + dignus (“worthy”). Compare deign.

conspectus.zh: n. 概观, 一览表, 大纲
def: A detailed survey or overview of a subject.

colour.zh: n. 颜色, 面色, 颜料, 外貌 / vt. 把...涂上颜色, 粉饰, 使脸红, 歪曲 / vi. 变色
def: having or capable of producing colors
any material used for its color

comatose.zh: a. 昏睡的, 昏睡状态的 / [医] 昏迷的
def: relating to or associated with a coma
in a state of deep and usually prolonged unconsciousness; unable to respond to external stimuli
comatose.ety: Perhaps from French comateux, or from Ancient Greek κῶμα (kôma, “deep sleep”) (genitive κώματος (kṓmatos)). Equivalent to coma + -ose (“full of”)

comestible.zh: a. 可吃的 / n. 食物
def: any substance that can be used as food
comestible.ety: Borrowed from Middle French comestible, or its source, Late Latin comestibilis, from Latin comedō (“to eat”), from com- (English com-) + edō (“I eat”) (as in English edible), from Proto-Indo-European

comity.zh: n. 礼貌, 礼让 / [法] 礼让, 友谊
def: a state or atmosphere of harmony or mutual civility and respect
Courtesy and considerate behaviour towards others; social harmony.

cowardly.ety: From Middle English *cowardly (adjective) and cowardly (adverb), equivalent to coward + -ly. Displaced native Old English earg.

convalescent.zh: a. 恢复健康的, 恢复期的, 渐愈的, 康复的 / n. 恢复中的病人, 康复的人
def: a person who is recovering from illness
returning to health after illness or debility
convalescent.ety: From French convalescent, from Latin convalēscēn(t-)s, present participle of convalēscere (“to become strong or well”); see convalesce.

convection.zh: n. 传送, 对流, 传导 / [化] 对流
def: the transfer of heat through a fluid (liquid or gas) caused by molecular motion
(meteorology) the vertical movement of heat or other properties by massive motion within the atmosphere
convection.ety: From Latin convectiōnem, from convectiō (“act of carrying”), from convect-, past participle stem of convehō (“to carry together”), combination of com- and vehō. By surface analysis, convect + -ion.

conventional.zh: a. 传统的, 习惯的, 约定的 / [经] 惯例的, 常规的, 传统的
def: (weapons) using energy for propulsion or destruction that is not nuclear energy

conversant.zh: a. 熟悉的, 亲近的, 有交情的
def: (usually followed by `with') well informed about or knowing thoroughly
Closely familiar; current; having frequent interaction.
Familiar or acquainted by use or study; well-informed; versed.
conversant.ety: From Old French conversant, present participle of converser.

conversation.zh: n. 会话, 说话, 交谈 / [法] 交谈, 社交, 性交
def: the use of speech for informal exchange of views or ideas or information etc.
Expression and exchange of individual ideas through talking with other people; also, a set instance or occasion of such talking.
Dialogue or interaction regarding a topic.
conversation.ety: From Middle English conversacioun, from Old French conversacion and its etymon, Latin conversātiōnem, accusative singular of conversātiō (“conversation”), from conversor (“abide, keep company with”).

conveyance.zh: n. 运输, 运输工具, 财产转让 / [经] 运输工具, 转让证书, 财产的转让
def: something that serves as a means of transportation
conveyance.ety: From Middle English conveiance, conveyaunce, equivalent to convey + -ance.

conviction.zh: n. 定罪, 信服, 坚信 / [法] 定罪, 证明有罪, 判罪
def: an unshakable belief in something without need for proof or evidence
(criminal law) a final judgment of guilty in a criminal case and the punishment that is imposed
conviction.ety: From late Middle English conviction, from Anglo-Norman conviction, from Latin convictiō, from convictus, the past participle of convincō (“to convict”). Equivalent to convict + -ion.

convulsion.zh: n. 震动, 震撼, 动乱, 惊厥, 痉挛 / [医] 惊厥, 抽搐

cooker.zh: n. 炊事用具, 炉灶, 锅, 炊具, 烹饪用水果, 窜改者, 伪造者 / [化] 蒸锅
def: An appliance or utensil for cooking food.
cooker.ety: From cook + -er (agent noun suffix) or + -er (patient suffix) (apple; one who is cooked).

cookie.zh: n. 饼干, 小甜点 / [建] 糕点
def: any of various small flat sweet cakes (`biscuit' is the British term)
the cook on a ranch or at a camp
a short line of text that a web site puts on your computer's hard drive when you access the web site
cookie.ety: Borrowed from Dutch koekie, dialectal diminutive of koek (“cake”), from Proto-Germanic *kōkô (compare German Low German Kookje (“biscuit, cookie, cracker”), Low German Kook (“cake”), German Kuchen (“c

cooler.zh: n. 冷却器 / [化] 冷却器
def: an iced drink especially white wine and fruit juice

copier.zh: n. 誊写者, 模仿者, 抄写员 / [计] 复制机
def: apparatus that makes copies of typed, written or drawn material
A machine that copies graphical material; a duplicator.

cordial.zh: n. 兴奋剂, 补品 / a. 热忱的, 诚恳的, 有兴奋作用的
def: strong highly flavored sweet liquor usually drunk after a meal
cordial.ety: Inherited from Middle English cordial, from Old French cordial, from Medieval Latin cordiālis (“of the heart”), from cor (“heart”).

corny.zh: a. 谷类的, 乡巴佬似的, 粗野的 / [建] 角制的, 角(质)的
def: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
corny.ety: From Middle English corny, equivalent to corn (“a type of cereal or grain”) + -y. Piecewise doublet of grainy. In the "hackneyed" sense, from "corn catalogue jokes", reputedly low-quality jokes that w

corporal.zh: n. 下士 / a. 肉体的, 身体的, 个人的
def: a noncommissioned officer in the Army or Air Force or Marines
affecting or characteristic of the body as opposed to the mind or spirit
possessing or existing in bodily form- Shakespeare
corporal.ety: From Middle English corporall, corporalle, from the Latin corporāle, the neuter of corporālis representing the doctrine of transubstantiation in which the Eucharist becomes the body of Christ.

corporate.zh: a. 社团的, 合伙的, 公司的 / [经] 团体的, 法人的, 社团的
def: of or belonging to a corporation
possessing or existing in bodily form- Shakespeare
done by or characteristic of individuals acting together
corporate.ety: The adjective is first attested in 1429, the noun in 1849; from Middle English corporat(e) (“(if a true adjective) corporeal, physical, embodied; (participle/participial adjective) incorporated; corpo

corporeal.zh: a. 肉体的, 有形的, 物质的 / [法] 有体的, 具体的, 物质的
def: having material or physical form or substance - Benjamin Jowett
affecting or characteristic of the body as opposed to the mind or spirit
corporeal.ety: From Middle English corporealle, equivalent to Latin corporeus + -al, from corpus (“body”); compare corporal.

corpulent.zh: a. 肥大的, 肥胖的 / [医] 肥胖的
corpulent.ety: From Middle English corpulent, from Old French corpulent, from Latin corpulentus.

correction.zh: n. 订正, 改正, 改正的地方 / [化] 校正
def: the act of offering an improvement to replace a mistake; setting right
a quantity that is added or subtracted in order to increase the accuracy of a scientific measure
correction.ety: From Middle English correccioun, correction, from Old French correccion (French correction), from Latin corrēctiō. Doublet of correctio.

correctly.zh: adv. 对, 正确, 恰当, 符合一般性准则, 符合行为准则, 端正, 符合

correspondence.zh: n. 相符, 通信, 信件 / [医] 对应, 相对
def: communication by the exchange of letters
the relation of corresponding in degree or size or amount
correspondence.ety: From Middle English correspondence, from Latin correspondentia. By surface analysis, correspond + -ence.

correspondent.zh: n. 通讯记者, 通信者 / [经] 客户, 代理商行, 代理银行
def: someone who communicates by means of letters
a journalist employed to provide news stories for newspapers or broadcast media
similar or equivalent in some respects though otherwise dissimilar
correspondent.ety: From Latin, via Middle French or directly, from Medieval Latin correspondēns, present participle of correspondeō.

corrosion.zh: n. 腐蚀, 侵蚀, 腐蚀产生的物质, 铁锈, 锈 / [计] 腐蚀
def: a state of deterioration in metals caused by oxidation or chemical action
corrosion.ety: From Middle English corrosioun, from Old French corrosion, or its source, Late Latin corrōsiōnem, accusative singular of corrōsiō (“gnawing away, corroding”), from Latin corrōdō (“gnaw away, corrode”)

corrosive.zh: a. 腐蚀的, 腐蚀性的, 有害的 / n. 腐蚀物, 腐蚀剂
def: of a substance, especially a strong acid; capable of destroying or eating away by chemical action
a substance having the tendency to cause corrosion (such a strong acids or alkali)

cosmic.zh: a. 宇宙的, 宇宙航行的, 无限的, 有秩序的 / [医] 宇宙的
def: of or from or pertaining to or characteristic of the cosmos or universe
inconceivably extended in space or time

costly.zh: a. 昂贵的, 奢华的, 费用大的
costly.ety: From Middle English costly, costely, costeley, equivalent to cost + -ly.

councillor.zh: n. 地方议会成员, 议会委员, 顾问, 评议员, 参赞 / [法] 议员, 评议员, 顾问
def: In particular, a representative elected to a local authority, such as a city council: a city councillor.
councillor.ety: Alteration of counsellor, by assimilation with council. By surface analysis, council + -or.

counselor.zh: n. 顾问, 参事, 法律顾问
def: someone who gives advice about problems
someone who has supervisory duties at a summer camp
a lawyer who pleads cases in court
counselor.ety: From Middle English counseilour, counseiler, from Anglo-Norman cunseiler, from Old French conseillier, from Latin cōnsiliārius, agent noun from cōnsilior (“to take counsel”), from cōnsilium (“plan, co

countable.zh: a. 能算的, 可计算的 / n. 可数的东西, 可数名词
def: Capable of being counted; having a quantity.
Finite or countably infinite; having a one-to-one correspondence (bijection) with a subset of the natural numbers.

congruity.zh: n. 适合, 一致, 共同点
def: the quality of agreeing; being suitable and appropriate
The quality of agreeing; the quality of being suitable and appropriate.
An instance or point of agreement or correspondence; a resemblance.

congruous.zh: a. 一致的, 适合的, 符合的
congruous.ety: From Middle English [Term?], from Latin congruus, from congruō (“to coincide with; to agree”).

def: the act of acknowledging that someone has an occasion for celebration
(usually plural) an expression of pleasure at the success or good fortune of another
congratulation.ety: From Middle English congratulacion, from Middle French congratulation or its etymon Latin congrātulātiō, from congrātulor (“to congratulate”). By surface analysis, congratulate + -ion.

congruence.zh: n. 适合, 一致, 和谐
def: the quality of agreeing; being suitable and appropriate
The quality of agreeing or corresponding; being suitable and appropriate.
A relation between two numbers indicating they give the same remainder when divided by some given number.
congruence.ety: From Middle English congruence, from Latin congruentia (“agreement”), from congruēns, present active participle of congruō (“meet together, agree”).

connection.zh: n. 连接, 关系, 前后关系 / [计] 连接
def: a relation between things or events (as in the case of one causing the other or sharing features with it)
connection.ety: From Middle English conneccioun, connexioun, conneccyon, conneccion, from Latin connexionem (nominative connexio (“a conclusion, binding together”)), from connectō, an alternative spelling of cōnectō

connivance.zh: n. 默许, 纵容 / [法] 纵容, 默许
connivance.ety: From early 18th c., replaced earlier form connivence (late 16th c.), from Latin connīventia, from connīvēns (“winking”).

def: what you must know in order to determine the reference of an expression
an idea that is implied or suggested
connotation.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin connotātiō, from connotō (“to mark in addition”), from Latin con- (“together, with”) + notō (“to note”); equivalent to connote + -ation.

conqueror.zh: n. 征服者, 胜利者
def: someone who is victorious by force of arms
conqueror.ety: From Middle English conquerour, from Old French conquereor, from conquerre. By surface analysis, conquer + -or.

conscientious.zh: a. 有责任心的, 负责的, 本着良心的 / [法] 凭良心做的, 有道德感的

conscientious.ety: From Middle French conscientieux, from Medieval Latin cōnscientiōsus. Its English equivalent could possibly be analyzed as conscient + -ous. See more at conscience.

def: In a conscious manner; knowingly, volitionally.

consciousness.zh: n. 意识, 知觉, 自觉 / [医] (有)意识, 清醒
def: an alert cognitive state in which you are aware of yourself and your situation

consequential.zh: a. 作为结果的, 随之发生的, 推论的, 间接的, 重大的, 自大的, 傲慢的, 自傲的 / [法] 结果的, 相应而生的, 接着发生的

def: (sentence connectors) because of the reason given
consequently.ety: From Middle English consequentely, consequentliche, consequently; equivalent to consequent + -ly.

considerable.zh: a. 相当的, 可观的, 重要的

considerate.zh: a. 体贴的, 体谅的, 考虑周到的

Consciously thoughtful and observant (often of other people and their rights, needs, feelings and comfort).
Characterised by careful and conscious thought.

consideration.zh: n. 考虑, 原因 / [法] 考虑, 思考, 报酬

information that should be kept in mind when making a decision
a discussion of a topic (as in a meeting)
consideration.ety: From Middle English consideracioun, from Old French consideracion, from Latin cōnsīderātiō. By surface analysis, consider + -ation.

consignment.zh: n. 委托 / [经] 委托, 寄销, 寄销品

the official act of consigning a person to confinement (as in a prison or mental hospital)
the delivery of goods for sale or disposal

consortium.zh: n. 协会, 合伙, (国际性)财团 / [经] 合作, 联合, 财团
def: an association of companies for some definite purpose
An association or combination of businesses, financial institutions, or investors, for the purpose of engaging in a joint venture.
A similar arrangement among non-commercial institutions or organizations.

conspiracy.zh: n. 同谋, 阴谋, 阴谋集团 / [法] 阴谋, 通谋, 共谋
def: a secret agreement between two or more people to perform an unlawful act
a plot to carry out some harmful or illegal act (especially a political plot)
a group of conspirators banded together to achieve some harmful or illegal purpose
conspiracy.ety: From Middle English conspiracie, from Anglo-Norman conspiracie, from Latin cōnspīrātiō, from conspire + -acy.

constancy.zh: n. 坚定不移, 持久不变
def: the quality of being enduring and free from change or variation
(psychology) the tendency for perceived objects to give rise to very similar perceptual experiences in spite of wide variations in the conditions of observation
faithfulness and dependability in personal attachments (especially sexual fidelity)

constantly.zh: adv. 不变地, 不断地, 时常地
def: without variation or change, in every case
constantly.ety: From constant + -ly. Displaced native Old English singallīċe.

consternation.zh: n. 惊愕, 恐怖, 惊惶失措

Amazement or horror that confounds the faculties, and incapacitates for reflection; terror, combined with amazement; dismay.
consternation.ety: From French consternation, from Latin consternātiō. By surface analysis, consternate + -ion.

consulate.zh: n. 领事, 领事任期, 领事馆 / [经] 领事馆
def: diplomatic building that serves as the residence or workplace of a consul
Rule by consuls, as during most periods of the Roman Republic or in France between 1799 and 1804.
The office of a consul, in its various senses.
consulate.ety: From Middle English consulat, consulate, from Latin consulātus, from consul + -ātus. In some senses, via French consulat. By surface analysis, consul + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office).

consultant.zh: n. 顾问, 征询意见者 / [医] 顾问医师
def: A person or party that is consulted.
A person whose occupation is to be consulted for their expertise, advice, service or help in an area or specialty; a party whose business is to be similarly consulted.
consultant.ety: From French consultant, present participle of consulter, from Latin cōnsultāre (“to deliberate, consult”), frequentative of cōnsulere (“to consult, deliberate, consider, reflect upon, ask advice”), fr

consultation.zh: n. 请教, 咨询, 磋商会 / [医] 会诊
def: a conference between two or more people to consider a particular question
the act of referring or consulting
consultation.ety: From Middle French consultation, from Latin consultatio. Morphologically consult + -ation.

contagious.zh: a. 触染性的, 会蔓延的 / [医] (接)触(传)染的
def: easily diffused or spread as from one person to another
(of disease) capable of being transmitted by infection
contagious.ety: From Old French contagieus, from Late Latin contagiosus, from contagio.

contamination.zh: n. 污染, 污物 / [化] 污染; 沾污
def: the act of contaminating or polluting; including (either intentionally or accidentally) unwanted substances or factors

contender.zh: n. 参赛者, 争论者, 斗争者, 竞争者
def: the contestant you hope to defeat
Someone who competes with one or more other people.
Someone who has a viable chance of winning a competition.

contemptible.zh: a. 卑鄙的, 可轻蔑的, 不足挂齿的
contemptible.ety: From Middle English contemptible, from Latin contemptibilis. By surface analysis, contempt + -ible.

contemptuous.zh: a. 轻蔑的, 鄙视的, 瞧不起人的
def: Showing contempt; expressing disdain; showing a lack of respect.

contention.zh: n. 争论, 争辩, 所持的论点 / [计] 争用
def: a point asserted as part of an argument
a contentious speech act; a dispute where there is strong disagreement
the act of competing as for profit or a prize
contention.ety: From Middle English contencion, borrowed from Old French contencion, from Latin contentio, contentionem, from contendō (past participle contentus); equivalent to contend + -tion (similar formation to

contentious.zh: a. 好争吵的, 爱争论的, 有异议的 / [法] 诉讼的, 争执的, 引起争论的
def: inclined or showing an inclination to dispute or disagree, even to engage in law suits
involving or likely to cause controversy- Tim W.Ferfuson

contiguous.zh: a. 邻近的, 接近的 / [医] 接触的
def: very close or connected in space or time
connecting without a break; within a common boundary
having a common boundary or edge; abutting; touching
contiguous.ety: From Latin contiguus (“touching”) + -ous, from contingere (“to touch”); see contingent, contact, contagion.

continence.zh: n. 自制 / [医] 节制; 节欲

voluntary control over urinary and fecal discharge
continence.ety: Dated from the 14th century as Middle English contynence, from Old French continence, from Latin continentia (“a repression”). See also countenance.

continent.zh: n. 大陆, 洲 / a. 自制的
def: one of the large landmasses of the earth
having control over urination and defecation
continent.ety: From Middle English contynent, from Old French continent, from Latin continentem (“continuous; holding together”), present participle of continēre (“to contain”).

contingent.zh: a. 或许发生的, 附随的, 偶然发生的 / n. 偶然事件, 分遣队
def: a gathering of persons representative of some larger group
possible but not certain to occur
contingent.ety: From Middle English, from Old French contingent (whence con- and -ent), from Medieval Latin contingens (“possible, contingent”), present participle of contingere (“to touch, meet, attain to, happen”),

continual.zh: a. 持续不断的, 继续的 / [建] 连续的
def: occurring without interruption; chiefly restricted to what recurs regularly or frequently in a prolonged and closely spaced series
`continual' (meaning seemingly uninterrupted) is often used interchangeably with `continuous' (meaning without interruption)
continual.ety: From Middle English continuel, from Old French continuel, formed from Latin continuus (“continuous”) with the suffix -el, equivalent to continue + -al.

continuation.zh: n. 继续, 续集, 补编 / [医] 连续
def: the act of continuing an activity without interruption
a part added to a book or play that continues and extends it
a Gestalt principle of organization holding that there is an innate tendency to perceive a line as continuing its established direction
continuation.ety: From Middle English continuacion, from Old French continuation, from Latin continuātiō. Morphologically continue + -ation.

continuous.zh: a. 连续的, 继续的, 连续不断的 / [计] 连续的
def: continuing in time or space without interruption- James Jeans
of a function or curve; extending without break or irregularity
continuous.ety: From Latin continuus, from contineō (“hold together”). Displaced native Old English singal.

continuity.zh: n. 连续性 / [化] 连续性
def: a detailed script used in making a film in order to avoid discontinuities from shot to shot
the property of a continuous and connected period of time
continuity.ety: Borrowed from Middle French continuité, from Latin continuitas. By surface analysis, continu(e) + -ity.

contraction.zh: n. 收缩, 缩写式, 害病 / [医] 收缩; 挛缩; 牙弓内缩

the process or result of becoming smaller or pressed together
a word formed from two or more words by omitting or combining some sounds
contraction.ety: PIE word *ḱóm From Late Middle English contraccioun, contraxion (“spasm, contraction; constriction, shrinking; act of pressing together”), from Old French contraction (modern French contraction), from

contractor.zh: n. 立契约的人, 承包商 / [化] 承包者; 承包工厂
def: someone (a person or firm) who contracts to build things
the bridge player in contract bridge who wins the bidding and can declare which suit is to be trumps
contractor.ety: From contractor, an occupational surname for a supplier of goods or services; this surname originated in India, but derives from the English word.

contrary.zh: a. 相反的, 矛盾的, 对立的 / n. 相反, 对立面 / adv. 相反地

contrition.zh: n. 完全悔悟, 悔改, 悔罪

compensatory.zh: a. 赔偿的, 补偿的, 代偿的 / [医] 代偿的, 补偿的

competence.zh: n. 胜任, 职称, 能力 / [医] 能力, 活性

competent.zh: a. 能干的, 胜任的, 有效的, 足够的 / [经] 有权的, 授权的, 胜任的

competition.zh: n. 竞争, 竞赛 / [经] 竞争, 竞销, 比赛

the act of competing as for profit or a prize

competitive.zh: a. 竞争的 / [经] 竞争的
competitive.ety: From Latin competītus (past participle of competere) + -ive.

competitor.zh: n. 竞争者 / [经] 竞争者, 竞争对手
def: the contestant you hope to defeat
A person or organization against whom one is competing.
A participant in a competition, especially in athletics.
competitor.ety: Borrowed from Middle French compétiteur, from Latin competitor.

complacency.zh: n. 满足, 自鸣得意, 自满

A feeling of contented self-satisfaction, especially when unaware of upcoming trouble.
complacency.ety: Late Middle English complacence, from Late Latin complacentia. Compare French complaisance.

completely.zh: adv. 完全地, 十分地, 圆满地

so as to be complete; with everything necessary

completion.zh: n. 完成 / [经] 完井, 结束, 完工
def: (American football) a successful forward pass in football
completion.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin completio. By surface analysis, complete + -tion.

compliance.zh: n. 遵从, 顺从, 屈从 / [化] 柔顺; 顺应

small nocturnal Old World mammal covered with both hair and protective spines

A row of closely planted bushes or trees forming a hedge.
hedgerow.ety: From Middle English heggerowe, heggerewe, heggerawe, from Old English *heċġrāw, *heċġrǣw (attested only as Old English heġerǣwe, heġerēwe (“hedgerow”)), equivalent to hedge + row.

heirloom.zh: n. 传家宝, 动产继承物 / [法] 祖传动产, 传家宝

From now on; from this time on.

hereto.zh: adv. 到此为止, 关于这个 / [法] 至此为止, 至此

headache.zh: n. 头痛, 令人头痛之事 / [医] 头痛

headlamp.zh: n. (汽车的)前灯, (矿工头上的)照明灯, 桅灯

Coastal land that juts into the sea.
The unplowed boundary of a field.

A bright light, with a lens and reflector, on the front of a motor vehicle (or originally a ship or train), designed to illuminate the road when driving at night; normally one of a pair.

headline.zh: n. 大标题, 新闻摘要 / vt. 为...做标题, 写标题

headway.ety: Partly from Middle English hauedwei, from Old English hēafodweġ (“head-road, main-road”); partly as a shortening of ahead-way, the source of the nautical sense. By surface analysis, head + way.

def: contrary to or forbidden by law
the illegitimate offspring of unmarried parents
of marriages and offspring; not recognized as lawful
illegitimate.ety: First attested in 1536, from Latin illēgitimus, most likely an adapted borrowing of Middle French illegitime, equivalent to il- + legitimate, see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3).

illiberal.zh: a. 狭隘的, 无教养的, 吝啬的
def: Restricting or failing to sufficiently promote individual choice and freedom.
illiberal.ety: From Middle French illibéral, from Latin illiberalis, equivalent to il- + liberal.

def: a condition of spiritual awareness; divine illumination
the degree of visibility of your environment

def: to say, state, or perform again

italic.zh: a. 斜体的 / n. 斜体字, 斜体 / [计] 斜体

a branch of the Indo-European languages of which Latin is the chief representative

a contagious skin infection caused by the itch mite; characterized by persistent itching and skin irritation
itch.ety: From Middle English icchen, ȝicchen, from Old English ġiċċan, ġyċċan (“to itch”), from Proto-West Germanic *jukkjan (“to itch”), of unknown origin. Cognate with Scots yeuk (“to itch”), West Frisian jû

traveling from place to place to work
itinerant.ety: From Late Latin itinerantem, present active participle of itineror (“travel”), from itiner-. By surface analysis, Latin itiner- + -ant.

def: an established line of travel or access
itinerary.ety: From Middle English itinerarie, from Latin itinerārium (“an account of a journey, a road-book”), from iter (“a way, journey”). By surface analysis, Latin itiner- + -ary.

italian.zh: n. 意大利人, 意大利语 / a. 意大利的, 意大利语的
def: of or pertaining to or characteristic of Italy or its people or culture or language
a native or inhabitant of Italy
