def: sell or offer for sale from place to place
To sell things, especially door to door or in insignificant quantities.
peddle.ety: Back-formation from pedlar. (Compare burgle from burglar.)

pedestal.zh: n. 支柱, 基架, 基座, 基础 / vt. 加座, 搁在台上, 支持, 提高...的地位
def: a position of great esteem (and supposed superiority)
an architectural support or base (as for a column or statue)
pedestal.ety: Borrowed from Middle French piédestal, itself borrowed from Italian piedistallo (literally “foot stand”). Spelling influenced by Latin pēs, pedem.

pedestrian.zh: n. 行人, 步行者 / a. 人行的, 徒步的, 呆板的, 通俗的, 平淡无奇的
def: a person who travels by foot
pedestrian.ety: From Latin pedester (oblique stem pedestri-) + English -an.

pedigree.zh: n. 血统, 家谱, 名门世系 / [法] 家系, 出身, 血统
def: having a list of ancestors as proof of being a purebred animal
line of descent of a purebred animal
pedigree.ety: From Anglo-Norman pé de grue, a variant of Old French pié de gru (“foot of a crane”), from Latin pes (“foot”) + grus (“crane”).

peek.zh: vi. 偷看, 窥视 / n. 偷看, 看一眼
def: throw a glance at; take a brief look at
peek.ety: From Middle English *peken, piken, pyken (“to peep”), probably a fusion of Middle English pepen (“to peep”) and keken, kiken (“to keek, look, spy”), equivalent to a blend of peep + keek. Perhaps also

peel.zh: n. 皮, 外壳 / vt. 削...皮, 剥去...的壳 / vi. 蜕皮, 剥落, 脱皮, 脱去衣服
def: the rind of a fruit or vegetable
peel.ety: From Middle English pelen, from Old English pilian and Old French peler, pellier; both from Latin pilō, pilāre (“to remove hair from, depilate”), from pilus (“hair”). Doublet of pill.

peep.zh: n. 一瞥, 偷看, 不完全的景象, 初现, 吱吱声, 嘀咕抱怨声, 汽车喇叭声 / vi. 窥视, 出现, 吱吱叫 / vt. 使隐约显现
def: the short weak cry of a young bird
peep.ety: From Middle English pepen. Compare Dutch piepen (“peep”), German Low German piepen (“to peep”), German piepen and pfeifen, all probably onomatopoeic.

peer.zh: n. 同等的人, 匹敌, 贵族 / vi. 凝视, 窥视, 费力地看, 隐现 / vt. 与...同等, 封为贵族
def: a person who is of equal standing with another in a group
a nobleman (duke or marquis or earl or viscount or baron) who is a member of the British peerage
peer.ety: From Middle English peren, pyren, piren (“to peer, gaze”), perhaps from Old English *pȳran (“to look, peer”), from Proto-West Germanic *pūrijan (“to look”), related to Saterland Frisian pierje (“to lo

pettish.zh: a. 易怒的, 闹情绪的, 怒气冲冲的

peregrination.zh: n. 徒步旅行, 旅程, 人生历程, 漫谈, 泛论
def: A person's life regarded as a temporary stay on earth and a journey to the afterlife.
A journey made by a pilgrim; a pilgrimage; also (uncountable) the making of pilgrimages.
peregrination.ety: From Late Middle English peregrinacioun, peregrinacion (“journey; pilgrimage; (figuratively) human journey through life”), from Anglo-Norman peregrinaciun (“human journey through life”), peregrination

perfidious.zh: a. 不忠贞的, 背信的, 有异心的
def: tending to betray; especially having a treacherous character as attributed to the Carthaginians by the Romans
Of, pertaining to, or representing perfidy; disloyal to what should command one's fidelity or allegiance.

perspicacious.zh: a. 聪颖的, 聪明的, 敏锐的, 有洞察力的
perspicacious.ety: First attested 1548, from Late Latin perspicācitās (“discernment”), from Latin perspicax (“sharp-sighted”), from perspiciō (“look through”), from per- (“through”) + speciō (“look at”). See also perspe

perspicuity.zh: n. 明晰, 明了, 简明, 表达清楚, 易懂
def: clarity as a consequence of being perspicuous
Clarity, lucidity, especially in expression; the state or characteristic of being perspicuous.
perspicuity.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin perspicuitās (“evidentness”, “self-evidency”, literally “transparency”, “clarity”, “lucidity”), from Latin perspicuus (“clear”, “transparent”; “evident”); compare perspicacity

perspicuous.zh: a. 表达得清楚的, 明白的, 明了的
def: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable- Robert Burton
Clearly expressed, easy to understand; lucid.
(Of a language or notation) the process of inference from premises to conclusion is explicitly laid out.
perspicuous.ety: From Latin perspicuus, in turn from perspiciō (“see through”).

pertinacious.zh: a. 坚持不放的, 执拗的, 顽固的, 顽强的, (疾病)难以治好的
def: Holding tenaciously to an opinion or purpose.
pertinacious.ety: From pertinace + -ious, from Old French pertinace, from Latin pertinax, from per- (“very”) + tenax (“tenacious”).

peerless.zh: a. 无比的, 出类的, 无双的
def: Without peer or equal; unparalleled, nonpareil. Of the highest quality, best.
peerless.ety: From Middle English pereles, perles; equivalent to peer + -less.

peevish.zh: a. 易怒的, 暴躁的, 带怒气的, 撒娇的
def: Constantly complaining, especially in a childish way due to insignificant matters; fretful, whiny.
Quick to become bad-tempered or cross, especially due to insignificant matters; irritable, pettish, petulant.
peevish.ety: The adjective is derived from Late Middle English pievish, peuysche, pevish, pevysh (“capricious, wilful; perverse, wayward”); further etymology uncertain, possibly from one of the following: * From a

penalize.zh: vt. 处刑, 对...处罚(刑), 使不利 / [法] 处罚, 对...处以刑事惩罚
def: impose a penalty on; inflict punishment on
To subject to a penalty, especially for the infringement of a rule or regulation.

penalty.zh: n. 处罚, 刑罚, 罚款, 罚球, 报应, 不利结果, 妨碍 / [经] 罚金(款), 违约金
def: a payment required for not fulfilling a contract
the disadvantage or painful consequences of an action or condition
penalty.ety: From Middle French pénalité, from pénal, from Latin poenālis, from poena, borrowing of Ancient Greek ποινή (poinḗ), from Proto-Hellenic *kʷoinā́, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷoynéh₂, comprising *kʷey-

pendant.zh: n. 垂饰, 下垂物, 补充的东西, 补编 / [电] 垂环
def: an adornment that hangs from a piece of jewelry (necklace or earring)
branched lighting fixture; often ornate; hangs from the ceiling
pendant.ety: From Anglo-Norman pendaunt, Middle French pendant, noun use of adjective.

pendulum.zh: n. 钟摆, 摇锤, 摇摆不定的事态(或局面) / [化] 摆
def: an apparatus consisting of an object mounted so that it swings freely under the influence of gravity
A body suspended from a fixed support so that it swings freely back and forth under the influence of gravity, commonly used to regulate various devices such as clocks.
The tendency of a situation to oscillate (between two extremes).
pendulum.ety: Borrowed from the neuter of Latin pendulus (“hanging”).

penetrate.zh: vt. 穿透, 刺穿, 渗透, 看穿, 洞察, 了解, 使充溢 / vi. 刺入, 看穿, 渗透, 打进
def: pass into or through, often by overcoming resistance
become clear or enter one's consciousness or emotions
penetrate.ety: From Latin penētrātus, perfect passive participle of penētrō (“to put, set, or place within, enter, pierce, penetrate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from penes (“within, with”) by analogy to intr

penitent.zh: a. 忏悔的, 悔悟的, 表示悔罪的 / n. 忏悔的人, 悔罪者
def: (Roman Catholic Church) a person who repents for wrongdoing (a Roman Catholic may be admitted to penance under the direction of a confessor)
feeling or expressing remorse for misdeeds
penitent.ety: From Middle English, from Old French, from Latin paenitēns, poenitēns (“penitent”), present participle of paeniteō, poeniteō (“to cause to repent; to regret, repent”). Doublet of penitente.

pensioner.zh: n. 领取抚恤金者, (英国剑桥大学的)自费生, 为金钱所收买的人, 帮佣 / [法] 领取退休金者, 领取抚恤金者
def: the beneficiary of a pension fund
Someone who lives on a pension, especially the retirement or old age pension.
Someone who is at the age at which one typically receives a pension; an elderly person.
pensioner.ety: From Middle English pensioner, from Anglo-Norman pensionner and Old French pensionnier, from Medieval Latin pēnsiōnārius. By surface analysis, pension + -er.

peptic.zh: a. 有助消化的, 胃液素的, 胃蛋白酶的 / n. 健胃剂, 促进消化物质
def: Of, pertaining to, capable of, or aiding digestion.
peptic.ety: From Latin pepticus, from Ancient Greek πέψις (pépsis, “digestion”), a form of πέσσω (péssō).

percentage.zh: n. 百分比, 比率, 部分, 可能性 / [计] 百分比
def: a proportion in relation to a whole (which is usually the amount per hundred)
assets belonging to or due to or contributed by an individual person or group
percentage.ety: From percent, from Latin per centum (“for every hundred”), + -age (suffix indicating a rate).

percussion.zh: n. 敲打, 碰撞, 叩击, 叩诊, 击发, 打击, 打击乐器组 / [医] 叩诊
def: the act of playing a percussion instrument
the act of exploding a percussion cap
the section of a band or orchestra that plays percussion instruments
percussion.ety: From Middle English percussioun, from Middle French, Old French percussion, from Latin percussiō (“striking”), from percutiō (“to strike”).

perfunctorily.zh: adv. 敷衍地, 马虎地, 潦草地, 表面地
def: in a set manner without serious attention
In a perfunctory manner, without interest or concern for quality.

perishable.zh: a. 易腐坏的, 会枯萎的, 易毁灭的, 不经久的 / n. 易腐坏的东西
def: food that will decay rapidly if not refrigerated
liable to perish; subject to destruction or death or decay
perishable.ety: From Middle English *persishable, perysabyl, equivalent to perish + -able. Compare Old French perissable (and modern French périssable).

performance.zh: n. 施行, 工作情况, 成绩, 行为, 表现, 演出 / [电] 绩效, 性能
def: the act of presenting a play or a piece of music or other entertainment
the act of performing; of doing something successfully; using knowledge as distinguished from merely possessing it
performance.ety: From Middle English parfourmaunce; equivalent to perform + -ance.

performer.zh: n. 表演者, 执行者, 完成者 / [法] 执行者, 履行者, 实行者
def: an entertainer who performs a dramatic or musical work for an audience
One who performs for, or entertains, an audience.
One who performs or does anything.

perilous.zh: a. 危险的, 濒临毁灭的
perilous.ety: From Middle English perilous, from Old French perilleus, equivalent to peril + -ous, from the noun peril, or from Latin perīculōsus. Doublet of periculous.

periodic.zh: a. 周期的, 定期的, 间歇(性)的, 循环的, 用完整句的, 高碘的 / [医] 周期性的
def: happening or recurring at regular intervals
recurring or reappearing from time to time
periodic.ety: From French périodique, from Medieval Latin periodicus (“cyclical”), from Latin periodus (“complete sentence, period, circuit”), from Ancient Greek περίοδος (períodos, “cycle, period of time”). By sur

perky.zh: a. 得意洋洋的, 快活的, 敏捷的, 美观的, 傲慢的, 神气的
def: Lively and often cheerful and enthusiastic.

permanence.zh: n. 永久, 持久, 固定性 / [法] 永久性, 持久性
def: the property of being able to exist for an indefinite duration
permanence.ety: From Middle English permanence, permanens, from Middle French permanence, from Medieval Latin permanentia, from Latin permaneō (“to remain; last”).

permanent.zh: a. 永久的, 不变的, 固定的, 持久的 / n. 烫发 / [计] 永久的
def: continuing or enduring without marked change in status or condition or place
a series of waves in the hair made by applying heat and chemicals
not capable of being reversed or returned to the original condition
permanent.ety: From Middle English permanent, permanente, from Middle French permanent, from Latin permanēns, from permaneō (“to stay through”). First attested in the 15th century.

permeable.zh: a. 有渗透性的, 能透过的 / [化] 渗透性的; 可渗透的
def: allowing fluids or gases to pass or diffuse through
Able to be permeated; absorbing or allowing the passage of fluids.
Allowing the passage of persons, information, or other things, especially when such passage occurs despite hopes or expectations otherwise.
permeable.ety: From Middle English permeable, permiable, from Latin permeābilis.

permeate.zh: vt. 弥漫, 渗透, 充满, 影响, 感染 / vi. 透入, 散布
permeate.ety: First attested in 1656; borrowed from Latin permeātus, perfect passive participle of permeō (“to pass through”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (noun-forming suffix).

permission.zh: n. 许可, 允许 / [计] 许可, 认可
def: the act of giving a formal (usually written) authorization
permission.ety: From Middle English permision, permission, permissioun, permyssion, from Middle French permission, from Latin permissiō. Equivalent to permit + -ion. Mostly replaced native English leave, from Old Eng

permissible.zh: a. 可允许的, 可容许程度的
def: that may be permitted especially as according to rule
that may be accepted or conceded
permissible.ety: From Middle English permyssyble, from Old French permissible, from Medieval Latin permissibilis.

permissive.zh: a. 许可的, 获准的, 宽容的, 放任的, 放纵的, 允许选择的, 自由的 / [法] 表示许可的, 随意的, 纵容的
def: granting or inclined or able to grant permission; not strict in discipline

perpetrator.zh: n. 作恶者, 犯罪者, 行凶者 / [法] 作恶者, 行凶者, 犯罪者
def: One who perpetrates; especially, one who commits an offence or crime.
perpetrator.ety: From Latin perpetrātor. By surface analysis, perpetrate + -or.

perpetual.zh: a. 永久的, 不断的, 无期限的, 没完没了的, 四季开花的 / [经] 永远的, 终身的, 持续的
def: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing
perpetual.ety: From Middle English perpetuel, from Old French perpetuel, from Latin perpetuālis (“universal”), from perpetuus, from petō.

perpetuate.zh: vt. 使永存, 使不朽, 保持
def: To make (something) perpetual; to make (something) continue for an indefinite time; also, to preserve (something) from extinction or oblivion.
To record (the testimony of a witness) which may be lost before a matter comes to trial.
perpetuate.ety: (16th century) From earlier perpetuat, learned borrowing from Latin perpetuātus (“perpetuated”), perfect passive participle of perpetuō (“to cause to continue uninterruptedly, to proceed with continua

perplexity.zh: n. 困惑, 混乱状态, 使人困惑的事物
def: trouble or confusion resulting from complexity
The state or quality of being perplexed.
perplexity.ety: From Middle English perplexite, borrowed from Middle French perplexité or post-classical Latin perplexitās, from perplexus (“entangled”). By surface analysis, perplex + -ity.

perseverance.zh: n. 毅力, 忍耐, 锲而不舍, 不屈不挠
def: the act of persisting or persevering; continuing or repeating behavior
perseverance.ety: From Middle English perseveraunce, from Old French perseverance, from Latin persevērantia.

persian.zh: n. 波斯人, 波斯语
def: a native or inhabitant of Iran
of or relating to Iran or its people or language or culture
the language of Persia (Iran) in any of its ancient forms
persian.ety: From Middle English Persien, from Middle French persien, from Italian persiano, from Medieval Latin Persiānus, from Persia (itself from Persēs/Persa (“Persian man”) [from Ancient Greek Πέρσης (Pérsēs)

personable.zh: a. 风度好的, 讨人喜欢的, 具有行为能力的
def: (of persons) pleasant in appearance and personality
Of a person: having a pleasing appearance; attractive; handsome.
Of a person: having a pleasant manner; amiable, friendly.
personable.ety: From Late Middle English personable, personabil (“having a pleasing appearance, handsome”), and then from both of the following: * For sense 1 (“having a pleasing appearance”) and sense 2 (“having a p

personage.zh: n. 重要人士, 显要, 名士, 人物, 角色
def: another word for person; a person not meriting identification
a person whose actions and opinions strongly influence the course of events
personage.ety: From Middle French personnage, from Old French personage; by surface analysis, person + -age (compare French suffix -age).

personal.zh: a. 私人的, 涉及隐私的, 有人性的, 人称的, 亲自的, 身体的 / [医] 人的; 个人的, 自身的
def: concerning or affecting a particular person or his or her private life and personality
personal.ety: From Middle English personal, personele, from Anglo-Norman personel, personal, personell, Old French personal, personel, from Late Latin persōnālis (“of a person, personly”), equivalent to person + -a

personify.zh: vt. 看做人, 赋与人性, 使人格化, 体现, 是...的化身
def: invest with or as with a body; give body to
represent, as of a character on stage

persuasion.zh: n. 说服, 信念, 派别, 说服力
def: the act of persuading (or attempting to persuade); communication intended to induce belief or action
a personal belief or judgment that is not founded on proof or certainty
persuasion.ety: From French persuasion and its source, Latin persuāsiō, from persuādēre, from suādēre (“to advise, recommend”).

persuasive.zh: a. 有说服力的, 劝诱的, 劝导性的
def: intended or having the power to induce action or belief
persuasive.ety: From Middle French persuasif, from Medieval Latin persuāsīvus, from Latin past participle stem of persuādēre + -īvus.

pertinent.zh: a. 相关的, 中肯的, 切题的 / [法] 恰当的, 有关的
def: having precise or logical relevance to the matter at hand
being of striking appropriateness and pertinence
pertinent.ety: Inherited from Middle English pertinent, borrowed from Old French pertinent and Latin pertinēns, pertinentem.

pervasive.zh: a. 普遍的, 流行的, 到处蔓延的, 到处渗透的
def: Manifested throughout; pervading, permeating, penetrating or affecting everything.
pervasive.ety: From Latin pervāsus, from pervādō (“spread through, pervade”), from per (“through”) + vādō (“go, walk”).

pessimism.zh: n. 悲观, 悲观情绪, 悲观主义 / [医] 悲观主义
def: the feeling that things will turn out badly
a general disposition to look on the dark side and to expect the worst in all things
pessimism.ety: From French pessimisme, from Latin pessimus (“worst”) + -ism, superlative of malus (“bad”). As a doctrine, from German Pessimismus as used by the German philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer in 1819.

pessimist.zh: n. 悲观者, 厌世者, 悲观主义者
def: a person who expects the worst
Someone who habitually expects the worst outcome; one who looks on the dark side of things.
pessimist.ety: From French pessimiste, from Latin pessimus (“worst”) + -ist.

pestilence.zh: n. 瘟疫, 散布毒害的事物, 罪恶 / [医] 疫病, 疫病流行
def: a serious (sometimes fatal) infection of rodents caused by Yersinia pestis and accidentally transmitted to humans by the bite of a flea that has bitten an infected animal
any epidemic disease with a high death rate
a pernicious and malign influence that is hard to get rid of
pestilence.ety: From Middle English, from Old French, from Latin pestilentia (“plague”), from pestilens (“infected, unwholesome, noxious”); equivalent to pestilent + -ence.

pestilent.zh: a. 致命的, 传染性的, 有害的, 伤风败俗的, 引起瘟疫的
def: likely to spread and cause an epidemic disease- Jonathan Swift
pestilent.ety: Middle English, from Latin pestilens, from Latin pestis.

petitioner.zh: n. 请愿人, 诉愿人, (离婚案)原告 / [法] 诉愿人, 上诉人, 请愿人
def: someone who petitions a court for redress of a grievance or recovery of a right

petrify.zh: vt. (非正式)使惊呆, 使吓得要死, 使发呆 / vt.vi. 使石化, 使成为化石, 使变僵, 变僵硬, 使消失活力, 使僵化
def: cause to become stonelike or stiff or dazed and stunned
make rigid and set into a conventional pattern
petrify.ety: From Middle French pétrifier, from Medieval Latin petrificāre, from Latin petra (“rock”), from Ancient Greek πέτρα (pétra, “rock”) + -ficāre, from facere (“do, make”), equivalent to petro- + -ify.

def: a dark oil consisting mainly of hydrocarbons
A flammable liquid ranging in color from clear to very dark brown and black, consisting mainly of hydrocarbons, occurring naturally in deposits under the Earth's surface.
An unincorporated community in Nottingham Township, Wells County, Indiana.
petroleum.ety: Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin petroleum. Doublet of petrol.

peaceful.zh: a. 平静的, 和平的, 和平时期的, 爱好和平的, 喜爱安静的 / [法] 和平的, 爱好和平的, 和平时期的
def: not disturbed by strife or turmoil or war
peacefully resistant in response to injustice
peaceful.ety: Derived from the derogatory term religion of peace, which is used against Islam itself for its association with violent attacks by Islamic extremists, and alleged support and lack of condemnation agai

peaky.zh: a. 有峰的, 多峰的, 尖的, 消瘦的
def: having or as if having especially high-pitched spots

peculiarity.zh: n. 特质, 特性, 怪癖
def: something unusual -- perhaps worthy of collecting

pedagogic.zh: a. 教育学的, 教授法的, 小学教师的
pedagogic.ety: First attested in 1781. From French pédagogique, from Latin paedagōgicus, pēdagōgicus, from Ancient Greek παιδαγωγικός (paidagōgikós), from παιδαγωγός (paidagōgós, “teacher, tutor”), from παῖς (paîs,

pedagogy.zh: n. 教育学, 教授法, 教学工作
def: the principles and methods of instruction
the activities of educating or instructing; activities that impart knowledge or skill
pedagogy.ety: From Middle French pédagogie, from Ancient Greek παιδαγωγία (paidagōgía). By surface analysis, ped- (“child”) + -agogy.

pedal.zh: n. 踏板, 脚蹬子 / a. 脚的, 脚踏的 / vt. 用脚踏动
def: of or relating to the feet
pedal.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin pedālis. Cognate with French pédal (doublet of the pédale mentioned in § Etymology 1). Same surface analysis as in § Etymology 1.

pedantic.zh: a. 卖弄学问的, 学究式的, 假装学者的
def: marked by a narrow focus on or display of learning especially its trivial aspects
Being overly concerned with formal rules and trivial points of learning, like a pedant.
Tending to show off one’s knowledge, often in a tiresome manner.

penetration.zh: n. 穿透, 渗透, 侵入, 识穿, 洞察(力) / [化] 渗入
def: an attack that penetrates into enemy territory
clear or deep perception of a situation
the act of entering into or through something
penetration.ety: From Middle English penetracioun, from Old French penetracïon, and its source, Latin penetrātiō, from the participle stem of penetrō (“pierce”, verb). Morphologically penetrate + -ion.

percussionist.zh: n. 敲击乐器演奏者, 敲奏打击乐器的人
def: a musician who plays percussion instruments
A trained musician who plays percussion instruments, as opposed to a drummer who lacks formal training.

periodical.zh: n. 期刊 / a. 定期出版的, (有关)期刊的, 间歇(性的), 周期的, 定期的
def: a publication that appears at fixed intervals
happening or recurring at regular intervals

permanently.zh: adv. 永久, 不变, 持久 / [计] 永久性的

retrenchment.ety: Probably partly from both of the following: * Middle French retrenchement, retranchement (“removal of a portion from a larger whole; reduction of expenses”) (modern French retranchement (“deduction, s

regressive.zh: a. 后退的, 退化的, 回归的 / [医] 退化的, 退行的, 消退的, 回归的
def: (of taxes) adjusted so that the rate decreases as the amount of income increases
opposing progress; returning to a former less advanced state
regressive.ety: Borrowed from Latin regressīvus, equivalent to regress + -ive.

repairable.zh: a. 可修理的, 可赔偿的, 可挽回的

reportage.zh: n. 新闻报道, 报告文学
def: the news as presented by reporters for newspapers or radio or television
The reporting of news, especially by an eyewitness.
News or information that has been reported; media coverage of a topic or event.
a communal dining-hall (usually in a monastery)
A dining hall, especially in an institution such as a college or monastery.
refectory.ety: Via Middle English refectori from Late Latin refectorium, from Latin reficere (“to remake, to rebuild”).

retention.zh: n. 保持, 留置, 保留, 保持力, 保留物, 记忆, 停滞, 固位 / [计] 保贸, 保持
def: the power of retaining and recalling past experience
retention.ety: From Middle English retencioun, borrowed from Latin retentiō, retentiōnis, from retentus, the perfect passive participle of retineō (“retain”) (from re- (“back, again”) + teneō (“hold, keep”)).

retentive.zh: a. 保持的, 有保持力的, 记性好的
def: having the capacity to retain something
having the power, capacity, or quality of retaining water
retentive.ety: Borrowed from Middle French rétentif, from Old French retentif, from Medieval Latin retentivus, from Latin retentus.

retroactive.zh: a. 反动的, 追溯的, 有追溯效力的 / [经] 有追溯效力的
def: descriptive of any event or stimulus or process that has an effect on the effects of events or stimuli or process that occurred previously
retroactive.ety: First attested in 1610. From French rétroactif, equivalent to retro- + active.

retrospection.zh: n. 回顾, 追忆, 反省 / [医] 追想, 回忆
def: memory for experiences that are past

retrospective.zh: a. 回顾的, 怀旧的, 在后面的 / n. 回顾展
def: an exhibition of a representative selection of an artist's life work
concerned with or related to the past
retrospective.ety: From retrospect + -ive. From Latin retrōspectus, perfect passive participle of retrōspiciō (“to look back at”).

reunion.zh: n. 团圆, 重聚 / [医] 再连合, 复连[合]
def: a party of former associates who have come together again
the act of coming together again
reunion.ety: From Middle French reunion (modern French réunion). By surface analysis, re- + union. Doublet of Réunion.

def: unify again, as of a country

reversal.zh: n. 翻转, 颠倒, 反转 / [医] 逆转, 颠倒
def: a change from one state to the opposite state
an unfortunate happening that hinders or impedes; something that is thwarting or frustrating
turning in an opposite direction or position
reversal.ety: Borrowed from French réversal or Medieval Latin reversālis. By surface analysis, reverse + -al.

reversible.zh: a. 可逆的, 可撤消的 / n. 双面可用织物
def: capable of reversing or being reversed
a garment (especially a coat) that can be worn inside out (with either side of the cloth showing)
capable of being reversed or used with either side out
reversible.ety: Probably from Middle French, equivalent to reverse + -ible.

reversion.zh: n. 回复, 复原, 归还, 继承权 / [化] 返硫
def: (law) an interest in an estate that reverts to the grantor (or his heirs) at the end of some period (e.g., the death of the grantee)
(genetics) a return to a normal phenotype (usually resulting from a second mutation)
a reappearance of an earlier characteristic
reversion.ety: Borrowed into late Middle English from Old French reversion (modern réversion), from Latin reversio, from revertō. By surface analysis, revert + -sion.

reviewer.zh: n. 评论者, 书评作者, 评论家, 剧评家, 报刊评论家
def: someone who reads manuscripts and judges their suitability for publication
a writer who reports and analyzes events of the day

revision.zh: n. 校订, 修正, 修订本, 修订版 / [计] 修订版
def: the act of revising or altering (involving reconsideration and modification)
something that has been written again
revision.ety: Borrowed from French révision, from Latin revīsiō.

revitalize.zh: vt. 使恢复生气, 使复活, 使复兴
def: give new life or vigor to

revival.zh: n. 复兴, 复活, 恢复精神, 苏醒 / [医] 复苏, 回生, 精神重振
def: bringing again into activity and prominence
an evangelistic meeting intended to reawaken interest in religion

revivify.zh: v. (使)再生, (使)复活, (使)振奋精神
def: give new life or energy to
To reanimate, bring back to life.
revivify.ety: Partly from French revivifier and partly from Latin revīvificō, corresponding to re- + vivify.

revolution.zh: n. 革命, 大变革, 旋转, 转数, 循环 / [化] 回转
def: a drastic and far-reaching change in ways of thinking and behaving
the overthrow of a government by those who are governed
a single complete turn (axial or orbital)
revolution.ety: Inherited from Middle English revolucion, borrowed from Old French revolucion, from Late Latin revolūtiō (“the act of revolving; revolution”), from Latin revolvō (“roll back, revolve”).

revolver.zh: n. 左轮手枪 / [化] 旋转炉
def: a pistol with a revolving cylinder (usually having six chambers for bullets)
a door consisting of four orthogonal partitions that rotate about a central pivot; a door designed to equalize the air pressure in tall buildings
revolver.ety: From revolve + -er, coined by American inventor Samuel Colt in 1835.

reparable.zh: a. 可修缮的, 可赔偿的, 可补偿的 / [法] 可修补的, 可补救的, 可纠正的
def: capable of being repaired or rectified
reparable.ety: From Middle French réparable, from Latin reparābilis.

reparation.zh: n. 补偿, 赔偿, 弥补, 修复, 修理 / [经] 赔偿, 补偿, 修理
def: compensation (given or received) for an insult or injury
(usually plural) compensation exacted from a defeated nation by the victors
the act of putting something in working order again

repatriate.zh: vt. 把...遣返 / vi. 回国 / n. 被遣返回国者
def: a person who has returned to the country of origin or whose citizenship has been restored
send someone back to his homeland against his will, as of refugees
repatriate.ety: Borrowed from Latin repatriare, from re- + patria (“homeland”). Cognate to repair (“to return”).

repayment.zh: n. 付还, 偿还, 报复, 付还的钱 / [经] 偿还, 付还
def: the act of returning money received previously
payment of a debt or obligation
repayment.ety: From repay + -ment, also equivalent to re- + payment.

repercussion.zh: n. 弹回, 反响, 反射 / [医] 消退[法], 消肿[法], 浮动诊胎法
def: a remote or indirect consequence of some action
a movement back from an impact
repercussion.ety: From Middle French répercussion, from Latin repercussio (“rebounding; repercussion”), from repercutio (“cause to rebound, reflect, strike against”), from re- + percutio (“beat, strike”), from per- (“t

replacement.zh: n. 归还, 更换, 代替者 / [医] 复位, 置换
def: the act of furnishing an equivalent person or thing in the place of another
someone who takes the place of another person
an event in which one thing is substituted for another

replenish.zh: vt. 把...重新补足, 把...再装满 / vi. 被再装满, 充满
def: fill something that had previously been emptied
To refill; to renew; to supply again or to add a fresh quantity to.
To fill up; to complete; to supply fully.
replenish.ety: From Middle English replenisshen, borrowed from Old French repleniss-, stem of some of the conjugated forms of replenir, from re- + plenir, from plein, from Latin plenus.

replica.zh: n. 复制品 / [计] 目录分区复制
def: copy that is not the original; something that has been copied
A copy made at a smaller scale than the original.
replica.ety: Borrowed from Italian replica, derived from Latin replicare (“to fold or bend back; to reply”). Doublet of reply and replicate.

replicate.zh: vt. 折叠, 折转, 复制 / n. 复现试验, 复制品, 高八度音 / a. 复现的, 复制的, 折转的, 弯回的
def: reproduce or make an exact copy of
make or do or perform again
replicate.ety: From Latin replicātus, past participle of replicāre (“to fold or bend back; reply”), from re (“back”) + plicāre (“to fold”); see ply. Doublet of reply and replica.

reporter.zh: n. 记者, 报告者 / [化] 指示器
def: a person who investigates and reports or edits news stories
A journalist who investigates, edits and reports news stories for newspapers, radio and television.
reporter.ety: From Middle English reportour, from Old French reporteur; equivalent to report + -er.

repository.zh: n. 贮藏所, 贮物器, 仓库, 博物馆, 店铺, 陈列室, 资源丰富地区, 墓地, 亲信, 知己 / [经] 仓库, 栈房, 贮藏所
def: a facility where things can be deposited for storage or safekeeping
a person to whom a secret is entrusted
a burial vault (usually for some famous person)
repository.ety: From reposit or its etymon Classical Latin reposit-, past participial stem of repōnō, + -ory. Compare Medieval Latin repositōrius (“used for storage”).

reprehensible.zh: a. 应斥责的, 应该谴责的 / [法] 应受严责的, 应受指责的, 应受申斥的
def: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
reprehensible.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin reprehensibilis, from Latin reprehendo; equivalent to reprehend + -ible.

repression.zh: n. 抑制, 压抑, 制止 / [医] 压抑, 抑制
def: (psychiatry) the classical defense mechanism that protects you from impulses or ideas that would cause anxiety by preventing them from becoming conscious
the act of repressing; control by holding down

repressive.zh: a. 压抑的, 抑制的, 镇压的
def: Serving to repress or suppress; oppressive

repulsion.zh: n. 击退, 排斥力, 反感 / [医] 排斥, 斥力
def: the force by which bodies repel one another
the act of repulsing or repelling an attack; a successful defensive stand
repulsion.ety: Borrowed from Middle French répulsion, from Late Latin repulsio, repulsionem, from Latin repulsus.

repulsive.zh: a. 排斥的, 可恶的, 击退的
def: so extremely ugly as to be terrifying
repulsive.ety: Borrowed from Middle French repulsif, from Medieval Latin repulsivus, from Latin repulsus. By surface analysis, repuls(e) + -ive. Compare typologically Polish odpychający (< pchnąć), Russian отта́лкив

requirement.zh: n. 需求, 必要条件, 要求 / [化] 要求; 合同要求
def: something that is required in advance

requisition.zh: n. 正式请求, 申请, 需要, 征用, 通知单, 申请书, 引渡要求 / vt. 征用, 要求
def: make a formal request for official services
the act of requiring; an authoritative request or demand, especially by a military or public authority that takes something over (usually temporarily) for military or public use
an official form on which a request in made
requisition.ety: From Middle English requisicion, from Old French requisicion, from Medieval Latin requisitio. By surface analysis, requisit(e) + -ion.

def: a scientist who devotes himself to doing research

resemblance.zh: n. 相似处, 类似, 肖像
def: similarity in appearance or external or superficial details
The quality or state of resembling.
That which resembles, or is similar; a representation; a likeness.
resemblance.ety: From Anglo-Norman resemblance, from Old French (compare French ressemblance). Morphologically resemble + -ance.

resistance.zh: n. 抵抗力, 反抗, 耐力, 阻力, 电阻 / [化] 抵抗; 抗性; 阻力; 抗药性; 电阻
def: the action of opposing something that you disapprove or disagree with
any mechanical force that tends to retard or oppose motion
a material's opposition to the flow of electric current; measured in ohms
resistance.ety: From earlier resistence, from Middle English resistence, from Old French resistence, from Latin resistentia. Morphologically resist + -ance.

resistant.zh: n. 抵抗者, 反抗者 / a. 抵抗的, 反抗的, 耐...的
def: relating to or conferring immunity (to disease or infection)
able to tolerate environmental conditions or physiological stress
resistant.ety: From French résistant; equivalent to resist + -ant.

resistor.zh: n. 电阻器 / [化] 电阻器
def: an electrical device that resists the flow of electrical current
One who resists, especially a person who fights against an occupying army.
An electric component that transmits current in direct proportion to the voltage across it.

resonance.zh: n. 共鸣, 回声, 反响, 谐振, 共振 / [化] 共振; 共鸣
def: an excited state of a stable particle causing a sharp maximum in the probability of absorption of electromagnetic radiation
a vibration of large amplitude produced by a relatively small vibration near the same frequency of vibration as the natural frequency of the resonating system
having the character of a loud deep sound; the quality of being resonant
resonance.ety: From Old French resonance (French résonance), from Latin resonantia (“echo”), from resonō (“to resound”).

resonant.zh: a. 共鸣的, 反响的, 洪亮的, 共振的 / [医] 反响的, 叩响的, 共鸣的, 共振的
def: serving to bring to mind- Wilder Hobson
resonant.ety: Borrowed from French résonnant or Latin resonantem.

respiration.zh: n. 呼吸, 一口气, 呼吸作用 / [化] 呼吸
def: the metabolic processes whereby certain organisms obtain energy from organic molecules; processes that take place in the cells and tissues during which energy is released and carbon dioxide…
a single complete act of breathing in and out
the bodily process of inhalation and exhalation; the process of taking in oxygen from inhaled air and releasing carbon dioxide by exhalation
respiration.ety: From Middle English respiracioun, borrowed from Latin respīrātiō, respīrātiōnem.

restrictive.zh: a. 限制的, 约束的, 限定的 / n. 限制词
def: (of tariff) protective of national interests by restricting imports
restrictive.ety: From Middle French restrictif. Morphologically restrict + -ive.

restitution.zh: n. 归还, 偿还, 赔偿 / [医] 整复, 恢复, 转回(胎头)
def: a sum of money paid in compensation for loss or injury
the act of restoring something to its original state
restitution.ety: From Old French restitucion, from Latin restitutio. By surface analysis, restitute + -ion.

restraint.zh: n. 抑制, 克制, 束缚 / [医] 约束, 拘束
def: the act of controlling by restraining someone or something
discipline in personal and social activities
the state of being physically constrained
restraint.ety: From Middle English restreynte, from Old French restreinte; more at restrain.

restriction.zh: n. 限制, 限定, 约束 / [计] 限定
def: a principle that limits the extent of something
an act of limiting or restricting (as by regulation)
the act of keeping something within specified bounds (by force if necessary)
restriction.ety: From Middle English restriccioun, from Anglo-Norman restriction, Middle French restriction, and their source, Late Latin restrictiō, from Latin restringō. Morphologically restrict + -ion.

resumption.zh: n. 取回, 恢复, 再开始 / [经] 再取回, 恢复, 重新占用
def: The act of resuming or starting something again.
resumption.ety: From re- + Latin sūmptus + -ion, from past participle of sūmō (“to take”).

resurrection.zh: n. 复活, 复兴, 恢复, 掘墓盗尸 / [法] 复活, 恢复, 修复
def: (New Testament) the rising of Christ on the third day after the Crucifixion
a revival from inactivity and disuse
resurrection.ety: From Middle English resurreccioun, resurrection, from Anglo-Norman resurrectiun, Old French resurrection (French: résurrection), and their etymon Late Latin resurrēctiōnem (accusative of resurrēctiō)

retainer.zh: n. 家臣, 侍从, 保持者 / [化] 保持器; 定位器; 隔栅; 隔环; 护圈; 止动器; 止动装置
def: a fee charged in advance to retain the services of someone
a person working in the service of another (especially in the household)
a dental appliance that holds teeth (or a prosthesis) in position after orthodontic treatment

refusal.zh: n. 拒绝, 推却, 优先决定权 / [法] 拒绝, 谢绝, 取舍权
def: a message refusing to accept something that is offered
refusal.ety: Inherited from Middle English refusell. By surface analysis, refuse + -al.

regenerate.zh: vt. 使再生, 重建, 革新 / vi. 新生, 再生 / a. 新生的, 再生的
def: reestablish on a new, usually improved, basis or make new or like new
amplify (an electron current) by causing part of the power in the output circuit to act upon the input circuit
regenerate.ety: From Latin regenerātus, perfect passive participle of regenerō, from re- + generō, from genus, generis (“descent, origin, birth”); -ō, equivalent to re- + generate.

regression.zh: n. 退步, 回归 / [计] 回归
def: an abnormal state in which development has stopped prematurely
(psychiatry) a defense mechanism in which you flee from reality by assuming a more infantile state
the relation between selected values of x and observed values of y (from which the most probable value of y can be predicted for any value of x)
regression.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin regressio. Equivalent to regress + -ion. The statistics sense comes from regression to the mean.

rehabilitation.zh: n. 复原 / [医] 复原, 恢复, 康复
def: the restoration of someone to a useful place in society
the conversion of wasteland into land suitable for use of habitation or cultivation
vindication of a person's character and the re-establishment of that person's reputation
rehabilitation.ety: From Middle French réhabilitation, from Medieval Latin rehabilitatio.

rejection.zh: n. 拒绝, 抛弃, 驳回, 被抛弃的东西, 呕出物 / [化] 报废; 拒收
def: (medicine) an immunological response that refuses to accept substances or organisms that are recognized as foreign
rejection.ety: From French réjection or directly from Latin reiectiōnem, accusative of Latin reiectiō. Displaced native Old English āworpennes (literally “thrown-out-ness”).

rejuvenate.zh: vt. 使年轻, 使复原, 使恢复精神 / vi. 返老还童, 复原
def: cause (a stream or river) to erode, as by an uplift of the land
rejuvenate.ety: From re- (“again”) + Latin iuvenis (“young”) + -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare Old French rejuvener. Displaced native Middle English gingen, from Old English *ġinġan (literally “to make young”), e

reminder.zh: n. 提醒的人, 暗示 / [经] 催单
def: a message that helps you remember something
an experience that causes you to remember something
someone who gives a warning so that a mistake can be avoided

remonstrance.zh: n. 抗议, 忠告, 规劝 / [法] 抗议, 抗辩, 规劝
def: the act of expressing earnest opposition or protest
A remonstration; disapproval; a formal, usually written, objection or protest.

remonstrate.zh: vi. 表示异议, 抗议, 责备 / vt. 抗议地说
def: present and urge reasons in opposition
remonstrate.ety: From (the participle stem of) Late Latin remōnstrō, from Latin re- + mōnstrō.

removable.zh: a. 可移去的, 可免职的, 可移动的 / [电] 可移动的
def: capable of being removed or taken away or dismissed

removal.zh: n. 移动, 移居, 迁移, 排除, 切除 / [医] 切除, 除去

remuneration.zh: n. 报酬 / [经] 报酬, 酬劳
def: the act of paying for goods or services or to recompense for losses

remunerative.zh: a. 有报酬的, 有利可图的, 合算的

renewable.zh: a. 可更新的, 可恢复的, 可继续的, 可换新的, 可重复的, 可重说的 / [计] 可更新, 可再生的
def: that can be renewed or extended

renewal.zh: n. 更新, 革新, 复兴, 恢复, 修补, 补充, 继续, 重订, 重申, 续借 / [经] 更新, 换新, 重申
def: the conversion of wasteland into land suitable for use of habitation or cultivation
filling again by supplying what has been used up

rearmament.zh: n. 重整军备, 改良装备
rearmament.ety: From re- + armament. Compare French réarmement.

recantation.zh: n. 放弃信仰, 改变论调
def: a disavowal or taking back of a previous assertion
The act of recanting or something recanted.

recapture.zh: n. 取回, 夺回 / vt. 再捕获, 夺回, 重温
def: a legal seizure by the government of profits beyond a fixed amount

receiver.zh: n. 接收器；接受者；收信机；收款员, 接待者
def: set that receives radio or tv signals
(law) a person (usually appointed by a court of law) who liquidates assets or preserves them for the benefit of affected parties
earphone that converts electrical signals into sounds
receiver.ety: Inherited from Middle English receyvour, from Anglo-Norman receverre, receivour et al., later also reformed as receive + -er. Compare recevor, rescaivour.

receptacle.zh: n. 容器, 花托, 插座 / [医] 容器, [接]受器, 花托
def: a container that is used to put or keep things in
enlarged tip of a stem that bears the floral parts
an electrical (or electronic) fitting that is connected to a source of power and equipped to receive an insert
receptacle.ety: From Middle English receptacle, from Anglo-Norman receptacle and Middle French receptacle (“organ containing a fluid; gathering place; water basin”) (modern French réceptacle), from Latin receptāculum

reception.zh: n. 接待, 接受, 招待会 / [医] 接受, 感受
def: the manner in which something is greeted
a formal party of people; as after a wedding
quality or fidelity of a received broadcast
reception.ety: From Middle English recepcion, reception, from Middle French reception, from Latin receptiōn- (“the act of receiving; reception”), from recipiō (“receive”), from re- (“back”) + capiō (“to hold”). Equi

receptive.zh: a. 能接纳的 / [医] 接受的, 感受的
def: open to arguments, ideas, or change
ready or willing to receive favorably
of a nerve fiber or impulse originating outside and passing toward the central nervous system
receptive.ety: From Late Middle English receptive, receptyue (“capable of receiving something; acting as a receptacle”), borrowed from Medieval Latin receptivus (“capable of receiving something”), from Latin receptu

recession.zh: n. 后退, 凹处, 衰退, 归还 / [医] 退缩
def: the state of the economy declines; a widespread decline in the GDP and employment and trade lasting from six months to a year
the withdrawal of the clergy and choir from the chancel to the vestry at the end of a church service
recession.ety: Borrowed from Latin recessiō, from recēdō (“recede, retreat”), from re- (“back”) + cēdō (“to go”). By surface analysis, recess + -ion.

recessive.zh: a. 后退的, 逆行的, 隐性的 / n. 隐性性状
def: an allele that produces its characteristic phenotype only when its paired allele is identical
of or pertaining to a recession
(of genes) producing its characteristic phenotype only when its allele is identical
recessive.ety: From Latin recēdō + -ive, or directly from New Latin recessīvus.

recital.zh: n. 背诵, 吟诵, 详述 / [法] 叙述, 评述, 列举
def: the act of giving an account describing incidents or a course of events
performance of music or dance especially by soloists
a public instance of reciting or repeating (from memory) something prepared in advance

recitation.zh: n. 详述, 吟诵, 背诵的诗 / [法] 叙述, 评述, 书面陈述
def: written matter that is recited from memory
a public instance of reciting or repeating (from memory) something prepared in advance
a regularly scheduled session as part of a course of study
recitation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French récitation, from Latin recitatio, equivalent to recite + -ation.

reclamation.zh: n. 开垦, 教化 / [经] 经济上的复原再造
def: the conversion of wasteland into land suitable for use of habitation or cultivation
rescuing from error and returning to a rightful course
the recovery of useful substances from waste products
reclamation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French réclamation, from Latin reclamatio. Equivalent to reclaim + -ation.

recognition.zh: n. 赞誉, 认得, 识别, 承认, 认可, 认识 / [电] 认识
def: the state or quality of being recognized or acknowledged
the process of recognizing something or someone by remembering
recognition.ety: Inherited from Middle English recognicion, from Middle French recognicion, recognition and its etymon Latin recognitiōnem (accusative of recognitiō), from recognitus, past participle of recognōscere.

imaginary.zh: a. 想像的, 虚构的, 假想的
def: not based on fact; unreal- F.D.Roosevelt
(mathematics) a number of the form a+bi where a and b are real numbers and i is the square root of -1
imaginary.ety: From Middle English ymaginarie, ymagynary, from Latin imāginārius (“relating to images, fancied”), from imāgō, equivalent to imagine + -ary. The mathematical sense derives from René Descartes's use (o

imagination.zh: n. 想像, 听觉, 想像力 / [医] 想像
def: the formation of a mental image of something that is not perceived as real and is not present to the senses
the ability to form mental images of things or events
the ability to deal resourcefully with unusual problems
imagination.ety: From Middle English ymaginacioun, from Old French imaginacion, ymaginacion, from Latin imāginātiō. Equivalent to imagine + -ation.

imaginative.zh: a. 想像的, 虚构的
def: (used of persons or artifacts) marked by independence and creativity in thought or action- Lewis Mumford
Having a lively or creative imagination.
Tending to be fanciful or inventive.
imaginative.ety: From Middle English ymagynatif, from Middle French imaginatif, from Medieval Latin imāginātīvus. By surface analysis, imagine + -ative.

imbecility.zh: n. 低能, 愚钝, 愚蠢言行 / [医] 痴愚, 愚钝
def: retardation more severe than a moron but not as severe as an idiot
imbecility.ety: From Middle English inbecillite, from Middle French imbecilité, imbecillité, and its etymon Classical Latin imbēcillitās. By surface analysis, imbecile + -ity.

imitate.zh: vt. 模仿, 效法, 冒充, 仿造
def: appear like, as in behavior or appearance
make a reproduction or copy of
imitate.ety: Borrowed from Latin imitātus, perfect active participle of imitor (“to copy, portray, imitate”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix). Cognate with French imiter.

imperialism.zh: n. 帝国主义, 帝制 / [法] 帝国主义
def: a policy of extending your rule over foreign countries
a political orientation that advocates imperial interests
any instance of aggressive extension of authority

imperialist.zh: n. 帝国主义者, 皇帝统治的拥护者, 皇帝派的人 / a. 帝国主义的

imitation.zh: n. 模仿, 效法, 冒充, 赝品 / [医] 模仿, 仿制, 仿制品
def: the doctrine that representations of nature or human behavior should be accurate imitations
something copied or derived from an original
copying (or trying to copy) the actions of someone else
imitation.ety: From Middle English imitacioun, from Middle French imitacion, from Old French imitacion, from Latin imitatio.

imitative.zh: a. 喜模仿的, 伪造的, 仿制的, 摹拟的
def: marked by or given to imitation
(of words) formed in imitation of a natural sound- Harry Hoijer

impolitic.zh: a. 失策的, 不得当的
def: Not in accordance with good policy.

impugn.zh: vt. 责难, 抨击, 攻击 / [法] 驳斥, 指责, 非难
def: To verbally assault, especially to argue against an opinion, motive, or action; to question the truth or validity of; cast doubt on.
impugn.ety: Borrowed from Middle French impugner, from Latin impugnō, from im- + pugnō (“fight”), from pugnus (“fist”), as in English pugilism (“fighting with fists, boxing”).

immerse.zh: vt. 沉浸, 使陷入 / [医] 浸[入]
def: enclose or envelop completely, as if by swallowing
immerse.ety: Borrowed from Latin immersus, from immergō, from in + mergō.

immobile.zh: a. 不动的, 不变的, 固定的, 静止的
def: not capable of movement or of being moved
immobile.ety: From Old French immobile, from Latin immōbilis, equivalent to im- + mobile.

impend.zh: vi. 迫近, 威胁, 悬挂
def: be imminent or about to happen
To hang or be suspended over (something); to overhang.
To hang over (someone) as a threat or danger.
impend.ety: Borrowed from Latin impendere (“to hang over, to weigh out”), 1590s.

immoral.zh: a. 不道德的, 邪恶的, 放荡的 / [法] 不道德的, 道德败坏的, 邪恶的
def: deliberately violating accepted principles of right and wrong
not adhering to ethical or moral principles

impair.zh: vt. 损害, 减少, 削弱 / [法] 损害, 伤害, 减少
impair.ety: From Middle English impairen, empeiren, from Old French empeirier, from Early Medieval Latin impeiōrāre, from in- + Late Latin peiōrāre (“worsen”), from peiōrem (“worse”), comparative of malus (“bad”)

impale.zh: vt. 刺穿, 使绝望, 钉住
def: pierce with a sharp stake or point
kill by piercing with a spear or sharp pole
impale.ety: From Middle French, from Medieval Latin impālāre, from Latin palus, whence also pale.

impart.zh: vt. 给予, 传授, 告知
def: transmit or serve as the medium for transmission
impart.ety: From Middle English imparten, borrowed from Middle French impartir, empartir, from Late Latin impartiō, impertiō, from im- (“in”) + Latin partiō (“divide”).

impassive.zh: a. 无感情的, 冷淡的, 无感觉的, 不能伤害的
def: having or revealing little emotion or sensibility; not easily aroused or excited- Nordhoff & Hall-Virginia Woolf
impassive.ety: From im- (prefix meaning ‘not’) + passive (“which is, or is capable of being, acted on; (obsolete) which suffers, or may suffer, pain, death, etc.”, adjective).

impatience.zh: n. 性急, 难耐, 焦急, 急躁
def: a lack of patience; irritation with anything that causes delay
a restless desire for change and excitement
a dislike of anything that causes delay
impatience.ety: Inherited from Middle English impacience, from Old French impacience (modern French impatience), from Latin impatientia. By surface analysis, im- + patience.

impatient.zh: a. 不耐烦的, 着急的, 急切的
def: restless or short-tempered under delay or opposition
impatient.ety: From Old French impacient (modern French impatient), from Latin impatiēns. By surface analysis, im- + patient.

impecunious.zh: a. 没有钱的, 身无分文的, 贫穷的
def: not having enough money to pay for necessities
impecunious.ety: From im- + pecunious, from Latin pecūniōsus, from pecūnia (“money”) + -ōsus (“full of”).

impede.zh: vt. 妨碍, 阻碍, 阻止
def: be a hindrance or obstacle to
impede.ety: Borrowed from Latin impediō (“to shackle”), from pēs (“foot”) (compare pedestrian). First attested use as a verb was in William Shakespeare's Macbeth, see quotations.

imperil.zh: vt. 使处于危险, 危害
def: pose a threat to; present a danger to
To put into peril; to place in danger.

impervious.zh: a. 透不过的, 不易损坏的, 无动于衷的, 不受影响的 / [医] 不能透过的
def: not admitting of passage or capable of being affected
Unaffected or unable to be affected by something.
Preventive of any penetration; impenetrable, impermeable, particularly of water.
impervious.ety: From Latin impervius (“that cannot be passed through”), from in- (“not”) + pervius (“letting things through”).

impious.zh: a. 无信仰的, 不敬神的, 不虔诚的, 不孝的
def: lacking piety or reverence for a god

implant.zh: vt. 深植, 灌输, 嵌入 / n. 植入物, 植入管
def: fix or set securely or deeply
a prosthesis placed permanently in tissue
become attached to and embedded in the uterus
implant.ety: From Middle French implanter, from Latin implantō. By surface analysis, im- + plant.

implement.zh: n. 工具, 器具, 手段 / vt. 实现, 使生效, 执行
def: apply in a manner consistent with its purpose or design
instrumentation (a piece of equipment or tool) used to effect an end
ensure observance of laws and rules;
implement.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin implēmentum (“a filling up”), from Latin impleō (“to fill up”).

implode.zh: vi. 内爆, 向内破裂, 爆裂 / [电] 内裂
def: To collapse or burst inward violently.
To suddenly lose support in all areas of a campaign simultaneously.
To beg or plead for (something) earnestly or urgently; to beseech.
To beg or plead that (someone) earnestly or urgently do something; to beseech, to entreat.
implore.ety: PIE word *h₁én The verb is borrowed from Middle French implorer (modern French implorer (“to beg, plead, implore”)), or directly from its etymon Latin implōrāre, the present active infinitive of implō

impolite.zh: a. 无礼的, 粗鲁的
def: Not polite; discourteous; not of polished manners; wanting in good manners.
impolite.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin impolītus. Equivalent to im- + polite.

import.zh: n. 进口货, 进口, 输入, 含义, 重要性 / vt. 输入, 引入, 进口, 含...的意思, 重要 / vi. 有关系
def: commodities (goods or services) bought from a foreign country
an imported person brought from a foreign country
import.ety: From Middle English importen, from Old French emporter, importer, from Latin importō (“bring in from abroad, import”, verb), from in (“in, at, on; into”) + portō (“to carry, bear; convey”).

impose.zh: vt. 征(税), 把...强加于, 以...欺骗 / vi. 利用, 欺骗, 施加影响
def: compel to behave in a certain way
impose.ety: The verb is derived from Late Middle English imposen (“to place, set; to impose (a duty, etc.)”), borrowed from Middle French imposer, and Old French emposer, enposer (“to impose (a duty, tax, etc.)”)

impossible.zh: a. 不可能的, 难以置信的, 令人无法忍受的
def: not capable of occurring or being accomplished or dealt with
impossible.ety: From Middle English impossible, equivalent to im- + possible.

impotence.zh: n. 无力, 虚弱, 无效, 阳萎 / [医] 阳萎, 无能力
def: the quality of lacking strength or power; being weak and feeble
an inability (usually of the male animal) to copulate
impotence.ety: From Middle French impotence, from Latin impotentia.

impound.zh: vt. 关在栏中, 拘留, 充公 / [经] 扣押
def: take temporary possession of as a security, by legal authority
place or shut up in a pound

imprecise.zh: a. 不严密的, 不精确的, 不明确的
def: Not precise or exact; containing some error or uncertainty.

improper.zh: a. 不合适的, 错误的, 不成体统的, 不道德的 / [法] 不适当的, 不合适的, 不正确的
def: not suitable or right or appropriate
not conforming to legality, moral law, or social convention
not appropriate for a purpose or occasion
improper.ety: From Middle English empropren, perhaps from an unattested Anglo-Norman variant enproprier of Anglo-Norman apropr(i)er, approprier, related to modern French approprier.

impress.zh: n. 印象, 特征, 印记 / vt. 使有印象, 印, 铭刻, 传送, 影响, 强征 / vi. 给人印象
def: have an emotional or cognitive impact upon
produce or try to produce a vivid impression of
impress.ety: From Middle English impressen, from Latin impressus, perfect passive participle of imprimere (“to press into or upon, stick, stamp, or dig into”), from in (“in, upon”) + premere (“to press”).

imprint.zh: vt. 印, 铭刻 / n. 印, 印记, 特征, 痕迹, 版本说明
def: establish or impress firmly in the mind
a concavity in a surface produced by pressing
imprint.ety: From Middle English emprinten, enprinten, from Old French empreinter, from the past participle of empreindre, from Latin imprimere.

imprison.zh: vt. 使下狱, 关闭, 拘禁, 限制 / [法] 关押, 监禁, 限制
def: lock up or confine, in or as in a jail
confine as if in a prison

impropriety.zh: n. 不适当, 不得体, 不正当行为, 用词不当
impropriety.ety: From French impropriété, from Latin improprietās. By surface analysis, improper + -iety or im- + propriety.

impulse.zh: n. 冲动, 驱使, 刺激, 推动, 冲力, 建议, 脉冲 / vt. 推动
def: the electrical discharge that travels along a nerve fiber
impulse.ety: Borrowed from Middle French impulser, from Latin impulsus.

impunity.zh: n. 不受惩罚, 无事, 无患 / [法] 不受刑罚, 免罚, 免罪
def: Freedom from punishment or retribution; security from any reprisal or injurious consequences of an action, behaviour etc.
impunity.ety: From Middle French impunité, from Latin impunitas, from impunis (“without punishment”).

impure.zh: a. 不纯的, 肮脏的, 掺杂的, 混合的 / [医] 不纯的
def: (used of persons or behaviors) immoral or obscene
having a physical or moral blemish so as to make impure according to dietary or ceremonial laws-Leviticus 11:3
impure.ety: From Middle French impur, from Latin impūrus.

imbalance.zh: n. 不平衡, 不均衡 / [医] 不平衡, 失调
def: a lack of balance or state of disequilibrium

immaterial.zh: a. 非物质的, 无形的, 精神的 / [法] 非物质的, 无形的, 非实质的
def: of no importance or relevance especially to a law case
immaterial.ety: The adjective is derived from Late Middle English immaterial, inmateriall (“incorporeal; spiritual”), from Middle French immateriel (“not material”) (modern French immatériel), and from its etymon Med

immature.zh: a. 不成熟的, 未完全发育的, 粗糙的 / [医] 未成熟的
def: characteristic of a lack of maturity
(used of living things especially persons) in an early period of life or development or growth
not fully developed or mature; not ripe
immature.ety: From Middle French immature. Partially displaced unripe, from Old English unrīpe (“unripe, immature”).

impenitent.zh: a. 不知悔改的, 顽固的 / n. 不知悔改的人, 顽固的人
impenitent.ety: The adjective is derived from Late Middle English impenitent (“not penitent, unrepentant”), from Latin impaenitentem, the accusative feminine or masculine singular of impaenitēns (“unrepentant”), from

immigrant.zh: n. 移民 / a. 移入的, 移民的
def: a person who comes to a country where they were not born in order to settle there
A non-native person who comes to a country from another country to permanently settle there.
A plant or animal that establishes itself in an area where it previously did not exist.
immigrant.ety: From Latin immigrans, present active participle of immigrāre (“to migrate into”), from in- (“into”) + migrāre (“to migrate”).

immigrate.zh: vt. 使移居入境 / vi. 移入
def: come into a new country and change residency
immigrate.ety: From Latin immigratus, past participle of immigro (“remove, move into”).

immobility.zh: n. 不动性, 不动, 固定 / [医] 不动[性]
immobility.ety: From Middle French immobilité, equivalent to immobile + -ity.

immobilize.zh: vt. 使不动, 使固定, 使不能移动 / [医] 制动, 固定
def: hold as reserve or withdraw from circulation; of capital
to hold fast or prevent from moving
immobilize.ety: From French immobiliser, equivalent to immobile + -ize.

def: the trait of being vain and conceited
the perverse act of exposing and attracting attention to your own genitals

immortal.zh: n. 不朽人物, 神仙 / a. 永远的, 不死的, 长久的
def: a person (such as an author) of enduring fame
any supernatural being worshipped as controlling some part of the world or some aspect of life or who is the personification of a force
immortal.ety: From Latin immortālis, from prefix im- (“not”) (from in-) + mortālis (“mortal”) (from mors (“death”), combining form mort- + adjectival suffix -alis), equivalent to im- + mortal. Displaced native unde

impalpable.zh: a. 不可触知的, 不能感知的, 难以理解的 / [医] 不可接触的, 极细微的
def: incapable of being perceived by the senses especially the sense of touch- James Jeans
imperceptible to the senses or the mind
impalpable.ety: From Middle French impalpable, from Medieval Latin impalpabilis. See im- + palpable.

impartial.zh: a. 公平的, 不偏不倚的 / [法] 公正无私的, 不偏袒的, 公平的
def: free from undue bias or preconceived opinions
impartial.ety: Borrowed from Middle French impartial. See im- + partial.

impeccable.zh: a. 无懈可击的, 勿容置疑的, 无瑕疵的, 不会做坏事的
impeccable.ety: From Middle French impeccable, from Latin impeccabilis (“not liable to sin”), from im- (“not”) + peccare (“to err, to sin”).

impediment.zh: n. 妨碍, 障碍, 阻止, 口吃 / [经] 对履行义务的阻碍
def: something immaterial that interferes with or delays action or progress
any structure that makes progress difficult
impediment.ety: From Middle English impediment, borrowed from Latin impedimentum.

impenetrable.zh: a. 不能通过的, 不可理喻的, 费解的, 顽固的
def: not admitting of penetration or passage into or through
permitting little if any light to pass through because of denseness of matter
impenetrable.ety: From Middle English inpenetrabel, inpenetrabyle, from Middle French impenetrable or directly from its etymon, Latin impenetrābilis. By surface analysis, im- + penetrable.

impermanent.zh: a. 暂时的, 非永久的
def: not permanent; not lasting- James Thurber
existing or enduring for a limited time only
impermanent.ety: From Middle French impermanent, from im- + permanent.

impersonal.zh: a. 客观的, 和个人无关的, 没有人情味的, 非人称的 / n. 非人称动词(或代词)
def: not relating to or responsive to individual persons
impersonal.ety: From French impersonnel, from Latin impersōnālis, from im- (“not”) + persōnālis (“personal”), equivalent to im- + personal.

impersonate.zh: vt. 模仿, 扮演, 体现, 使人格化 / [法] 体现, 模仿, 拟人
def: assume or act the character of
represent another person with comic intentions
pretend to be someone you are not; sometimes with fraudulent intentions

impertinence.zh: n. 不切题, 鲁莽, 无礼, 不恰当 / [法] 不切题, 不对题, 不适合
def: the trait of being rude and impertinent; inclined to take liberties
impertinence.ety: Borrowed from Middle French impertinence, from impertinent (“impertinent”); by surface analysis, im- + pertinent.

impertinent.zh: a. 不切题的, 鲁莽的, 无礼的, 粗鲁的, 不恰当的
def: characterized by a lightly pert and exuberant quality
not pertinent to the matter under consideration
impertinent.ety: Inherited from Middle English impertinent, from Middle French impertinent, from Old French impertinent, from Latin impertinēns; by surface analysis, im- + pertinent.

imperturbable.zh: a. 沉着的, 泰然自若的, 镇静的
def: not easily perturbed or excited or upset; marked by extreme calm and composure
Not capable of being, or not easily, perturbed, excited, or upset; calm and collected, even under pressure.
imperturbable.ety: PIE word *né From Late Middle English imperturbable (“undisturbed; impossible to disturb”), borrowed from Late Latin imperturbābilis, from Latin im- (variant of in- (prefix meaning ‘not’)) + Late Lati

imponderable.zh: a. 无重量的, 无法计算的, 不可估价的 / n. 无法衡量的事物
def: a factor whose effects cannot be accurately assessed
difficult or impossible to evaluate with precision

importer.zh: n. 输入者, 进口商 / [法] 进口商, 输入者
def: someone whose business involves importing goods from outside (especially from a foreign country)
One who, or that which, imports: especially a person or company importing goods into a country.

imposition.zh: n. 征收, 课税, 强加, 欺骗 / [经] 征税, 税, 税款
def: the act of imposing something (as a tax or an embargo)
imposition.ety: From Middle English imposicioun, from Old French imposicion, from Latin impositio.

impossibility.zh: n. 不可能之事, 不可能 / [法] 不可能性, 不可能的事
def: an alternative that is not available
impossibility.ety: From Middle French impossibilité, from Latin impossibilitās. By surface analysis, im- + possibility and impossible + -ity.

impotent.zh: a. 无力的, 虚弱的, 无效的, 阳萎的
def: lacking power or ability- Freeman J.Dyson
impotent.ety: From Old French impotent, from Latin impotēns, from in- (expresses negation) + potēns (“powerful”).

impoverish.zh: vt. 使贫穷, 耗尽...的力气
impoverish.ety: From Middle English empoverishen, impoverishen, empoverischen, enpoverisshen, Anglo-Norman empoveriss-, from Old French empoverir, from em- + povre, from Latin pauper (“poor”) (English poor).

impregnable.zh: a. 无法攻取的, 坚强不屈的, 驳不倒的
def: immune to attack; incapable of being tampered with
incapable of being overcome, challenged or refuted
impregnable.ety: From Late Middle English imprenable, impregnable (“impossible to capture, impregnable”), from Old French imprenable (modern French imprenable (“impregnable”)), from im- (a variant of in- (prefix meani

impregnate.zh: vt. 使怀孕, 使肥沃, 使充满, 灌输 / a. 怀孕的, 充满的
def: fill, as with a certain quality
impregnate.ety: The adjective is first attested in 1540, the verb in 1605; borrowed from Medieval Latin impraegnātus, perfect passive participle of Latin impraegnō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-

impression.zh: n. 印象, 意念, 盖印, 印记, 印数, 底色, 效果 / [医] 压迹, 印模, 印象, 影响
def: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed
a clear and telling mental image
impression.ety: From Old French impression, from Latin impressio. Equivalent to impress + -ion.

impressive.zh: a. 给人深刻印象的, 威严的
def: making a strong or vivid impression

improbable.zh: a. 不大可能的, 不象发生的, 荒谬可笑的 / [法] 未必会的, 不大可能发生的, 未必确实的
def: not likely to be true or to occur or to have occurred
having a probability too low to inspire belief
too improbable to admit of belief
improbable.ety: Borrowed from Latin improbābilis. By surface analysis, im- + probable.

imprisonment.zh: n. 监禁, 下狱, 坐牢 / [法] 监禁, 徒刑, 拘禁
def: putting someone in prison or in jail as lawful punishment
the act of confining someone in a prison (or as if in a prison)
imprisonment.ety: From Anglo-Norman emprisonement, from Old French emprisonnement. See imprison + -ment.

imprudent.zh: a. 轻率的, 鲁莽的
imprudent.ety: From Middle French imprudent, from Latin imprūdens (“not foreseeing, ignorant”), prefix im- (“not”) + prūdens (“foreseeing, skilled, judicious”).

impulsive.zh: a. 冲动的, 受感情驱使的, 任性的 / [医] 冲动的
def: proceeding from natural feeling or impulse without external stimulus
having the power of driving or impelling
impulsive.ety: Borrowed from Middle French impulsif, from Latin impulsivus.

impurity.zh: n. 杂质, 不洁, 不纯 / [化] 杂质
def: worthless or dangerous material that should be removed
impurity.ety: From impure + -ity. From Middle French impurité, from Latin impuritas.

immaculate.zh: a. 无污点的, 纯洁的, 无缺点的, 无辜的 / [医] 无斑点, 无瑕疵的, 洁净的
immaculate.ety: From Late Middle English immaculat, immaculate (“blameless; flawless, spotless; specifically of the Virgin Mary: pure, undefiled”), borrowed from Latin immaculātus (“unstained”), from im- (negative pr

immeasurable.zh: a. 不可测量的, 无限的, 广大无边的
immeasurable.ety: From Middle English inmesurable, ynmesurable; equivalent to im- + measurable.

impartially.zh: adv. 公平地, 无私地; 秉公

immemorial.zh: a. 太古的, 远古的, 无法追忆的 / [法] 无法追溯的, 无法记忆的, 太古的
def: long past; beyond the limits of memory or tradition or recorded history
immemorial.ety: From French immémorial. By surface analysis, im- + memorial.

immigration.zh: n. 移民, 移居 / [医] 移民
def: migration into a place (especially migration to a country of which you are not a native in order to settle there)
the body of immigrants arriving during a specified interval

impersonation.zh: n. 扮演, 装扮, 模仿 / [计] 模仿
def: a representation of a person that is exaggerated for comic effect
imitating the mannerisms of another person

impractical.zh: a. 不切实际的, 不能实行的, 不现实的, 不合情理的
def: not practical; not workable or not given to practical matters

impressionable.zh: a. 易感的, 敏感的, 可塑的
def: Being easily influenced (especially of young people).

impracticality.zh: n. 不切实际, 办不到
def: concerned with theoretical possibilities rather than actual use
The state or quality of being impractical.

implicate.zh: vt. 涉及, 含意, 暗示, 牵连 / n. 包含的东西
def: bring into intimate and incriminating connection
impose, involve, or imply as a necessary accompaniment or result

implication.zh: n. 牵连, 含义, 暗示 / [法] 推断, 含蓄之意, 暗示

implication.ety: From Middle French implication, from Latin implicationem (accusative of implicatio). Equivalent to implicate + -ion.

imperfect.zh: a. 不完美的, 不完整的, 减弱的, 未完成过去时的 / n. 未完成体

improvident.zh: a. 无远见的, 浪费的

improvident.ety: From the Latin improvidens, equivalent to in- + provident.

imperceptible.ety: Inherited from Middle English imperceptible, from Middle French imperceptible and its etymon Medieval Latin imperceptibilis. By surface analysis, im- + perceptible.

rubicund.zh: a. 红润的, 透红的
def: inclined to a healthy reddish color often associated with outdoor life
rubicund.ety: From Latin rubicundus, from rubere (“to be red”).

rumour.ety: From Middle English rumour, from Old French rumour, rumor, from Latin rūmor (“common talk”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *rewH- (“to shout, roar”).

ruddy.zh: a. 红的, 红润的 / v. (使)变红

of a color at the end of the color spectrum (next to orange); resembling the color of blood or cherries or tomatoes or rubies
ruddy.ety: Inherited from Middle English rody, from Old English rudiġ (“reddish; ruddy”), from rudu + -iġ. By surface analysis, rud (“redness”) + -y. Compare Icelandic roði (“redness”).

rude.zh: a. 粗鲁无礼的, 粗陋的, 粗暴的, 原始的, 未开化的, 大略的, 崎岖不平的, 狂暴的

rude.ety: From Middle English rude, from Old French rude, ruide, from Latin rudis (“rough, raw, rude, wild, untilled”).

ruffle.zh: n. 皱褶, 波纹, 生气, 混乱 / vt. 弄皱, 触怒, 洗(牌), 连续轻擂(鼓) / vi. 起皱, 发脾气, 连续轻擂

rueful.zh: a. 悲伤的, 后悔的, 可怜的

via.zh: prep. 经由, 经过, 通过 / [医] 病毒灭活剂

A small hole in a printed circuit board filled with metal which connects two or more layers.
via.ety: Borrowed from Latin via (“road”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ-. Possible doublet of way. The sense in electronics is also explained as vertical interconnect access.

viable.zh: a. 能养活的, 能生长发育的 / [医] 有活力的, 有生机的

viable.ety: Borrowed from French viable (further from Latin vīta), with semantic influence of Latin viābilis (“passable”).

vial.zh: n. 小瓶 / vt. 装入小瓶

A glass or plastic vessel or bottle, especially a small tube-shaped bottle used to store medicine, perfume or other chemicals.
To keep or put (something, especially a liquid) in, or as if in, a vial (noun sense).
vial.ety: From Middle English vial, viole, a variant of fiole, phiole, phial (“small bowl or cup for liquids, etc.; flask”) [and other forms]: see further at phial. Doublet of phiale.

vicarious.zh: a. 代理的, 代用的, 替代的 / [医] 替代的, 错位的

vicarious.ety: From Latin vicārius (“vicarious, substituted”) + English -ous. First attested in the 17th century. Doublet of vicar.

vice.zh: n. 恶习, 恶行, 罪恶, 堕落, 缺陷, 恶癖, 老虎钳 / vt. 钳住 / prep. 代替
vice.ety: PIE word *dwóh₁ From Middle English vice, from Old French vice, from Latin vitium (“fault or blemish”). Displaced native Old English unþēaw.

def: Proximity; the state of being near.
vicinity.ety: From vicine + -ity, from Latin vīcīnitās (“neighborhood”) (compare French vicinité), from vīcīnus (“neighbor”) (compare French voisin), from vīcus (“village”).

vicious.zh: a. 邪恶的, 堕落的, 品性不端的, 恶毒的, 恶性的, 有错误的 / [医] 缺点的, 恶的
def: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
vicious.ety: PIE word *dwóh₁ From Middle English vicious, from Anglo-Norman vicious, (modern French vicieux), from Latin vitiōsus, from vitium (“fault, vice”). Equivalent to vice + -ous.

vicissitude.zh: n. 变化无常, 变迁, 荣枯, 盛衰
def: a variation in circumstances or fortune at different times in your life or in the development of something
mutability in life or nature (especially successive alternation from one condition to another)

victim.zh: n. 受害人, 牺牲者, 牺牲品 / [法] 受害人, 被害人, 遭难者
def: an unfortunate person who suffers from some adverse circumstance
a person who is tricked or swindled
victim.ety: From Middle French victime, from Latin victima (“sacrificial animal”). Although this root and victor drive from homophonous PIE roots, they are traditionally reconstructed as separate words and thus n

victor.zh: n. 胜利者 / a. 胜利的
def: a combatant who is able to defeat rivals
the contestant who wins the contest
victor.ety: Inherited from Middle English victour, victor, from Anglo-Norman victor, Latin victor (“conqueror”). Doublet of Victor.

video.zh: n. 影像, 电视 / a. 图像的, 电视的
def: the visible part of a television transmission
a recording of both the visual and audible components (especially one containing a recording of a movie or television program)
(computer science) the appearance of text and graphics on a video display
video.ety: From the root vide of Latin videō (“to see”) + -o, formed in analogy to audio.

vie.zh: vi. 争, 竞争, 争胜 / vt. 提出...来竞争, 以...作较量

To fight for superiority; to contend; to compete eagerly so as to gain something.
vie.ety: Apheretic form of envy, from Middle English envien, from Old French envier, from Latin invītō.

view.zh: n. 视野, 风景, 见解, 视力, 观看, 视图, 指望, 意图, 印象 / vt. 看, 考虑, 视察, 查看, 估量 / [计] 视图
def: a way of regarding situations or topics etc.
the visual percept of a region

a purposeful surveillance to guard or observe

vile.zh: a. 恶劣的, 肮脏的, 低廉的, 卑鄙的 / [法] 极坏的, 恶劣的, 卑鄙的

vile.ety: From Middle English vile, vyle, vyl, from Anglo-Norman ville, Old French vil, vile, from Latin vīlis.

vilify.ety: From Late Latin vīlificāre (“vilify”). Equivalent to vile + -ify. Compare vilipend.

villa.ety: Borrowed from Italian villa, from Latin vīlla (“country house”). Doublet of vill and ville.

def: show to be right by providing justification or proof

vindictive.zh: a. 有报仇心的, 怀恨的, 惩罚的 / [法] 报复的, 有报仇心的, 复仇的

showing malicious ill will and a desire to hurt; motivated by spite
vindictive.ety: From Latin vindicta (“vengeance”) + -ive. Contrast Latin vindicātīvus.

Someone who believes in vitalism, the doctrine that life cannot be entirely reduced to physical and chemical factors.

Watchful, especially for danger or disorder; alert; wary.
