Similar reverence to one's parents and family or to one's country.
piety.ety: From Middle English piete, borrowed from Middle French pieté, from Latin pietās. See also the doublets pietà and pity. By surface analysis, pious + -ety.

pig.zh: n. 猪, 猪肉, 贪婪的人, 猪一样的人 / v. 生小猪, 象猪般地生活
def: live like a pig, in squalor
pig.ety: From Middle English pigge (“pig, piglet”) (originally a term for a young pig, with adult pigs being swyn (“swine”)), from Old English *picga, *pycga (attested in picgbrēad (“mast, pig-fodder”)), perha

pigeon.zh: n. 鸽子, 易上当受骗的人, 年轻女子
def: wild and domesticated birds having a heavy body and short legs
One of several birds of the family Columbidae within the order Columbiformes.
pigeon.ety: Inherited from Middle English pygeoun, borrowed from Old French pyjon, inherited from Late Latin pīpiōnem (“chirping bird”), derived from Latin pīpiāre (“to chirp”), of imitative origin. Partly displa

pigment.zh: n. 色素, 色质, 颜料 / [化] 颜料
def: dry coloring material (especially a powder to be mixed with a liquid to produce paint, etc.)
acquire pigment; become colored or imbued
any substance whose presence in plant or animal tissues produces a characteristic color
pigment.ety: From Middle English pigment, from Latin pigmentum (“pigment”), itself from pingō (“to paint”) + -mentum; variants of this word may have been known in Old English (e.g. 12th century pyhmentum). Doublet

pike.zh: n. 长矛, 尖头, (体操)屈体, 流浪者, 狗鱼, 通行费 / vi. 用矛刺杀, 刺, 离开, 谨慎办事, 采用屈体姿势
def: a broad highway designed for high-speed traffic
highly valued northern freshwater fish with lean flesh
a sharp point (as on the end of a spear)
pike.ety: From Middle English pyke, pyk, pik, pike (“pike; sharp point, iron tip of a staff or spear, pointed toe of an item of footwear; sharp tool; mountain, peak”), from Old English pīc (“pointed object, pic

pile.zh: n. 堆, 大堆, 大厦, 建筑群, 电池, 大量, 桥桩, 软毛, 痔疮 / vi. 堆起, 堆积, 积累, 挤, 猛烈攻击 / vt. 堆于, 累积, 堆叠, 打桩于, 用桩支撑
def: a collection of objects laid on top of each other
(often followed by `of') a large number or amount or extent
pile.ety: From French pile (“battery”), with the pronunciation adapted to the existing English word pile. Doublet of Etymology 1, which may have influenced the sense development by emphasizing the stack (“pile”

pilfer.zh: v. 盗取, 小偷小摸, 剽窃
def: make off with belongings of others
To steal in small quantities, or articles of small value; to practise petty theft.
pilfer.ety: From earlier pilfre, from Middle English pilfre (“booty”), from Old French pelfre (“plunder, booty, spoils”), of unknown origin. Compare pelf.

pilgrim.zh: n. 旅行者, 朝圣者, 香客 / vi. 朝圣
def: someone who journeys in foreign lands
one of the colonists from England who sailed to America on the Mayflower and founded the colony of Plymouth in New England in 1620
someone who journeys to a sacred place as an act of religious devotion
pilgrim.ety: Inherited from Middle English pilegrim, from Old English pilegrī̆m, from Old French pelegrin, from Latin peregrīnus (“foreigner”). Doublet of peregrine. The change of /r…r/ to /l…r/ is an effect of di

pill.zh: n. 药丸, 弹丸, 屈辱, 胡说 / v. 做成药丸, 形成丸状, 服药丸, 挫败, 抢劫
def: something that resembles a tablet of medicine in shape or size
a dose of medicine in the form of a small pellet
pill.ety: From Middle English *pill, *pyll, from Old English pyll (“a pool, pill”), from Proto-Germanic *pullijaz (“small pool, ditch, creek”), diminutive of Proto-Germanic *pullaz (“pool, stream”), from Proto-

pillage.zh: n. 掠夺, 抢劫, 掠夺物, 战利品 / v. 掠夺, 抢劫
def: the act of stealing valuable things from a place
pillage.ety: From Old French pillage, from piller (“plunder”), from an unattested meaning of Late Latin piliō, probably a figurative use of Latin pilō (“to remove (hair)”), from pilus (“hair”).

pillar.zh: n. 柱子, 栋梁, 台柱, 重要的支持者 / [医] 柱, 脚
def: anything that approximates the shape of a column or tower
pillar.ety: From Middle English piler, from Old French pilier, from Medieval Latin or Vulgar Latin *pilāre (“a pillar”), from Latin pila (“a pillar, pier, mole”).

pillow.zh: n. 枕头, 靠垫, 枕状岩 / vt. 作...的枕头, 垫, 枕于 / vi. 靠在枕上
def: a cushion to support the head of a sleeping person
rest on or as if on a pillow
pillow.ety: From Middle English pilwe, from Old English pyle, pylu (“pillow”), from Proto-West Germanic *pulwī (“pillow”), from Latin pulvīnus (“cushion”), derived from pulvis (“dust”), for the filler of a pillow

pilot.zh: n. 飞行员, 领航员, 航船者, 导向器, 驾驶仪, 向导, 领导人 / vt. 领航, 驾驶, 引导, 试用 / a. 引导的, 控制的, 试点的
def: someone who is licensed to operate an aircraft in flight
act as the navigator in a car, plane, or vessel and plan, direct, plot the path and position of the conveyance
pilot.ety: From Middle French pilot, pillot, from Italian pilota, piloto, older also pedotta, pedot(t)o (the form in pil- is probably influenced by pileggiare (“to sail, navigate”)); ultimately from unattested B

pimple.zh: n. 丘疹, 小脓疱 / [医] 丘疹, 小脓疱
def: a small inflamed elevation of the skin; a pustule or papule; common symptom in acne
An inflamed (raised and colored) spot on the surface of the skin that is usually painful and fills with pus.
pimple.ety: Early Modern English pimple, pumple, from Middle English pymple, pympyl, of uncertain origin but probably a nasalized variant of Old English *pipel, *pypel, from Old English piplian, pyplian (“to brea

pin.zh: n. 大头针, 针, 别针, 栓, 销子, 图钉, 插头, 管脚, 品(液量单位) / vt. 将...用针别住, 钉住, 压住, 牵制, 使不能动, 归罪于 / a. 针的, 销子的, 闩的
def: to hold fast or prevent from moving
a piece of jewelry that is pinned onto the wearer's garment
attach or fasten with pins or as if with pins. "pin the blame on the innocent man"
pin.ety: From Middle English pinne, from Old English pinn (“pin, peg, bolt”), from Proto-Germanic *pinnaz, *pinnō, *pint- (“protruding point, peak, peg, pin, nail”), from Proto-Indo-European *bend- (“protrudin

pinch.zh: n. 捏, 拧, 撮, 少量, 收缩, 挤压, 夹痛, 苦恼, 逮捕, 指控, 匮乏, 紧急关头 / vt. 捏, 拧, 掐, 挤压, 修剪, 使困苦, 使萎缩, 节制, 少量加入, 逮捕, 勒索 / vi. 收缩, 节省, 挤压, 引起苦恼
def: make ridges into by pinching together
pinch.ety: From Middle English pinchen, from Old Northern French *pinchier (compare Old French pincier, pincer (“to pinch”)), a word of uncertain origin, possibly from Vulgar Latin *pinciāre (“to puncture, pinch

pine.zh: n. 松树, 松木 / vi. 消瘦, 憔悴, 痛苦, 怀念, 渴望 / [计] 邮件程序
def: straight-grained durable and often resinous white to yellowish timber of any of numerous trees of the genus Pinus
have a desire for something or someone who is not present
pine.ety: From Middle English pyne, pine, probably from Old English *pīne (“pain”), from Proto-West Germanic *pīnā (“pain, torment, torture”), possibly from Latin poena (“punishment”), from Ancient Greek ποινή

pink.zh: n. 粉红色, 石竹花, 化身, 典范, 头面人物, 极度 / a. 粉红的, 石竹科的, 比较激进的, 脸色发红的, 精致的, 有点下流的 / vt. 刺, 扎, 刺痛, 射伤, 使面红耳赤, 使变粉红色
def: of a light shade of red
make light, repeated taps on a surface
pink.ety: * As an English surname, from Old English pinca (“chaffinch”). This would not be a native Germanic inheritance as the expected form would be finc, thus probably borrowed or contaminated from Vulgar La

pinnacle.zh: n. 小尖塔, 尖峰, 高峰, 极点 / vt. 造小尖塔, 置于尖顶上
def: (architecture) a slender upright spire at the top of a buttress of tower
the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development
pinnacle.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French pinacle, pinnacle, from Late Latin pinnāculum (“a peak, pinnacle”), from Latin pinna (“a pinnacle”); see pin. Doublet of panache.

pint.zh: n. 品脱(干量或液量的单位) / [医] 量磅, 品脱
def: a British imperial capacity measure (liquid or dry) equal to 4 gills or 568.26 cubic centimeters
a United States dry unit equal to 0.5 quart or 33.6 cubic inches
a United States liquid unit equal to 16 fluid ounces; two pints equal one quart
pint.ety: From Middle English pinte, from Old French pinte, assumed from Vulgar Latin *pincta (“a mark used to indicate a level of quantity against a larger measure”), from Latin picta (“painted”), from Latin p

pioneer.zh: n. 先锋, 拓荒者, 创始人 / vt. 提倡, 开辟, 开创, 倡导 / vi. 作先驱, 开路
def: open up an area or prepare a way
someone who helps to open up a new line of research or technology or art
one the first colonists or settlers in a new territory
pioneer.ety: From Middle French pionnier (“originally, a foot soldier”), Old French peonier, from peon (“a foot soldier”) (modern French: pion). See pawn (in chess).

pious.zh: a. 虔诚的, 敬神的, 尽责的, 可嘉的, 不可能实现的
def: having or showing or expressing reverence for a deity
Of or pertaining to piety, exhibiting piety, devout, god-fearing.
Relating to religion or religious works.
pious.ety: Borrowed from Latin pīus (“pious, dutiful, blessed, kind, devout”), from Proto-Indo-European *pewH- (“pure”). Cognate with Old English fǣle (“faithful, trusty, good; dear, beloved”). More at feal.

pipe.zh: n. 管, 导管, 输送管, 管状器官, 声带, 尖细的声音, 烟斗, 笛, 管乐器 / vt. 以管输送, 吹哨子, 吹奏, 尖声唱 / vi. 吹笛, 尖叫, 吹长哨发令
def: a tube with a small bowl at one end; used for smoking tobacco
a long tube made of metal or plastic that is used to carry water or oil or gas etc.
pipe.ety: From Middle English pīpe, pype (“hollow cylinder or tube used as a conduit or container; duct or vessel of the body; musical instrument; financial records maintained by the English Exchequer, pipe rol

piquant.zh: a. 辛辣的, 开胃的, 刺激的, 活泼的, 调皮的, 淘气的, 可爱的
piquant.ety: Borrowed from Middle French piquant (“pricking, stimulating, irritating”), present participle of piquer, possibly from Old French pikier (“to prick, sting, nettle”). Doublet of picong. Related to pike

pique.zh: n. 赌气, 愤怒, 不快, 凹凸织物 / vt. 伤害...自尊心, 激怒, 刺激, 引起兴趣, 使兴奋
def: tightly woven fabric with raised cords
cause to feel resentment or indignation
pique.ety: The verb is borrowed from French piquer (“to prick, sting; to anger, annoy; (reflexive) to get angry; to provoke, stimulate; (reflexive) to boast about”), from Middle French piquer, picquer (“to prick

piracy.zh: n. 海盗行为, 海上劫掠, 剽窃, 著作权侵害, 非法翻印 / [法] 海盗行为, 海上掠夺, 海盗罪
def: hijacking on the high seas or in similar contexts; taking a ship or plane away from the control of those who are legally entitled to it
the act of plagiarizing; taking someone's words or ideas as if they were your own
piracy.ety: From Medieval Latin pīrātia, from Classical Latin pīrāta + ia, or Ancient Greek πειρατεία (peirateía). The sense of “unauthorized duplication” developed in England between 1660 and 1710. The English C

pirate.zh: n. 海盗, 盗印者, 侵犯专利权者 / vt. 盗印, 掠夺, 翻印 / vi. 做海盗, 从事劫掠
def: someone who uses another person's words or ideas as if they were his own
someone who robs at sea or plunders the land from the sea without having a commission from any sovereign nation
pirate.ety: From Middle English pirate, pirat, pyrat, from Old French pirate, from Latin pīr

pirouette.zh: n. 脚尖旋转, 快速旋转 / vi. 以脚尖旋转, 作快速旋转
def: (ballet) a rapid spin of the body (especially on the toes as in ballet)
do a pirouette, usually as part of a dance
pirouette.ety: Borrowed from French pirouette, see there for more; attested since 1706.

piss.zh: vi. 小便, 下大雨, 抱怨 / vt. 撒尿弄脏, 尿在...上 / n. 小便
piss.ety: From Middle English pisse (noun) and pissen (verb), from Old French pissier, possibly from Vulgar Latin *pīssiāre, probably of imitative origin. Compare Old Norse pissa (“to urinate, piss”). Displaced

pistol.zh: n. 手枪, 信号枪 / vt. 以手枪杀死(或伤害)
def: a firearm that is held and fired with one hand
The type of handgun with the chamber integral with the barrel.
pistol.ety: Probably from Middle French pistole, or via Middle English pistolet, from Middle French pistolet (“small firearm or small dagger”). The origin is unclear. If via German to Romance probably from Middle

piston.zh: n. 活塞, 活塞阀键 / [医] 活塞(如注射器的)
def: mechanical device that has a plunging or thrusting motion

pit.zh: n. 深坑, 矿井, 果核, 地窖, 深渊, 绝境, 陷阱 / vt. 窖藏, 使凹下, 使有麻点, 去...之核, 使留疤痕, 使相斗, 使竞争 / vi. 起凹点, 凹陷
def: a sizeable hole (usually in the ground)
a concavity in a surface (especially an anatomical depression)
pit.ety: From Dutch pit (“kernel, core”), from Middle Dutch pitte, from Proto-Germanic *pittan (compare dialectal German Pfitze (“pimple”)), oblique of Proto-Germanic *piþō. Compare pith.

pitch.zh: n. 程度, 坡度, 顶点, 前倾, 倾斜, 投掷, 音高, 螺距, 节距, 摊位, 树脂, 沥青 / vt. 投, 掷, 向前倾跌, 扎营, 竭力推销, 为...定调, 定位于, 用沥青涂 / vi. 搭帐篷, 投掷, 向前跌, 猛然摔倒, 坠落, 倾斜
def: throw or toss with a light motion
the property of sound that varies with variation in the frequency of vibration
pitch.ety: From Middle English picche, piche, pich, from Old English piċ, from Proto-West Germanic *pik, from Latin pix. Cognate with Ancient Greek πίσσα (píssa, “pitch, tar”), Latin pīnus (“pine”). More at pine

pith.zh: n. 木髓, 骨髓, 要旨, 重要性, 力量, 核心, 意义, 精华 / vt. 从(植物茎)中取髓, 刺毁(动物的)脑脊髓
def: soft spongelike central cylinder of the stems of most flowering plants
the choicest or most essential or most vital part of some idea or experience
pith.ety: The noun is derived from Middle English pith, pithe (“soft interior; pith, pulp”) [and other forms], from Old English piþa [and other forms], from Proto-Germanic *piþô, from earlier *piþō (oblique *pi

pittance.zh: n. 少量津贴, 小额施舍, 少量
def: A small allowance of food and drink; a scanty meal.
A meagre allowance of money or wages.
pittance.ety: From Middle English pitaunce, from Old French pitance, pitence, from Medieval Latin *pietāntia, from Latin pietās (“piety”).

pity.zh: n. 遗憾, 同情, 怜悯, 憾事, 可惜 / vt. 同情, 怜悯 / vi. 觉得可怜, 有同情心
def: a feeling of sympathy and sorrow for the misfortunes of others
pity.ety: From Middle English pitye, pitie, pittye, pitee, pite, from Anglo-Norman pité, pittee etc., from Old French pitet, pitié, from Latin pietās. See also the doublets pietà and piety.

pivot.zh: n. 枢轴, 支点, 旋转运动, 中枢, 关键人物 / a. 枢轴的, (如)在枢轴上转动的 / vi. 在枢轴上转动, 随着转移
def: the person in a rank around whom the others wheel and maneuver
axis consisting of a short shaft that supports something that turns
pivot.ety: From Middle English pevet, *pivot, from Old French pivot (“hinge pin, pivot”) (12th c.), possibly from Latin pūgiō.

def: Italian open pie made of thin bread dough spread with a spiced mixture of e.g. tomato sauce and cheese
A baked Italian dish of a thinly rolled bread crust typically topped before baking with tomato sauce, cheese, and other ingredients such as meat or vegetables.
A single instance of this dish.
pizza.ety: First attested in 1931, borrowed from Neapolitan pizza (1590), the dialectal form of Byzantine Greek πίτα (píta, “cake, pie”). The Greek word is first attested in 1107 and is itself of uncertain origi

pilferage.zh: n. 小偷小摸, 偷窃, 赃物 / [经] 偷窃险, 脏物
def: the act of stealing small amounts or small articles
The individual act or recurring practice of stealing items of low value, especially in small quantities, for which the legal term is petty theft.

pianist.zh: n. 钢琴家, 钢琴演奏者
def: a person who plays the piano
A person who plays the piano, particularly with skill or as part of an orchestra.
A spy using radio or wireless telegraphy to keep in touch with headquarters during the Second World War.
pianist.ety: From French pianiste, from Italian pianista. Analyzable as piano + -ist.

pictorial.zh: a. 绘画的, 插图的, 用图画表示的, 形象化的, 有象形文字特征的 / n. 画报, 画刊, 有图邮票, 插图杂志, 插图报纸
def: pertaining to or consisting of pictures
evoking lifelike images within the mind
a periodical (magazine or newspaper) containing many pictures
pictorial.ety: From Latin pictōrius (“of painting”) + -al, from pictor (“painter”).

picture.zh: n. 图画, 照片, 景色, 美丽如画的人(或物), 化身, 生动的描述, 想像, 形象思维 / vt. 画, 拍摄, 用图说明, 描写, 想像 / [计] 图象; 形象; 字形
def: a visual representation (of an object or scene or person or abstraction) produced on a surface
graphic art consisting of an artistic composition made by applying paints to a surface
a clear and telling mental image
picture.ety: Inherited from Middle English picture, from Latin pictūra (“the art of painting, a painting”), from pingō (“to paint”). Doublet of pictura.

pitcher.zh: n. 有把的大罐, 瓶状体, 投手, 摊贩
def: (baseball) the person who does the pitching
an open vessel with a handle and a spout for pouring
the quantity contained in a pitcher
pitcher.ety: From Middle English picher, from Old French pichier, pechier (“small jug”), bichier (compare modern French pichet), from Late Latin or Medieval Latin pīcārium, alteration of bīcārium, itself possibly

pithy.zh: a. 有髓的, 由髓组成的, 简洁有力的
def: concise and full of meaning- Hervey Allen
Of, like, or abounding in pith; spongy or having small holes or pits.
pithy.ety: From Middle English pithy, pythy, equivalent to pith + -y.

pitiful.zh: a. 慈悲的, 可怜的, 令人同情的, 可鄙的
pitiful.ety: From Middle English pityful, piteful, piteeful. By surface analysis, pit(i) + -ful.

pitiless.zh: a. 无情的, 冷酷的, 无怜悯心的
def: deficient in humane and kindly feelings
pitiless.ety: From Middle English piteeles, pyteles; equivalent to pity + -less.

pivotal.zh: a. 枢轴的, 关键的, 起中心作用的
def: being of crucial importance- Henry Kissinger
Of, relating to, or being a pivot.
Being of crucial importance; central, key.

pithiness.zh: n. 多髓性, 简洁有力
def: terseness and economy in writing and speaking achieved by expressing a great deal in just a few words

picturesque.zh: a. 生动的, 如画的, 独特的, 别致的, 栩栩如生的
def: suggesting or suitable for a picture; pretty as a picture
picturesque.ety: From picture + -esque, a calque of French pittoresque, from picture (“a picture, painting”).

piebald.zh: a. 花斑的, 杂色的, 杂种的 / n. 花斑马
def: having sections or patches colored differently and usually brightly
Spotted or blotched, especially in black and white.
piebald.ety: From pie (“magpie”) + bald (“having white patches or blazes”). Compare typologically Polish srokaty < sroka.

def: a thief who steals from the pockets or purses of others in public places
One who steals from the pocket of a passerby, usually by sleight of hand.

pickup.zh: n. 拾起, 加速, 刺激, 猎物的收集, 好转, 恢复健康, 搭车者, 兴奋剂, 电视摄像 / [电] 拾音器
def: a light truck with an open body and low sides and a tailboard
a warrant to take someone into custody

piecemeal.zh: adv. 一件一件地, 逐个地, 零碎地 / a. 一片一片的, 逐渐的, 零碎的 / n. 断片
def: a little bit at a time
piecemeal.ety: From Middle English pecemele, from pece (“piece”) + mele (from Old English mǣlum (“at a time”), dative plural form of mǣl (“time, measure”), taking the place of Old English styċċemǣlum (“in pieces, bi

pigsty.zh: n. 猪舍, 肮脏地方
def: An enclosure where pigs are kept, either a building or part of one.
A dirty or very untidy place.
bed linen consisting of a cover for a pillow
A washable, easily removable cloth cover for pillows.

pineapple.zh: n. 凤梨, 菠萝, 失业救济金 / [医] 凤梨, 波萝
def: a tropical American plant bearing a large fleshy edible fruit with a terminal tuft of stiff leaves; widely cultivated in the tropics
large sweet fleshy tropical fruit with a terminal tuft of stiff leaves; widely cultivated
pineapple.ety: From Middle English pinappel (“pinecone”, literally “pine-apple/pine-fruit”), from Proto-West Germanic *pīnapplu. Later applied to the fruit of the pineapple plant due to its resemblance to a pinecone

pinhead.zh: n. 针头, 小东西, 微不足道的东西
pinhead.ety: So called because they sold pin-on lilies to commemorate the Easter Rising.

pinpoint.zh: n. 极小之物, 针尖, 立锥之地, 精确位置 / vt. 精确地找到, 准确地轰炸, 刺穿, 准确描述, 使突出, 强调 / a. 针尖的, 极微的, 精确的, 详尽的, 精确定位的

pipeline.zh: n. 管道, 传递途径 / [化] 管路; 管线
def: a pipe used to transport liquids or gases

pitfall.zh: n. 陷阱, 诱惑, 阴谋, 易犯的错误, 意想不到的困难
def: an unforeseen or unexpected or surprising difficulty
a trap in the form of a concealed hole
pitfall.ety: First recorded use in the 14th century from pit + fall in the sense of "pit trap, pit snare", from Old English fealle (“trap, snare”), from Proto-Germanic *fallą, *fallaz (“a fall, trap”), from Proto-

quisling.zh: n. 卖国贼 / [法] 卖国贼, 内奸, 通敌分子

quaver.zh: vi. 发颤音, 颤抖 / vt. 颤抖地说, 用颤声唱出 / n. 颤抖, 颤声, 八分音符

quagmire.zh: n. 沼泽地, 泥坑, 泥潭, 泥沼, 沼泽, 困境

quail.zh: n. 鹌鹑 / vi. 胆怯, 畏缩

quail.ety: From Middle English quayle, quaile, quaille, from Anglo-Norman quaille, from Late Latin quaccola (“quail”). (prostitute): So called because the quail was thought to be a very amorous bird.

quaint.ety: From Middle English queynte, quoynte, from Anglo-Norman cointe, queinte and Old French cointe (“pretty, clever, knowing”), from Latin cognitus, past participle of cognōscō (“to know”).

quake.zh: vi. 颤抖, 地震 / n. 颤抖, 地震

qualify.ety: Borrowed from Middle French qualifier (“to qualify”). Equivalent to quality + -fy.

quantum.ety: From Late Latin quantum, noun use of neuter form of Latin quantus (“how much”).

quarrel.zh: n. 吵架, 反目, 怨言, 方头凿 / vi. 吵架, 争论, 挑剔
def: an arrow that is shot from a crossbow; has a head with four edges
quarrel.ety: From Middle English querele (“altercation, dispute; argument, debate; armed combat; trial by combat; basis for dispute, complaint; claim, legal suit; a lament; illness”) [and other forms], from Anglo-

quarter.zh: n. 四分之一, 一刻钟, 季度, 地区 / vt. 四等分, 肢解 / vi. 驻扎, 住宿

def: a conveyance that transports people or objects
a medium for the expression or achievement of something
any substance that facilitates the use of a drug or pigment or other material that is mixed with it
vehicle.ety: Borrowed from French véhicule, from Latin vehiculum (“a carriage, conveyance”), from vehō, vehere (“to carry”).

veil.zh: n. 面纱, 面罩, 借口, 幕, 帐, 遮蔽物 / vt. 戴面纱, 隐藏, 遮蔽, 掩饰 / vi. 蒙上面纱
def: to obscure, or conceal with or as if with a veil
a garment that covers the head and face
a membranous covering attached to the immature fruiting body of certain mushrooms
veil.ety: From Middle English veil, veyl, from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French veil (“sail, veil, shroud”) (Francien Old French voil, French voile), Latin vēlum (“cloth, covering”). Displaced Middle Englis

vein.zh: n. 血管, 静脉, 纹理, 气质, 情绪 / vt. 使有脉络, 像脉络般分布于
def: a blood vessel that carries blood from the capillaries toward the heart
vein.ety: From Middle English veine, borrowed from Anglo-Norman veine, from Latin vēna (“a blood-vessel; vein; artery”) of uncertain origin. See vēna for more. Doublet of vena. Displaced native edre, from ǣdre

velvet.zh: n. 天鹅绒 / a. 天鹅绒的
def: a silky densely piled fabric with a plain back
smooth and soft to sight or hearing or touch or taste
resembling velvet in having a smooth soft surface
velvet.ety: From Middle English velvet, velwet, veluet, from Old Occitan veluet, from Vulgar Latin *villutittus, diminutive of villūtus, from Latin villus (“shaggy hair, tuft of hair”). Cognate with French velour

venal.zh: a. 可收买的, 贪污的, 用金钱买得的 / [经] 贪污的
venal.ety: Borrowed from French vénal, from Old French venel, from Latin vēnālis (“for sale”), from vēnum (“something for sale”); compare English vend.

vendetta.zh: n. 族间仇杀, 世仇, 宿怨 / [法] 血仇, 近亲复仇, 世仇
def: a feud in which members of the opposing parties murder each other
A bitter, destructive feud, normally between two families, clans, or factions, in which each injury or slaying is revenged: a blood feud.
vendetta.ety: Borrowed from Italian vendetta (“revenge”), from Latin vindicta. See vindicate, avenge.

veneer.zh: n. 饰面薄板, 饰面, 外表 / vt. 镶饰, 胶合, 虚饰
def: coating consisting of a thin layer of superior wood glued to a base of inferior wood
an ornamental coating to a building
veneer.ety: From German Furnier, from furnieren (“to inlay, cover with a veneer”), from French fournir (“to furnish, accomplish”), from Middle French fornir, from Old French fornir, furnir (“to furnish”), from Ol

venereal.zh: a. 性爱的, 性交的, 性病的, 生殖器的 / [医] 性病的, 性交的
def: of or relating to the external sex organs
Of or relating to the genitals or sexual intercourse.
Of a disease: sexually transmitted; of or relating to, or adapted to the cure of, a venereal disease.
venereal.ety: From Middle English venereal, venerealle (“of or relating to sexual intercourse”), from Latin venereus, venerius (“of or relating to sexual love”), from Venus (“Roman goddess of love”) (from Proto-Ind

venial.zh: a. 可原谅的, 可宽恕的, 轻微的 / [法] 可宽恕的, 可原谅的, 轻微的
venial.ety: From Old French venial, borrowed from Late Latin veniālem (“pardonable”), from Latin venia (“forgiveness”).

def: meat from a deer used as food
The meat of a deer, especially one that was hunted in its own natural habitat.
venison.ety: From Middle English venisoun, venesoun, from Anglo-Norman veneisun, venesoun, venesun (“meat of large game, particularly deer or boar; hunt”), from Latin vēnātiō, vēnātiōnem (“hunt; meat from a hunt”)

venom.zh: n. 毒液, 恶意 / vt. 放毒, 使有毒
def: toxin secreted by animals; secreted by certain snakes and poisonous insects (e.g., spiders and scorpions)
feeling a need to see others suffer
venom.ety: From Middle English venym, from Old French venim, from Vulgar Latin *venīmen, from Early Medieval Latin venīnum, from Classical Latin venēnum (“drug; poison; a charm”), ultimately derived from Proto-I

vent.zh: n. 排气口, 出口, 通风孔, 发泄 / vt. 发泄, 排出, 给...开孔
def: a hole for the escape of gas or air
external opening of urinary or genital system of a lower vertebrate
vent.ety: Partly from Middle French vent, from Latin ventus and partly from French éventer. Cognate with French vent and Spanish viento (“wind”) and ventana (“window”). Doublet of wind.

ventilate.zh: vt. 使空气流通, 使通风, 公开讨论, 公开 / [医] 通风, 换气
def: expose to cool or cold air so as to cool or freshen
expose to the circulation of fresh air so as to retard spoilage
ventilate.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Latin ventilātus, past participle of ventilō.

ventricle.zh: n. 室, 脑室, 心室 / [医] 室(如脑室,心室等)
def: one of four connected cavities in the brain; is continuous with the central canal of the spinal cord and contains cerebrospinal fluid
a chamber of the heart that receives blood from an atrium and pumps it to the arteries
ventricle.ety: From late Middle English, from Latin ventriculus (“the belly”), diminutive of venter (“the belly”). Doublet of ventriculus.

venture.zh: n. 冒险, 风险 / vt. 敢于, 冒...的危险 / vi. 冒险
def: proceed somewhere despite the risk of possible dangers
put forward, of a guess, in spite of possible refutation
any venturesome undertaking especially one with an uncertain outcome

venue.zh: n. 犯罪地点, 审判地, 发生地点
def: the scene of any event or action (especially the place of a meeting)
in law: the jurisdiction where a trial will be held
venue.ety: From Middle English venu, from Old French venue, the feminine singular past participle of the verb venir (to come). Doublet of veny.

venus.zh: n. 维纳斯(爱与美的女神), 金星
def: the second nearest planet to the sun; it is peculiar in that its rotation is slow and retrograde (in the opposite sense of the Earth and all other planets except Uranus); it is visible from…
goddess of love; counterpart of Greek Aphrodite
type genus of the family Veneridae: genus of edible clams with thick oval shells
venus.ety: Inherited from Middle English Venus, borrowed from Latin Venus.

def: a porch along the outside of a building (sometimes partly enclosed)
A gallery, platform, or balcony, usually roofed and often partly enclosed, extending along the outside of a building.
veranda.ety: An Indian English word of Indo-Portuguese origin, from Portuguese varanda (“balustrade; balcony”). Further etymology is unclear and disputed.

def: the word class that serves as the predicate of a sentence
a content word that denotes an action, occurrence, or state of existence
verb.ety: From Middle English verbe, directly from Latin verbum (“word, verb”), reinforced by Old French verbe, from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰo-. Doublet of verve and word.

verbatim.zh: a. 逐字的, 照字面的 / adv. 逐字地
def: in precisely the same words used by a writer or speaker
verbatim.ety: Attested in English since 1481 (therefore considered a Middle English derivation by some): from Medieval Latin verbātim (“word for word”), from Latin verbum (“word”) + -ātim (adverbial suffix).

verdant.zh: a. 翠绿的, 青翠的, 无经验的, 不老练的
def: Abundant in verdure; lush with vegetation.
verdant.ety: From Middle French verdoyant, from Old French verb verdier, verdoier, from vert (“green”), from Vulgar Latin *virdis, from Latin viridis.

verdict.zh: n. 裁决, 判决, 判断性意见, 定论, 结论 / [法] 定论, 判断, 意见
def: (law) the findings of a jury on issues of fact submitted to it for decision; can be used in formulating a judgment
A decision on an issue of fact in a civil or criminal case or an inquest.
verdict.ety: From Middle English verdit, from Anglo-Norman verdit (> Medieval Latin veredictum), from veir (“true”) + dit (“saying”); possibly a calque of a Germanic term such as Old English sōþword, sōþsprǣċ, sōþ

verge.zh: n. 边缘, 边界, 起始点 / vi. 处在边缘, 接近, 下沉, 趋向
def: the limit beyond which something happens or changes
verge.ety: Borrowed from Middle French verge (“rod or wand of office”), hence "scope, territory dominated", from Latin virga (“shoot, rod stick”), of unknown origin. Earliest attested sense in English is now-obs

vermin.zh: n. 害虫, 歹徒 / [医] 虫, 体外寄生虫(如蚤、臭虫、蚤等)
def: any of various small animals or insects that are pests; e.g. cockroaches or rats
vermin.ety: From Middle English vermyn, vermyne, from Old French vermine, from Vulgar Latin *verminum (“vermin”), collective noun formed from Latin vermis (“worm”). Compare vermiculate and vermivorous. See also w

vernacular.zh: n. 本地话, 方言 / a. 地方的, 用本地语写成的
def: a characteristic language of a particular group (as among thieves)
being or characteristic of or appropriate to everyday language
the everyday speech of the people (as distinguished from literary language)
vernacular.ety: From Latin vernāculus (“domestic, indigenous, of or pertaining to home-born slaves”), from verna (“a native, a home-born slave (one born in his master's house)”).

versatile.zh: a. 多才多艺的, 万用的, 万向的
def: competent in many areas and able to turn with ease from one thing to another
versatile.ety: From Latin versātilis (“turning easily”), from versātus, past participle of versō (“to turn, change”), frequentative of vertō (“to turn”).

verse.zh: n. 诗, 韵文, 诗句 / vt. 用诗表达 / vi. 作诗
verse.ety: From Middle English vers, from a mixture of Old English fers and Old French vers; both from Latin versus (“a line in writing, and in poetry a verse; (originally) row, furrow”), from vertō (“to turn ar

version.zh: n. 一种描述, 版本, 译文 / [计] 版本
def: an interpretation of a matter from a particular viewpoint
something a little different from others of the same type
a written work (as a novel) that has been recast in a new form
version.ety: Borrowed from Middle French version, from Medieval Latin versiō, from Latin vertō (“to turn”). Used in English since 16th century.

versus.zh: prep. 对... / [法] 诉, 对, 相形
versus.ety: From Middle English versus, borrowed from Latin versus (“facing”), past participle of vertere (“to turn, change, overthrow, destroy”).

vertex.zh: n. 顶点, 最高点, 头顶, 天顶 / [计] 顶点
def: the point of intersection of lines or the point opposite the base of a figure
vertex.ety: Late Middle English, borrowed from Latin vertex (“whirl, eddy; top, crown, peak, summit”). Doublet of vortex.

vertical.zh: a. 垂直的, 直立的 / [医] 垂直的, 顶的, 头顶的
def: at right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line
a vertical structural member as a post or stake
vertical.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vertical, from Late Latin verticālis.

vertigo.zh: n. 眩晕, 迷惘 / [医] 眩晕
def: a reeling sensation; a feeling that you are about to fall
A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, caused by looking down from a great height or by disease affecting the inner ear.
A disordered or imbalanced state of mind or things analogous to physical vertigo; mental giddiness or dizziness.

verve.zh: n. 热情, 气魄, 神韵, 活力
def: Enthusiasm, rapture, spirit, or vigour, especially of imagination such as that which animates an artist, musician, or writer, in composing or performing.
verve.ety: Borrowed from French verve (“animation; caprice, whim; rapture; spirit; vigour; type of expression”), probably from Late Latin verva, a variant of Latin verba (“words; discourse; expressions; language

very.zh: a. 真正的, 恰好的, 十足的, 特有的 / adv. 非常, 完全
def: used as intensifiers; `real' is sometimes used informally for `really'; `rattling' is informal
being the exact same one; not any other:
very.ety: From Middle English verray, from Old French verai (“true”), from Early Medieval Latin vērāgus, from Classical Latin vērāx, derived from vērus, from Proto-Italic *wēros, from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁r

vessel.zh: n. 船, 容器, 脉管 / [医] 管, 脉管, (容)器
def: a tube in which a body fluid circulates
a craft designed for water transportation
an object used as a container (especially for liquids)
vessel.ety: Inherited from Middle English vessel, vessell (“small container”); from Old French vaissel (compare modern French vaisseau and Catalan vaixell), from Late Latin vāscellum, diminutive of vāsculum, dimi

vest.zh: n. 背心, 汗背心 / vt. 使穿衣服, 授予 / vi. 穿衣服, 归属
def: a man's sleeveless garment worn underneath a coat
a collarless men's undergarment for the upper part of the body
vest.ety: Derived from French veste (“a vest, jacket”), from Latin vestis (“a garment, gown, robe, vestment, clothing, vesture”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéstis, from *wes- (“to be dressed”) (English wear). C

vestige.zh: n. 遗迹, 痕迹, 残余, 丝毫, 退化的器官 / [医] 遗迹, 剩件, 剩余
def: an indication that something has been present
A mark left on the earth by a foot.
A faint mark or visible sign left by something which is lost, or has perished, or is no longer present.
vestige.ety: From French vestige, from Latin vestīgium (“footstep, footprint, track, the sole of the foot, a trace, mark”). Doublet of vestigium.

vet.zh: n. 兽医 / vi. 当兽医 / vt. 诊断, 检审
def: a doctor who practices veterinary medicine
a person who has served in the armed forces
vet.ety: Possibly by analogy from Etymology 1, in the sense of "verifying the soundness [of an animal]"

veteran.zh: n. 老手, 退伍军人, 老兵, 老树 / a. 老兵的, 老练的, 经验丰富的
def: rendered competent through trial and experience
a serviceman who has seen considerable active service
a person who has served in the armed forces
veteran.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vétéran, from Latin veterānus.

def: In a vertical direction or position.
a doctor who practices veterinary medicine
A medical doctor who treats non-human animals.
veterinarian.ety: From Latin veterīnārius (“cattle doctor”) + -an, from veterīnae (“beasts of burden, draught-”), probably from vehō (“to convey, draw”), or from vetus (“old”). By surface analysis, veterinary + -an.

vexation.zh: n. 恼怒, 烦恼, 令人恼火的事情 / [法] 招人烦恼的事物, 烦恼, 苦闷
def: anger produced by some annoying irritation
the psychological state of being irritated or annoyed
something or someone that causes anxiety; a source of unhappiness
vexation.ety: From Late Middle English vexacioun, vexation (“physical suffering; act of inflicting trouble (specifically through unjustified legal action); anxiety, mental distress; mental disturbance”), from Anglo

vexatious.zh: a. 叫人发急的, 使人为难的, 无理缠讼的 / [经] 苛捐杂税
def: Causing vexation or annoyance; teasing; troublesome.

vegetable.zh: n. 蔬菜, 植物, 无精打采之人 / a. 蔬菜的, 植物的
def: edible seeds or roots or stems or leaves or bulbs or tubers or nonsweet fruits of any of numerous herbaceous plant
any of various herbaceous plants cultivated for an edible part such as the fruit or the root of the beet or the leaf of spinach or the seeds of bean plants or the flower buds of broccoli or…
vegetable.ety: From Middle English vegetable, from Old French vegetable, from Latin vegetābilis (“able to live and grow”), derived from vegetāre (“to enliven”). Displaced Old English wyrt and ofett, whence modern w

vegetarian.zh: n. 素食者, 食草动物 / a. 素食的
def: eater of fruits and grains and nuts; someone who eats no meat or fish or (often) any animal products
A person who does not eat animal flesh, or, in some cases, use any animal products.
An animal that eats only plants; a herbivore.
vegetarian.ety: From vegetable + -arian; popularized following 1847 foundation of British Vegetarian Society. (Alternatively, it may derive from Latin vegetus + -arian.)

vegetate.zh: vi. 植物似地生长, 过呆板单调的生活, 无所事事地生活, (赘疣)生长, 长大
def: lead a passive existence without using one's body or mind
vegetate.ety: Borrowed from Latin vegetātus, perfect passive participle of vegetō (“to enliven, to arouse”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

vehement.zh: a. 热烈的, 激烈的
def: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions; inclined to react violently; fervid
characterized by great force or energy
vehement.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vehement (modern French véhément; compare Italian veemente, Portuguese veemente, Spanish vehemente); or from Latin vehemēns (“vehement; very eager; ardent, furious, impetuo

velocity.zh: n. 速度, 迅速 / [化] 速度
def: A vector quantity that denotes the rate of change of position with respect to time, combining speed with a directional component.
velocity.ety: From Middle French vélocité, from Latin vēlōcitās (“speed”), from vēlōx (“fast”), thus a doublet of veloce.

vendor.zh: n. 小贩, 卖主, 自动售货机 / [计] 计算机销售商
def: someone who promotes or exchanges goods or services for money
A person or a company that vends or sells.
vendor.ety: Borrowed from Anglo-Norman vendor (Old French vendeor), from Latin venditor (“seller”), from vendere (“to sell, cry up for sale, praise”), contraction of venundare, venumdare, also, as originally, two

venerable.zh: a. 庄严的, 值得尊敬的
venerable.ety: From Middle French vénérable, from Old French, from Latin venerabilis.

venerate.zh: vt. 尊敬, 崇敬, 崇拜
def: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe of
To treat with great respect and deference.
To revere or hold in awe.
venerate.ety: First attested in 1623; borrowed from Latin venerātus, perfect active participle of veneror (“to worship, venerate”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

vengeance.zh: n. 复仇, 报仇 / [法] 报仇, 复仇
def: the act of taking revenge (harming someone in retaliation for something harmful that they have done) especially in the next life--Romans 12:19--James Garfield
Revenge taken for an insult, injury, or other wrong.
vengeance.ety: From Anglo-Norman vengeaunce, from Old French vengeance, venjance, from vengier (“to avenge”). Analysable as venge + -ance.

vengeful.zh: a. 复仇心重的, 报复的
def: disposed to seek revenge or intended for revenge- Shakespeare- M.R.Cohen

venomous.zh: a. 有毒的, 恶毒的, 分泌毒液的, 有毒腺的 / [医] 毒的, 有毒的
def: extremely poisonous or injurious; producing venom
marked by deep ill will; deliberately harmful
venomous.ety: From Middle English venymous, from Old French venimos, composed of venim (“venom”) + -os (adjective-forming suffix). Synchronically analysable as venom + -ous. Compare Modern French venimeux. Piecewis

ventilation.zh: n. 通风, 空气流通, 公开讨论 / [医] 通风, 换气
def: the act of supplying fresh air and getting rid of foul air
a mechanical system in a building that provides fresh air
free and open discussion of (or debate on) some question of public interest
ventilation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French ventilation, from Old French ventilacion, from Late Latin ventilatio, from Latin ventilo. Morphologically ventilate + -ion.

ventilator.zh: n. 通风设备, 送风机, 换气扇 / [医] 通风机
def: a device (such as a fan) that introduces fresh air or expels foul air
a device that facilitates breathing in cases of respiratory failure

venturesome.zh: a. 冒险的, 好冒险的, 不顾一切的
def: disposed to venture or take risks
Adventurous; bold; willing to take risks.

veracious.zh: a. 说实话的, 诚实的, 老实的, 真实的

veracity.zh: n. 说话老实, 老实, 诚实
def: The quality of speaking or stating the truth; truthfulness.
Something that is true; a truthful statement; a truth.
veracity.ety: From Middle French véracité, from Old French veracitie, from Medieval Latin vērācitās (“truthfulness”) (whence -acity), from Latin vērāx (“truthful, speaking truth”), from vērus (“true, real”). See ve

verbal.zh: a. 用言辞的, 言语的, 口头的, 逐字的, 动词的 / [医] 言语的, 口述的
def: communicated in the form of words
of or relating to or formed from words in general
of or relating to or formed from a verb
verbal.ety: From Old French verbal, from Late Latin verbālis (“belonging to a word”). Equivalent to verb + -al.

verbiage.zh: n. 罗嗦, 冗词, 措辞
def: the manner in which something is expressed in words- G.S.Patton
verbiage.ety: From French verbiage. Compare verb meaning "word" in verbal and verbose.

verbose.zh: a. 用字多的, 冗长的, 累赘的 / [计] 详述
def: using or containing too many words
Containing or using more words than necessary; long-winded, wordy.
Producing detailed output for diagnostic purposes.
verbose.ety: From Latin verbōsus (“prolix, wordy, verbose”). Verbōsus is derived from verbum (“word”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *werh₁- (“to say, speak”)) + -ōsus (suffix meaning ‘full of, overly, prone

verify.zh: vt. 证明, 查证, 证实, 检验, 校验 / [计] 校验, 检验; DOS内部命令:设定写入磁盘时是否验证写入的正确性
def: check or regulate (a scientific experiment) by conducting a parallel experiment or comparing with another standard
attach or append a legal verification to (a pleading or petition)
verify.ety: From Old French verifier (French: vérifier), from Medieval Latin vērificāre (“make true”), from Latin vērus (“true”) + faciō (“do, make”); see -fy.

versatility.zh: n. 多用途, 多才多艺, 易变
def: having a wide variety of skills
The property of being versatile or having many different abilities.

vertebrate.zh: n. 脊椎动物 / a. 有椎骨的, 有脊椎的
def: animals having a bony or cartilaginous skeleton with a segmented spinal column and a large brain enclosed in a skull or cranium
having a backbone or spinal column
vertebrate.ety: From the substantivization of the above adjective through the associated taxon's name (Vertebrata) (see -ate (noun-forming suffix) for more).

vestigial.zh: a. 残留的, 遗留的, 退化的 / [医] 遗迹的, 剩余的
def: not fully developed in mature animals
Of or pertaining to a vestige or remnant; like a trace from the past.
Not fully developed in mature animals.
vestigial.ety: From Latin vestīgium + -al. By surface analysis, vestige + -ial.

vestment.zh: n. 衣服, 衣裳, 礼服, 法衣, 祭服
def: gown (especially ceremonial garments) worn by the clergy
A robe, gown, or other article of clothing worn as an indication of office.
Any of the special articles of clothing worn by members of the clergy etc., especially a garment worn at the celebration of the Eucharist.
vestment.ety: From Middle English vestement, vestment, from Old French vestement, from Latin vestīmentum. By surface analysis, vest + -ment. Compare French vêtement.

vegetation.zh: n. 植物 / [医] 贽生物, 贽疣, 增殖体; 生长, 增殖
def: all the plant life in a particular region or period
the process of growth in plants
an abnormal growth or excrescence (especially a warty excrescence on the valves of the heart)
vegetation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French végétation, from Medieval Latin vegetātiōnem.

veneration.zh: n. 尊敬, 崇敬, 崇拜
def: a feeling of profound respect for someone or something
religious zeal; the willingness to serve God
veneration.ety: From Middle French vénération, from Old French veneracion, from Latin veneratio.

veritable.zh: a. 名副其实的, 真实的, 确实的, 真的
veritable.ety: From verity + -able, from Middle French veritable, from Old French veritable, from Latin veritabilis.

def: a performer who projects the voice into a wooden dummy
A person, especially an entertainer, who practices ventriloquism.

trumpery.zh: n. 华而不实的东西, 中看不中用的东西, 废物, 废话 / a. 虚有其表的, 浅薄的, 无用的
def: ornamental objects of no great value
trumpery.ety: From Middle English trompery, from Middle French tromperie (“deceit”).

trammel.zh: n. 鱼网, 拘束, 束缚 / vt. 拘束, 束缚
def: a fishing net with three layers; the outer two are coarse mesh and the loose inner layer is fine mesh
catch in or as if in a trap
an adjustable pothook set in a fireplace

lyric.zh: n. 抒情诗, 歌词 / a. 抒情的
def: the text of a popular song or musical-comedy number
used of a singer or singing voice that is light in volume and modest in range
lyric.ety: From French lyrique, or its source, Latin lyricus, from Ancient Greek λυρικός (lurikós), from λύρα (lúra, “lyre”). Its English equivalent would be lyre + -ic. The original Greek sense of "lyric poetry

lyrical.zh: a. 抒情诗调的, 有抒情味的, 感情丰富的
def: suitable for or suggestive of singing

lyricist.zh: n. 抒情诗人, 歌曲作者
def: a person who writes the words for songs
A person who writes the lyrics of a song.

lyrically.zh: adv. 抒情地；诗意地；狂热地
def: In a manner that is pleasing to hear, as singing or speaking; in a lyrical manner.

ajar.zh: a. 微开的, 半开的, 不和谐的 / adv. 微开, 半开, 不协调地
def: To turn or open slightly; to become ajar or to cause to become ajar; to be or to hang ajar.

eh.zh: interj. 啊!嗯!是吗?好吗? / [医] 氧化还原电位
def: Used to negate the following verb; (am/are/is/do/does) not.
eh.ety: Natural exclamation; first recorded mid-16th century. Perhaps an unstressed variant of aye (“yes, yeah”). The Philippine sense is possibly influenced by Tagalog e and/or Spanish eh.

ewer.zh: n. (有柄的)大口水壶, 花瓶状水罐
def: an open vessel with a handle and a spout for pouring
A kind of widemouthed pitcher or jug with a shape like a vase and a handle, and originally used for carrying water.
ewer.ety: From Middle English ewer, from Anglo-Norman or Old French ewer, eawer (modern French évier), from Latin aquārium, from aqua (“water”). Doublet of aquarium.

a Kwa language spoken by the Ewe in Ghana and Togo and Benin

ubiquitous.zh: a. 无所不在的, 到处存在的, 普遍存在的
def: Appearing to be everywhere at once; being or seeming to be in more than one location at the same time.
ubiquitous.ety: From ubiquity + -ous, from Medieval Latin ubīquitās, from Latin ubīque (“everywhere”), from ubī̆ (“where”) + -que (“each, ever”). Compare ubiety.

ooze.zh: n. 渗流, 分泌物 / v. 渗出, 泄漏
def: pass gradually or leak through or as if through small openings
ooze.ety: * (Noun) Middle English wose (“sap”), from Old English wōs (“sap, froth”), from Proto-Germanic *wōsą, from Proto-Indo-European *wóseh₂ (“sap”) (cf. Sanskrit वसा (vásā, “fat”)). Cognate to Middle Low G

zany.zh: n. 小丑, 笨人, 马屁精 / a. 滑稽的, 滑稽愚蠢的
def: a buffoon in one of the old comedies; imitates others for ludicrous effect
a man who is a stupid incompetent fool
zany.ety: From Middle French zani, zanni, from Italian zanni (“a kind of masked clown character”), from Zanni, a Venetian form of Giovanni. Doublet of Zanni, John, and Giovanni.

azure.zh: n. 天蓝色, 碧空 / a. 蔚蓝的
def: of a deep somewhat purplish blue color similar to that of a clear October sky
azure.ety: From Middle English asure, from Old French azur, derived from Arabic لَازَوَرْد (lāzaward, “lapis lazuli”), dropping the l as if it were equivalent to the French article l'. The Arabic is from Classic

akin.zh: a. 同类的, 同族的, 同源的
akin.ety: From a corruption of of kin, from Middle English of kyn (“related, of kin”), equivalent to a- + kin (1550s). Compare Old English cyn, cynn (“akin, proper, suitable”, adj.).

vying.zh: a. 竞争的 / vie的现在分词
def: present participle and gerund of vie
present participle and gerund of vy
The act of one who vies; rivalry.

aorta.zh: n. 主动脉 / [医] 主动脉
def: the large trunk artery that carries blood from the left ventricle of the heart to branch arteries
The great artery which carries the blood from the heart to all parts of the body except the lungs; the main trunk of the arterial system.
aorta.ety: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀορτή (aortḗ, “the arteries springing from the heart”), from ἀορτέω (aortéō), lengthened form of ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift, raise”).

kudos.zh: n. 称赞, 光荣, 荣誉
def: an expression of approval and commendation
kudos.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κῦδος (kûdos, “praise, renown”).

ogle.zh: n. 眉目传情 / vt. 挑逗地注视 / vi. 做媚眼
def: To stare at (someone or something), especially impertinently, amorously, or covetously.
An impertinent, flirtatious, amorous or covetous stare.

svelte.zh: a. 苗条的；线条清晰的；和蔼的
def: showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience
being of delicate or slender build- Frank Norris
svelte.ety: Borrowed from French svelte, from Italian svelto (“stretched out”), past participle of svellere (“to pluck out, root out”), from Vulgar Latin *exvellere, from ex + vellere (“to pluck, stretch”).
